In Week 2, Philadelphia will face a dismal Titans squad that allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Hurts tossed two touchdowns and two interceptions in a last-second win over Tennessee last game. Hurts threw for 264 yards in the rollercoaster battle and was able to overcome the two picks to find Darius Cooper for the winning score. Hurts has five touchdowns in two games for the Eagles. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jalen Hurts had a performance to forget last game for the Eagles. Hurts threw for just 153 yards and an interception in a dismal loss to the Bears in Week 3. Hurts did score once on the ground, though gained just 25 yards as a rusher. Hurts will look to get back on track in Week 4 versus a Rams defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026. The Rams are allowing just 171.3 passing yards per tilt, which is fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Hurts enters his seventh NFL season and sixth as the starter in Philadelphia. The 28-year-old tossed a career-high 25 touchdowns last season, but his rushing production was way down (105-421-8 after delivering at least 139 carries, 605 yards and 10 TDs in each of the prior four seasons). Hurts' fantasy production dipped, as his 18.7 points per game was his lowest as a starter and ranked eighth at the position after three straight top-five campaigns. Hurts' supporting cast remains strong (even without A.J. Brown), and new playcaller Sean Mannion very well could add some juice back to the offense. Hurts' fantasy stock is down a bit from years past, but his dual-threat ability locks him in as a midrange QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyren Williams may again be part of a pretty evenly split backfield when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Though Williams scored Los Angeles' only touchdown in a season-opening loss to the 49ers, he had 13 fewer rushing yards on one more carry than backfield mate Blake Corum. Williams did produce more total yards thanks to logging 24 receiving yards on three catches, but Corum seems to have forced his way into a substantial backfield role after averaging over five yards per carry last year. Both backs will look to break through a Giants defense that gave up just 69 yards and 3.8 YPC against Dallas in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyren Williams will look to get into the end zone for the Rams again in Week 3 versus Denver. Williams posted a 12-85-0 rushing line against the Giants on Monday Night Football and added a 2-12-1 line through the air. The veteran running back has scored each of the first two weeks of the campaign after racking up double-digit scores each of the past three seasons. The Broncos have struggled against the run so far in 2026, allowing the third-most rushing yards (286) to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyren Williams is fresh off his most productive performance of the campaign heading into the Rams' Week 4 clash against Philadelphia. Williams posted season-best tallies with 15 carries for 88 yards in Week 3 against Denver, and he complemented his output on the ground with a season-high six catches for 70 yards through the air. Whereas fellow running back Blake Corum has frequently eaten into Williams' volume since last season, Corum recorded just six totes and 15 total yards against the Broncos. Corum isn't likely to exit the picture anytime soon, but Williams remains a consistent week-to-week producer. However, he could have his work cut out for him in Week 4 versus an Eagles defense that ranks 12th in the league in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams continues to produce at a high level as the Rams' lead back. The 2022 fifth-round pick has produced 1,350-plus scrimmage yards in three straight seasons (including a career-high 1,533 in 2025), and he's one of 11 backs in NFL history who have scored 13-plus touchdowns in three of his first four seasons. Williams' carry share actually dropped quite a bit last season, but it was mostly offset by a boost in both rushing and receiving efficiency, and he still averaged a healthy 15.5 fantasy points. Williams doesn't do much as a receiver (he has never cleared 36 catches in a season), but his overall usage and scoring potential in the Rams' elite offense is enough to make the 26-year-old a solid RB2 option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Omarion Hampton looked like the clear lead back for the Chargers in their season-opening loss to the Cardinals, taking 12 carries for 43 yards and a touchdown, while backup Keaton Mitchell saw only four carries. Neither RB caught a pass as Justin Herbert had a very narrow target tree under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, connecting with just five different receivers. Hampton had been headed for a big rookie campaign before getting injured, so staying healthy will be the biggest factor in any potential 2026 breakout. He could post better numbers in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 21st last season in points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Omarion Hampton has been one of the few Chargers who seems to be benefiting from new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The second-year back racked up 115 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 2's loss to the Raiders, and he's been the clear top option in the backfield, getting 37 touches through two weeks compared to Keaton Mitchell's 10 and Kimani Vidal's zero. Hampton lost a fumble in each game, and that split could begin to shift Mitchell's way if ball security is deemed an issue for the 2025 first-round pick. Hampton could cash in on his bell-cow role in Week 3 against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.
outlooksByWeek.4: Omarion Hampton's workload took a step backward in a Week 3 loss to the Bills, as the Chargers' backfield teeters toward a committee. The second-year back hasn't been awful, producing 214 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns in three games while averaging 3.9 yards per carry, but Keaton Mitchell is averaging 5.0 yards per carry on limited usage and may be a better fit for offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. Kimani Vidal also had his first touches of the season in Buffalo. Hampton is the most talented player of the three on paper, but with the 0-3 Chargers struggling to generate offense, every possible solution will be on the table. He isn't likely to start turning things around in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Hampton is primed for a breakout second season following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie campaign. The first-round pick was busy during nine appearances, averaging 13.8 carries and 3.9 targets. He scored five touchdowns, averaged 15.1 fantasy points per game (13th best) and ranked third among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF. With Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell as his primary competition, Hampton has a clear path to lead rusher duties in 2026, and his targets only figure to increase with Greg Roman out and Mike McDaniel in as the team's playcaller. Add in a much-improved offensive line with star tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater back healthy, and Hampton has nothing short of elite upside. Value him as a fringe RB1 with room for more.

The defending Super Bowl champions, who benefited greatly from what was the league's top-scoring fantasy defense, draw one of the toughest overall schedules as a ?reward.? Only the Cardinals (Weeks 2 and 9), Raiders (Week 10) and Giants (Week 14) appear to be clear plus matchups, and the team must also deal with the offseason losses of S Coby Bryant, edge rusher Boye Mafe and CB Riq Woolen. Mike Macdonald might extract maximum effort from his defenses, but some regression should be expected with this unit.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Nabers looked spry in his first game of the season for the Giants, a Week 1 victory over the Cowboys. Nabers led the G-Men in targets with nine, en route to six catches for 69 yards in the 28-20 triumph. Nabers showed no ill effects from his torn ACL and meniscus suffered in Week 4 last season, only needing to get tackled by his new head coach John Harbaugh to prove he could take a hit before suiting up. In Week 2, Nabers will face a Rams defense that struggled against the pass in Week 1, allowing 205 passing yards and three passing scores in its season opener. Nabers will likely be covered by all-pro cornerback Trent McDuffie, though.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malik Nabers injured his shoulder last game for the Giants. He was able to return, but still may undergo additional testing this week. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Nabers will likely see his stock take a hit. However, if Nabers can suit up in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malik Nabers shook off a shoulder injury to suit up last game for the Giants. He responded with five catches on six targets, though racked up a mere 26 yards in the 12-7 win over the Titans. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which limits the upside for Nabers. However, Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Nabers is on the comeback trail after a torn ACL limited him to only four appearances last season. In 18 full games in his career, Nabers has a massive 35% target share (11.3 per game) and he's averaging 18.2 fantasy PPG. As a rookie, the 2024 sixth overall pick finished seventh or better among receivers in targets, receptions, yards and fantasy points despite missing two games and dealing with New York's offensive struggles. Nabers' massive target share allowed him a high floor, as he was a top-30 fantasy scorer in 13 of 15 games, including 10 straight to end the 2024 season. He essentially has a new quarterback (Jaxson Dart threw only three passes his way last season), a new coach (John Harbaugh), a new offensive playcaller (Matt Nagy) and is recovering from the knee, so there are a lot of variables here, but the 23-year-old still holds elite upside. A healthy Nabers should be valued as a mid-to-back-end WR1, but the potential for a slow start needs to be considered on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Skattebo showed no ill effects from last season's injury in Week 1 for the New York Giants. Skattebo rushed 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in he stunning 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys. With the Giants poised to possess the ball and feed the running game under new coach John Harbaugh, Skattebo should continue to be in line for a heavy workload. In Week 2, the Giants will face a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season.  The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Skattebo managed just 55 yards from scrimmage last game for the Giants. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, teams will likely gameplan to stop the run, which starts with Skattebo. That could mean tough sledding for the running game for the G-Men overall. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a mediocre Titans run defense that has given up 120.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL. In addition, the Titans have already surrendered three rushing scores in the first two games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Skattebo racked up 100 yards from scrimmage in the 12-7 win for the Giants over the Titans. Skattebo took 20 carries for 60 yards while also catching three passes for 40 yards out of the backfield. With Jameis Winston under center, the Giants should continue to rely on the running game led by Skattebo in Week 4 versus Arizona. The Cardinals have been suspect against the run in 2026, allowing 127.7 yards per clash on the ground, which is 26th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Skattebo is a Year 2 breakout candidate following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie season. The fourth-round pick first played a significant offensive role in Week 2 and went on to average 16.0 carries, 4.7 targets and 96.3 yards while scoring six TDs during his six full games. His 19.1 fantasy points per game during the span would've ranked sixth over the full season. The 24-year-old enters 2026 with a new coach (John Harbaugh) and playcaller (Matt Nagy), but his competition for touches are Najee Harris and the same guys he beat out for work in 2025 (Tyrone Tracy Jr., Devin Singletary). Assuming his ankle heals up as expected, Skattebo will be on the RB2 radar with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to operate as Carolina's top pass catcher in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. McMillan caught just five passes for 75 yards and lost a fumble in last week's loss, despite the game ending with the most points ever scored in a Week 1 contest. He was out-shined by third-year wideout Jalen Coker, who paced Carolina's receiving corps in targets (nine), receptions (eight), yards (138) and touchdowns (two). McMillan will look to return to form in Week 2, but he's in for a tough matchup against a Falcons defense that gave up just 22.4 PPR fantasy points to wideouts in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain one of the Panthers' top targets in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. McMillan bounced back in Week 2 after a lackluster Week 1 performance, catching five of 10 targets for 101 yards while leading the team in receiving. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year is tied with Jalen Coker for the most targets on Carolina (18) entering Week 3, which is a positive sign for both players' outlooks going forward. With the Panthers' offensive success through two games, McMillan should be in for a great Week 3 matchup, especially while facing a Browns defense that's given up four receiving touchdowns to WRs through two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tetairoa McMillan will look to bounce back from an underwhelming performance in the Panthers' Week 4 matchup against the Lions. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year was held to just two catches for 17 yards in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, the second-fewest yards he's ever recorded in an NFL game. Despite this, McMillan has an extremely positive outlook going forward, as both Jalen Coker (quadriceps) and Xavier Legette (knee) are dealing with injuries, making him the clear number one target. Additionally, McMillan is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 39.0 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year, McMillan is a candidate to make the leap into the "elite" conversation at wide receiver this season. The 2025 eighth overall pick was very busy as a rookie (top 15 among WRs in snaps, routes, target share, targets, yards, end zone targets and touchdowns) and, while he finished 16th among receivers in fantasy points (22nd PPG), he lacked upside, producing only one top-10 outing (Week 9). Improving on a 56% catch rate will be key in Year 2, though that would require improvement from Bryce Young. McMillan, 23, remains positioned as Carolina's clear top target and, though Young's limitations may cap his ceiling a bit, McMillan's talent/usage combo supplies him with top-10 upside. He's safest as a midrange fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Breece Hall will look to remain busy when the Jets face the Packers in Week 2. Hall handled 24 total touches to open the year, finishing with 118 total yards and a touchdown-an encouraging start under new OC Frank Reich. The Packers allowed just 3.7 yards per carry last week but did give up two rushing scores. Much of Hall's volume came in a favorable game script, something that may not repeat in Week 2, but with better than a 2:1 touch split with Braelon Allen, Hall will garner ample opportunity.
outlooksByWeek.3: Breece Hall will look to find more running room for the Jets in Week 3 against the Lions. He was limited to 1.8 yards per carry in Week 2, but 16 rushes was encouraging, as were his five catches on five targets. Detroit's defense is leaky, and while their secondary has been the more glaring weakness, they're allowing 5.2 yards per carry. The Jets' offensive limitations will likely temper Week 3 production, but Hall's workload in a plus matchup boosts his outlook.
outlooksByWeek.4: Breece Hall is uncertain to face the Bears in the Jets' Week 4 matchup due to a thigh injury. Hall has struggled over the last two weeks, gaining just 61 yards on 29 carries, but his workload in the passing game has been steady. Should he play, Hall has an inviting matchup against a defense that's allowing 4.9 yards per carry. Braelon Allen would likely lead the backfield in the event of Hall's absence, with Isaiah Davis playing second fiddle.

player.seasonOutlook: Hall received the franchise tag during the offseason and will return for his fifth season with the Jets. Having worked in the Jets' underwhelming offenses the past two years, Hall has struggled to finishes of 17th and 21st in fantasy points per game among RBs, which is a far cry from top-eight finishes during his first two seasons. Hall has remained busy, however, producing 266-plus touches each of the past three seasons. The 2022 second-round pick saw a dip in receiving work in 2025 (career-low 10% target share) but finished fourth in that category in both 2023 and 2024, so a rebound is possible with pocket QB Geno Smith now under center. Though the Jets' offense might continue to limit Hall's upside, the 25-year-old's combination of workload and talent positions him as a solid RB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Joe Burrow and the Bengals travel to take on the Texans in Week 2. Burrow completed 25 of 35 passes for 254 yards with one TD and one INT, and he rushed five times for 20 yards in their season-opening win. Houston ranks 28th in fantasy points allowed per game (39.0) to QBs after Josh Allen torched them for 357 scrimmage yards and four TDs. Burrow will look to get Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins more involved after the receivers combined for 71 yards on just five catches.
outlooksByWeek.3: Joe Burrow and the Bengals are on the road to face the Steelers in Week 3. After dealing with back spasms in practice, Burrow was a full go in Week 2, throwing for 207 yards (20-for-31) with two TDs and no INTs in the 20-6 victory. He faces a stout Pittsburgh defense that ranks first in fantasy points allowed (11.6) to QBs and seventh in passing yards allowed. Burrow is one of the best at his position, but fantasy managers should approach this matchup with caution after the Steelers held Drake Maye to 208 passing yards (14-for-22) with one pick while sacking him three times in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Joe Burrow and the Bengals host the Jaguars for a battle between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He threw for 282 yards (28-for-37) with three TDs and no INTs and added 13 yards on two carries during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. Burrow also lost a fumble in the final minute of the contest, but he had a strong outing overall against a tough defense. Up next is another difficult task, as Jacksonville's defense is tied for fifth, allowing 16.8 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Burrow will attempt to bounce back after injuries limited him to eight games in 2025. The 29-year-old has now missed at least six games in three of his six pro seasons, including two of his past three. Burrow was still a starting-caliber fantasy quarterback when active last season (top-12 scorer in five of his final six games), but his ceiling was limited by a near complete lack of rushing (41 yards on 14 carries). Burrow was a top-five scoring quarterback in each of his past two full seasons, and coach Zac Taylor cut back a bit on his extreme pass-heavy playcalling last season, so Burrow is best valued as more of a midrange QB1 than an elite option.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Kittle had a quiet season opener but will look to increase his production when San Francisco faces the Dolphins in Week 2. Kittle tallied a modest two catches (on five targets) for 12 yards in last Thursday's win over the Rams. That was his first game back after tearing his Achilles in January, which may have been a factor in his receiving line following below his usual standards. Miami allowed Raiders tight end Michael Mayer to record six catches in Week 1, suggesting that Kittle could find room to operate against the Dolphins defense.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Kittle will look to build upon Sunday's strong performance when San Francisco hosts the Cardinals in Week 3. In just his second regular-season game since tearing his Achilles in January, Kittle led the 49ers with 80 receiving yards on four catches with one touchdown Sunday in a win over Miami. The veteran tight end remains a key target for QB Brock Purdy, and Kittle's importance in the passing game could be even more elevated with WRs Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Mike Evans (hip) both managing injuries. Through two weeks, Arizona has allowed tight ends to catch all 10 of their targets for 105 yards.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Kittle enters San Francisco's Week 4 game against Denver as one of the hottest tight ends in the league. Following a quiet season opener in Australia, Kittle has put up 10 catches for 162 yards and three touchdowns over the subsequent two weeks. He's caught all but one of his 11 targets during that span, as he has been clicking very well with QB Brock Purdy. Kittle could continue rolling against a Broncos defense that has given up the eighth-most receiving yards (199) to tight ends so far this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Kittle is undoubtedly among the best tight ends in the NFL and fantasy, but he simply can't dodge the injury bug. The 2017 fifth-round pick has played one full season (2018) and tore an Achilles in the team's wild-card victory after missing six regular-season games last season. Kittle may be ready for Week 1 and isn't expected to miss more than a game or two, though he's now 32 years old and might not be his usual, dominant self even when he returns. Kittle has finished sixth or better in fantasy PPG in each of the past eight seasons (including first in 2024), so his upside makes him worth a late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tee Higgins and the Bengals visit the Texans for a Week 2 battle between two playoff hopefuls. He caught three of six targets for 59 yards during Cincinnati's season-opening victory. Higgins tied for second on the team in receptions and targets while finishing behind Mike Gesicki for the lead in receiving yards. He draws a favorable matchup against Houston's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tee Higgins and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh to take on their division rivals in Week 3. He finished Week 2's win over Houston with five catches on 10 targets for 95 yards, pacing Cincinnati in yardage and targets. Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase accounted for 19 of Joe Burrow's 31 pass attempts, and that's likely to remain the case despite an unfavorable Week 3 matchup. The Steelers' defense ranks second in fantasy points allowed per game (15.5) and has yet to surrender a TD to WRs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tee Higgins and the Bengals return home to host the 2-1 Jaguars in Week 4. He tallied six catches for 90 yards and one TD on seven targets during Cincinnati's tough 30-27 loss in Week 3. Higgins was second on the team in receptions, yardage, and targets behind Ja'Marr Chase, but he led the way with 15.0 yards per catch. He'll aim to keep rolling against a Jacksonville defense that ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (31.5) and 27th in yards per target to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Higgins may be overshadowed by teammate Ja'Marr Chase, but that hasn't stopped the veteran receiver from playing a key role near the goal line in the Bengals' pass-friendly offense. Despite missing seven games over the past two seasons, Higgins sits eighth among receivers in end zone targets (24) and fourth in touchdowns (21) during the span. The 2020 second-round pick finished both seasons in the top 20 in fantasy points (overall and per game). Durability (he hasn't played a full season since 2020) and a limited target share are concerns here, but Higgins' combination of talent and role in a Joe Burrow-led offense are enough to allow fringe-WR2 production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bucky Irving is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' lead back in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Irving out-touched Kenneth Gainwell 15 to six in the Week 1 loss, which is a very promising sign for his outlook moving forward. The most impressive part about Irving's Week 1 performance was receiving, where he caught all seven of his targets for 48 yards. He could be in for another big week against a Browns defense that allowed 34 points in Week 1. However, Cleveland did give up just 3.9 yards per carry, so Irving may need to continue his success as a receiver for fantasy production.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bucky Irving is expected to remain Tampa Bay's lead back in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Irving remained efficient despite the Buccaneers' offensive struggles in Week 2, accounting for 90 total yards on 21 touches. Additionally, he's operated as the clear No. 1 running back, out-touching Kenneth Gainwell 36 to 11 in two contests. Irving will likely struggle in Week 3, however, as he'll be facing a Vikings defense that's allowed just 14.7 PPR fantasy points to RBs this season, the fourth-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bucky Irving is expected to continue leading the Buccaneers' backfield in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Irving was held in check by a strong Vikings defense in Week 3, totaling 58 yards on 17 touches. Despite this inefficient effort, Irving remained the Buccaneers' bell-cow back, as Kenneth Gainwell received just five touches (10 total yards). With Baker Mayfield (thumb) dealing with injury following the Week 3 loss, Irving could see less opportunities through the air. Regardless, Irving's strong workload should bode well for the Week 4 matchup, as Green Bay's defense has allowed the second-most PPR fantasy points per game to the RB position (30.7) this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Irving enters his third season coming off a disappointing 2025 campaign in which he missed seven games and struggled with efficiency. After averaging 5.42 yards per carry and producing 1,514 yards and eight touchdowns as a rookie, Irving fell to 3.40 YPC (fourth worst among qualified RBs), 865 yards and four touchdowns in 2025. He failed to clear 4.2 YPC in any of his 10 outings and had zero carries inside the opponent's 5 yard line. The 24-year-old remains positioned as the lead back in Tampa Bay, but the combination of his small frame (5-foot-9, 192 pounds) and the arrival of Kenneth Gainwell (not to mention Sean Tucker at the goal line) suggest he might play a lesser role moving forward. Irving should be valued as a back-end RB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Emeka Egbuka is expected to operate as Tampa Bay's top receiver in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns, whose defense struggled against wideouts in Week 1. Despite logging just six targets last week, Egbuka led the Buccaneers in receiving yards, solidifying himself as the team's top WR. Additionally, Egbuka had been nursing a toe injury leading up to the Week 1 loss, so he should only become more explosive as the season progresses. He's in for an incredible Week 2 matchup, as Cleveland's secondary allowed 50.6 PPR fantasy points to wideouts last week, the third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top receiving option in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings, whose defense has given up 38.9 PPR fantasy points to WRs this season. Egbuka had a rough Week 2 outing, finishing third on Tampa Bay in receptions (three) and targets (five) while slotting in at fifth in yards (16). However, he did score a touchdown and was on the field for 85 percent of the Buccaneers' offensive snaps, suggesting he'll remain the team's WR1. He's set for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that gave up just three points and 163 passing yards to the Bears in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Emeka Egbuka will remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Despite another relatively underwhelming Week 3 performance (5-62-0), Egbuka clearly remains atop Tampa Bay's receiving corps, leading the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards. Baker Mayfield (thumb) will be sidelined in Week 4, which suggests Egbuka will likely see less opportunities. Regardless of who starts at quarterback, Egbuka is in for a favorable matchup against a Green Bay defense that's allowed 34.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Egbuka is a fascinating evaluation following a rookie season that couldn't have started much better (five TDs and 20.5 fantasy PPG during his first five games), but that fell apart from there (one TD and 7.8 PPG during his final 12 games). By season's end, Egbuka sat in the top 10 in targets and air yards, but a horrific 49% catch rate led to a 34th-place finish in fantasy PPG. The good news is that, with Mike Evans out of the picture and Chris Godwin now 30 years old, Egbuka has a shot to emerge as Baker Mayfield's No. 1 target. The 2025 first-round pick is a strong bet for a leap forward and should be viewed as a WR2 with the potential for a full-on breakout.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brock Purdy and the 49ers head into a Week 2 tilt against Miami fresh off a big season-opening win over the Rams. Purdy threw for 205 yards and three touchdowns in that contest, connecting with wideouts Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson for the three scores while adding 29 yards on five rushes. It was a big victory against a vaunted NFC West rival that many have pegged as Super Bowl favorites, so San Francisco will look to avoid a letdown in Week 2 against a much less revered Dolphins team. Miami was beaten soundly by the Raiders in Week 1 while allowing QB Kirk Cousins to toss three touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brock Purdy will look to build upon a historic performance when San Francisco faces Arizona in Week 3. Purdy completed 20 of 22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns with no turnovers against Miami on Sunday, adding 30 yards and a touchdown on the ground. That stat line made Purdy the second passer in NFL history with 250 passing yards on a 90 performance completion rate in multiple games. The fifth-year signal caller may be without some of his weapons in Week 3 if Mike Evans (hip) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) need to sit out, though early reports suggest Evans isn't dealing with a serious injury. The Cardinals could have a hard time containing Purdy after giving up 235 passing yards and three TDs to Seattle QB Drew Lock in a Week 2 loss.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brock Purdy will lead the 3-0 49ers in a Week 4 matchup against the Broncos. Purdy threw for 297 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions in a Week 3 win against Arizona, and he currently holds the highest passer rating (133.1) in the NFL. Purdy is also tied for the league lead with nine TD passes, three of which have gone to star tight end George Kittle. However, Denver figures to pose a tough challenge, as the Broncos' defense -- led in the secondary by star cornerback Patrick Surtain -- has limited opponents to a 74.5 passer rating, fifth-best in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Purdy enters his fifth NFL season looking to rebound after injuries caused him to appear in only nine games in 2025. The good news is Purdy played well, scoring 17-plus fantasy points in seven of the nine games, including 26-plus points in three straight games during Weeks 15-17. A highly effective passer and solid contributor as a rusher, Purdy has quietly finished in the top 10 in fantasy points per game in each of the past three seasons. With a good supporting cast led by Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle and free agent additions Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel, Purdy is an underrated mid-to-back-end QB1 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: D'Andre Swift will aim to replicate a huge game as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Swift was dominant against the Panthers in Week 1, carrying the ball 18 times for 124 yards and three touchdowns. The veteran ball carrier topped any of his games in the 2025 season, showcasing that he should also benefit from a higher-scoring Chicago offense this year. He'll play a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but he has established himself more than the Packers' current RB room.
outlooksByWeek.3: D'Andre Swift will be a top option in Chicago's offense in Week 3 against the Eagles. Swift cooled down in Week 2 after a monster opener, logging 16 rushes for 45 yards on the ground. The veteran RB did see success in the passing game, logging five catches for 54 yards. With Tyson Bagent expected to start at quarterback for the Bears, Swift could be utilized more heavily on the ground. Philadelphia has also allowed 216 rushing yards to running backs this season, a bottom-10 mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: D'Andre Swift should remain Chicago's top option in the rushing game against the Jets in Week 4. Swift saw a season-high 20 carries in Week 3 versus Philly , taking them for 84 yards and adding on two catches for four yards. The veteran ball carrier eclipsed 80 rushing yards in two of the first three games of the campaign, but he's seen his only end zone appearances come from Week 1. He'll now turn his attention to a Jets defense that ceded 99 rushing yards and two touchdowns off 20 carries to Jahmyr Gibbs in their most recent outing.

player.seasonOutlook: Swift is entering his seventh NFL season and third with Chicago. The veteran back was busy as both a rusher and receiver en route to clearing 1,300 scrimmage yards in each of his first two seasons with the Bears. Though he found the end zone 10 times and finished 17th among backs in fantasy points per game last season, Swift deferred substantial work to Kyle Monangai and is likely to be in even more of a timeshare in 2026. Still in his prime at age 27, Swift continues to play at a high level (4.87 yards per carry last season), but his role in the Chicago offense figures to limit him to low-ceiling RB2/flex production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ladd McConkey seemed headed for a big performance in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching five of seven targets for 81 yards and a touchdown. However, he was knocked out of the game in the third quarter after a big hit left him with a rib injury. McConkey still led the team in receiving yards and was on the receiving end of Justin Herbert's only TD pass, and the club doesn't seem to believe the injury is serious. His status for Week 2 will remain up in the air until later in the week, if not right up to kickoff. If he is able to suit up, McConkey will be facing a Raiders secondary that was tied for 21st in points per game allowed to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ladd McConkey was clearly limited by a rib injury in the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders, catching all three of his targets for 35 yards. That was still good enough to tie for the team lead in receptions, however, as Justin Herbert and the entire offense continue to adjust to the new scheme instituted by OC Mike McDaniel. McConkey is Herbert's clear top downfield option, and as he gets healthier, his production should begin to look more like the 5-82-1 line he delivered in the season opener before getting hurt in the third quarter. McConkey will get a favorable matchup in Week 3 against a Bills secondary that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ladd McConkey seemed hampered by his rib injury in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills, but he still managed to turn five targets into four catches for 66 yards. The clear top option for Justin Herbert, McConkey has 15 targets through three games despite missing most of the second half in Week 2 after getting hurt, turning that volume into a 12-183-1 line. That's the only touchdown Herbert has thrown to a wide receiver so far in 2026. McConkey should be a little healthier in Week 4, but he'll be facing a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: McConkey is looking to rebound after falling short of high expectations in 2025. The 2024 second-round pick was terrific as a rookie (82-1,155-7 receiving line and a 12th-place finish among WRs in fantasy points), but dipped to 66-789-6 line and a 30th-place finish last season. Though he ran considerably more routes, saw similar target numbers and was used a lot more near the goal line (seventh among WRs with 12 end zone targets), McConkey's efficiency plummeted, with his catch rate dipping from 74% to 62% and his yards per target from 10.4 to 7.4. The good news is that there's reason for optimism that he'll bounce back, as he has a new playcaller in Mike McDaniel, the Chargers' offense figures to improve with a much healthier line, and Keenan Allen is out of the picture. McConkey, 24, makes for a fine fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Sam LaPorta should remain a big part of Detroit's offense in Week 2 at Buffalo. In Week 1 against the Saints, LaPorta's 5-48-0 receiving line put him second to Amon-Ra St. Brown in receiving yards while tying Jahmyr Gibbs for second in catches. The fourth-year tight end will face a Bills defense that allowed 14.4 PPR points to Texans tight ends this past Sunday, so he'll have plenty of opportunities to build on his season-opening performance.
outlooksByWeek.3: Sam LaPorta will look to remain a top target as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. LaPorta recorded six catches for 52 yards and his first touchdown of the season against the Bills in Week 2. The starting tight end has now been targeted 15 times across two games, and he's converted these into 11 grabs for 100 yards and a touchdown. He'll face a New York defense that held Green Bay's Tucker Kraft to just two catches for 15 yards this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Sam LaPorta should remain a complementary option as the Lions play the Panthers in Week 4. LaPorta caught three of four targets for 44 yards against the Jets in Week 3, which was his quietest game of the year. Detroit's ability to score and defensive problems keep the passing game alive even when running back Jahmyr Gibbs is tearing it up on the ground, so there don't look to be any issues with LaPorta's usage moving forward. He'll face a Carolina defense that ceded a 7-51-2 stat line to Harold Fannin in Week 3.

player.seasonOutlook: LaPorta has settled in as one of the league's top tight ends, but the 2023 second-round pick simply hasn't been able to match the fantasy success he enjoyed as a rookie. Since posting an 86-889-10 receiving line in 17 games that first season, LaPorta has totaled a 100-1,215-10 line in 25 games over the past two seasons. LaPorta's 2025 campaign was cut short by a back injury, otherwise he was well on his way to his third straight top-10 fantasy campaign (he finished seventh in PPG). The 25-year-old joins Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and Jahmyr Gibbs as the clear "Core Four" targets in a good, pass-friendly Detroit offense, and is thus a solid fantasy TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Patrick Mahomes proved he was fully recovered from last year's ACL injury in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, scoring a 15-yard rushing TD in addition to completing 15 of 27 passes for 184 yards and two touchdowns with one interception. The offense flowed through new lead back Kenneth Walker and benefited from some short fields, but Mahomes still took advantage of his opportunities. The star QB could be headed for better individual numbers in Week 2 against a Colts defense that looked awful in its opener and which ranked 31st in passing yards allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Patrick Mahomes has Kansas City's offense humming, and through two games, he's produced 566 passing yards and a 5:1 TD:INT while adding a touchdown on the ground. The superstar QB has spread the ball around effectively, as five different targets have been on the end of those TDs, and a revitalized running game with Kenneth Walker has prevented defenses from laying back and clogging the passing lanes. Mahomes could be headed for big numbers in Week 3 against a Dolphins defense that has yet to record a sack in 2026 and which sits 32nd in completion rate against at a stunning 78.8%.
outlooksByWeek.4: Patrick Mahomes continued his strong start to the season in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins, producing multiple touchdowns for a third straight game. The two-time MVP has a 7:2 TD-to-INT ratio in those three contests while adding another score on the ground, and his 8.3 yards per attempt would be his highest mark since 2019. He's done it without the benefit of a single dominant receiver, as Travis Kelce, Kenneth Walker, Rashee Rice, and Xavier Worthy have all logged between 15 and 18 targets. Mahomes will look to keep rolling in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mahomes is a bit of a wild card as he embarks on his 10th season. The two-time NFL MVP followed up a pair of disappointing fantasy seasons (2023-24) with an elite start to 2025 (24.5 points per game during Weeks 1-8) and a disappointing finish that included 15.0 points per game during his final six games and a torn ACL in Week 15. Mahomes' efficiency has dipped the past three seasons, and while he made up ground as a rusher in 2025 (fifth among QBs in rushing yards and TDs despite three missed games), he might not be able to run as often this season as he recovers fully from the knee injury. Mahomes will be ready to play in Week 1, but he hasn't been a consistent fantasy QB1 since 2022. He's a risky mid-round flier in drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Kelce showed he still has plenty left in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, leading the team with 71 receiving yards while catching three of five targets. The veteran tight end's production tailed off the last couple years, but he still topped 800 receiving yards in 12 straight seasons, and Week 1's performance moved him past Jason Witten into second place on the NFL's all-time list for TEs with 13,073 yards, trailing only Tony Gonzalez's 15,127. Kelce will take on a Colts defense in Week 2 that ranked 31st in receiving yards allowed to tight ends in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Kelce continued a strong start to his 14th NFL season in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, posting a 9-101-1 line on 11 targets. The future Hall of Famer last delivered a 1,000-yard campaign in 2022, but he's jumped out to an early pace in 2026 that would see him top 1,400 receiving yards and set a new career high. With Patrick Mahomes spreading the ball around and the offense prioritizing Kenneth Walker and the run game, Kelce may need to rely on spike games rather than steady production for his fantasy value. He'll take on a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's allowed 10.2 yards per target to tight ends through two weeks, 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Travis Kelce notched just two targets in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins, but he caught both for 59 yards and a touchdown. The future Hall of Famer seems revitalized in his age-36 season, and he's already hauled in two catches of 40 or more yards, just one short of the career-high three he produced way back in 2016. Patrick Mahomes is spreading the ball around effectively, and Kelce, Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets through three games. The tight end has turned his volume into a strong 14-231-2 line. Kelce will look to keep rolling in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs and has already coughed up five TDs to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Kelce re-signed with the Chiefs and is returning for what might be his final NFL season. The veteran tight end's days as an elite producer are behind him, and he saw a notable dip in usage last season (19.6% target share was his lowest since 2014). Kelce did hold up for 17 games and still finished in the top 10 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy PPG. Kelce has reeled off 10 consecutive top-five fantasy campaigns despite not offering much in the scoring department (he hasn't cleared five TDs in a season since 2022). The 36-year-old's role could dip even further this season, so he's best valued as a fringe TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: A.J. Brown won't suit up for at least four weeks for the Patriots, beginning in Week 2 against the Steelers, after landing on injured reserve due to a high-ankle sprain. Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas and Mack Hollins figure to be New England's top three wideouts.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown was traded to the Patriots in June. The veteran receiver enters 2026 looking to continue his streak of finishing in the top 15 in fantasy points per game during each of the four seasons he was with the Eagles. That includes an 11th-place finish in 2025 in which Brown reached the 1,000-yard mark for the sixth time in his seven NFL seasons while finding the end zone exactly seven times for the third year in a row. Brown continues to benefit from elite usage (he has finished no lower than seventh among WRs in target share each of the past seven seasons) and elite efficiency (he has finished 80th percentile or better in yards per route run all seven years). He could use more end zone targets in New England (he had a career-low four last season), but Brown, 29, is set to work as Drake Maye's top target in a good Patriots' offense. He is a fringe fantasy WR1.

outlooksByWeek.2: DJ Moore will look to build on an impressive debut when the Bills host the Lions in Week 2. Despite new quarterback Josh Allen continuing to spread the ball around, Moore popped with a 100-yard outing on eight targets. The Lions gave up 410 passing yards to open the year, but just 7.3 yards per attempt as New Orleans was forced to throw from behind. That may not be the case Thursday, and Moore is unlikely to garner high volume. Even so, facing a secondary void of high-end talent, Moore can get deep and provide big yardage without a lot of opportunity.
outlooksByWeek.3: DJ Moore will need to overcome a shoulder injury if he is to help the Bills in Week 3 against the Chargers. After showing sound chemistry with Josh Allen in his first action for Buffalo, Moore failed to haul in a touchdown late in the second quarter in Week 2, suffering the injury that forced him to miss the second half. The Chargers have allowed three touchdowns to opposing receivers through two weeks and two 75-plus yardage performances, which should thrust Moore back into fantasy relevance if he's able to reprise his No. 1 WR role.
outlooksByWeek.4: DJ Moore aims to remain heavily involved in the Bills' Week 4 game against the Patriots. In two healthy games, Moore has 18 targets as Josh Allen's top option, creating a stable floor. New England's secondary is middling, allowing the 18th-most fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts, but outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, no one has topped 64 yards against them. Moore's potential could be further capped if he draws shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez.

player.seasonOutlook: Moore was traded to Buffalo after spending his first eight NFL seasons with Carolina and Chicago. A featured target throughout most of his career, Moore was reduced to a 16% target share in 2025 -- his lowest since his rookie year in 2018. The result was a 35th-place finish in fantasy points, which ended a streak of six consecutive top 25s. Moore now heads to Buffalo with Khalil Shakir as his only roadblock to emerging as Josh Allen's No. 1 target in Buffalo's high-scoring offense. Still in his prime at age 29, Moore has the look of a fantasy WR3 with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: David Montgomery scored three total TDs in his Texans debut in Week 1 and profiles as a borderline fantasy RB1 for a Week 2 home game against a Bengals defense that gave up 93 scrimmage yards and a score to Tampa Bay's Bucky Irving. Montgomery had 23 touches to Woody Marks' 10 in Week 1 against the Bills, so the former Lions RB is operating as the clear lead back for his new team. Montgomery's 23 Week 1 touches were more than he had in any game last season with Detroit. Cincinnati beefed up its defensive front in the offseason after allowing the most rushing yards in the NFL last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: David Montgomery produced just 24 scrimmage yards in Houston's Week 2 loss to the Bengals after scoring three TDs in his Texans debut. The veteran RB will cede some backfield work to Woody Marks, particularly if the Texans are forced to play catch-up, but Montgomery is the team's preferred option in valuable red-zone and short-yardage situations. Montgomery is poised for a bounce-back effort in Week 3 and can be trusted as a fantasy RB2 against a Colts defense that's allowing 177 yards per game on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.4: David Montgomery is averaging a paltry 2.8 yards per carry, and Houston's offensive line has struggled to open up holes heading into a Week 4 home game against the Cowboys. The offseason trade acquisition scored three TDs in his Texans' debut but hasn't found the end zone since. Through three games, Montgomery has out-touched Woody Marks 44-29, but Marks scored a one-yard touchdown in the Week 3 loss to the Colts, so Montgomery doesn't have a monopoly on short-yardage opportunities. The Cowboys are allowing 27.3 points per game and have surrendered four total TDs to RBs, so Montgomery is a fantasy RB2 for Week 4, albeit a touchdown-dependent one.

player.seasonOutlook: Montgomery was traded to Houston after spending his first seven NFL seasons with Chicago and Detroit. The veteran back is coming off a down year in 2025, when he posted career lows in touches (182), yardage (908, his first season under 1,000) and fantasy points per game (9.8). Montgomery was still effective as a rusher (4.53 yards per carry, 2.28 yards after contact) but lost work to Jahmyr Gibbs and wasn't involved much as receiver. The latter doesn't figure to change much in Houston, and while Montgomery is a decent bet to pace the team in carries, second-year back Woody Marks figures to sustain a substantial offensive role. Montgomery enters his age-29 season as a touchdown-dependent flex with limited upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Parker Washington can safely be started as a fantasy WR2 in Week 2, even with the Jaguars facing a stout Broncos secondary. Washington paced Jacksonville's pass catchers with five catches for 83 yards and a TD on six targets in the season opener. In his last five games, including the playoffs, Washington has racked up 31 catches, 537 yards, and four TDs. Fellow Jaguars WR Brian Thomas (shoulder) tends to draw significant defensive attention, which should keep top Broncos CB Patrick Surtain from shadowing Washington as long as Thomas suits up.
outlooksByWeek.3: Parker Washington has established himself as the No. 1 WR for the Jaguars and is headed toward weekly fantasy WR1 territory ahead of a Week 3 home game against the Patriots. New England has one of the league's best secondaries, led by CB Christian Gonzalez, but Washington appears largely matchup-proof considering the 24-year-old WR just accounted for 98 of Trevor Lawrence's 189 passing yards in a Week 2 loss to Denver that could wind up being Lawrence's worst performance of the season. Washington has at least five catches and 83 receiving yards in each of his last five games, as well as three touchdown catches over that span, so the breakout star can be started with confidence regardless of the opponent.
outlooksByWeek.4: Parker Washington has entered set-and-forget fantasy WR1 territory. Jacksonville's top wideout is likely to thrive in Week 4 against a suspect Bengals secondary that just allowed touchdowns to Steelers WRs Roman Wilson, DK Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek. Despite facing the strong Cleveland, Denver, and New England secondaries, Washington is averaging 74 yards per game with two TDs through three weeks to start 2026 after averaging 116 receiving yards and scoring twice in the final three games of the 2025 regular season.

player.seasonOutlook: A strong finish to the 2025 season has made Washington one of the fascinating breakout candidates of 2026. Though he's primarily worked as a situational/depth player since being drafted in the sixth round in 2023, Washington has flashed when asked to play a bigger role. In 21 games since the start of 2024 in which he had a route participation above 50%, Washington handled a 20% target share and averaged 12.2 fantasy PPG. He surprisingly emerged as Jacksonville's top target late last season, which included a stretch of four straight games with at least nine targets and 19 fantasy points to end the season. The 24-year-old appears to have cemented a big role in Jacksonville, though Jakobi Meyers, Brian Thomas Jr. and perhaps Travis Hunter will battle him for snaps and targets. Washington should be targeted for your flex spot.

outlooksByWeek.2: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns travel to take on the Buccaneers and their 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (26.8) to RBs in Week 2. The second-year back rushed 12 times for 33 yards and caught both targets for 17 yards during Cleveland's 34-10 Week 1 loss. Running lanes and beneficial game flow are two things to be concerned with for Judkins, as the Browns again appear to be one of the worst offenses in the league. If the QB play improves even slightly, he could see an uptick in opportunities in both the running and passing games, but he should be started with caution until that situation improves.
outlooksByWeek.3: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Panthers to town for an interconference showdown in Week 3. He finished Cleveland's 23-19 upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with 12 carries for 21 yards and caught all five targets for 27 yards. No other running back tallied more than two carries, so it's clear Judkins is still the No. 1 option out of the backfield, but that hasn't come with much success through two weeks of action. Next up is a Carolina defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points allowed (36.3) and last in TDs surrendered to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Steelers to town for an AFC North clash on Thursday night in Week 4. He rushed 18 times for 70 yards and caught both targets for nine yards during Cleveland's upset win over the Panthers in Week 3. Judkins surpassed 35 yards on the ground for the first time this season, and there's a chance he could build upon that against their division rivals. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (22.1) per game to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Judkins is entering his second NFL season after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which a solid 14-game stretch of action was bookended by missed time early because of an off-field issue and late because of a season-ending leg injury in Week 16. When on the field, Judkins handled a massive 71.4% share of Cleveland's designed rush attempts (16.4 per game). Though he was held to 3.6 yards per carry, he was dealing with a league-high 7.4 box defenders per attempt. He wasn't involved much as a receiver (2.6 targets per game), however, and was limited to 12.1 fantasy points per game (26th among RBs). The Cleveland offense has a new coach (Todd Monken) and quarterback questions remain, so while Judkins has a clear path to a big carry total, the 22-year-old might cap out as a midrange RB2 in 2026.

The No. 1 D/ST selected on average last season, the Steelers finished a disappointing 14th in fantasy points and scored fewer than five points in 8-of-17 games. They've since overhauled their coaching staff, with Mike McCarthy replacing Mike Tomlin, and Patrick Graham as defensive coordinator, the same role he held with the Raiders from 2022-25. The offseason additions of S Jaquan Brisker and CB Jamel Dean should bolster this unit, and it benefits greatly from one of the softest September and October schedules in the league. Get this D/ST early, but be prepared to seek a replacement after that point.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Waddle did not contribute much in his Broncos' debut, catching just one of three targets for a meager two yards in the Week 1 loss to Kansas City. Steve Spagnuolo's rebuilt secondary prioritized taking Waddle out of the picture, and the former Dolphin wideout hasn't yet established enough chemistry with QB Bo Nix to overcome consistent double teams. Waddle will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Waddle broke out in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars, erupting for an 8-138-0 line on 10 targets as he began to get on the same page as quarterback Bo Nix. Waddle logged plenty of downfield targets but also had a red zone look, usage that promises plenty more big performances. The former Dolphin hasn't had a 1,000-yard season since 2023, but the early returns in Denver suggest he'll have little trouble returning to that level in 2026. He'll face a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, but three of those have gone for touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Waddle is struggling to adjust to his new offense with the Broncos. The former Dolphins wide receiver caught only two of his seven targets in a Week 3 win over the Rams for 10 yards, while adding a 14-yard run. Waddle leads Denver with 20 targets through three games, but he's turned them into just 11 catches for 150 yards, and he's still looking for his first TD of the season. He'll face a 49ers secondary in Week 4 that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Waddle was traded to Denver after spending his first five seasons in Miami. The 2021 first-round pick was solid during his Dolphins tenure, finishing in the top 30 among receivers in fantasy PPG four times, though never reaching the top 10 while often playing second fiddle to Tyreek Hill. Although he has been a reliable target and has missed only seven games in five years, Waddle hasn't finished a season higher than 20th in targets or catches since 2021. In Denver, the 27-year-old Waddle will compete with Courtland Sutton for the team lead in targets in a scheme that likes to spread the ball around. Not utilized near the goal line much at 5-foot-10 and 180 pounds (he's yet to clear seven end zone targets in a season), Waddle is likely to max out as a back-end WR2 in Denver.

outlooksByWeek.2: Christian Watson will seek to build off a monster outing as the Packers travel to take on the Jets in Week 2. Watson ended a Week 1 loss to the Vikings with a dominant stat line, catching six of his eight targets for 147 yards and two touchdowns. The fifth-year wideout could be a breakout star this season, especially if Green Bay continues to deploy a pass-heavy offense. The Jets secondary, who gave up a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1, looks weaker than Minnesota's as well.
outlooksByWeek.3: Christian Watson remains the top option in Green Bay's offense as they take on the Falcons in Week 3. Watson finished with a quieter four catches for 41 yards and a touchdown against the Jets in Week 2, but he did garner an impressive 11 targets. The fifth-year wideout has now scored three touchdowns on a team-high 19 targets across two games. He'll take on an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Christian Watson will look to keep his touchdown streak rolling as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 4. Watson finished Week 3 against the Falcons with seven catches for 96 yards and a touchdown, putting him at a 17-284-4 receiving line on the year. The fifth-year wideout remains quarterback Jordan Love's top option at this point in the year, with him and Matthew Golden making for a dangerous duo so far. Watson will face a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-ten 25.4 fantasy points per game to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Watson has had quite the boom/bust NFL career and that was on full display in 2025. After missing the first seven games due to injury, Watson returned and scored 18-plus fantasy points four times, but averaged 7.7 in his other six outings. The oft-injured 2022 second-round pick has still yet to play a full regular season, but has weirdly finished with between 611 and 620 receiving yards in three of his four campaigns. Though Watson has yet to deliver a top-40 fantasy season, he's been extremely efficient in his vertical role, ranking exactly second in average depth of target, YPR and YPT each of the last two seasons. Durability is an obvious concern, but the 27-year-old could very well lead Green Bay in targets following Romeo Doubs' departure. Watson should be valued as a volatile flex option with added value in non-PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chuba Hubbard is expected to continue leading the Panthers' backfield in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Hubbard out-touched Jonathon Brooks 13 to five in the Week 1 loss, which is a good sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. Hubbard also found the end zone twice and looked very efficient, averaging 6.7 yards per touch. He's in for a tougher Week 2 matchup, however, as Atlanta allowed just 16.4 PPR fantasy points to the running back position last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' top running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Hubbard appears to have returned to his 2024 form over Carolina's first two games this season, rushing for 102 yards (4.6 yards per carry) and a touchdown while catching all five of his targets for 49 yards and a score. Additionally, with Jonathon Brooks (groin) exiting the Week 2 win in the fourth quarter, Hubbard's role could continue growing. He faces a difficult matchup, however, as the Browns' defense has given up just 16.9 PPR fantasy points per game through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Without Jonathon Brooks (groin) in the Week 3 loss, Hubbard accounted for 82.1 percent of the Panthers' running back touches (23 to AJ Dillon's five). Despite Carolina throwing the ball over 40 times per game this season, Hubbard has remained one of fantasy's most productive backs, averaging 16.7 opportunities and 17.7 PPR points per game. He's likely to remain the bell-cow in Carolina's Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 19.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Hubbard is coming off a disappointing 2025 campaign in which he battled injury and lost lead-back duties to Rico Dowdle. The veteran was limited to 734 yards on 164 touches (he cleared 275 touches and 1,100 yards in 2023 and 2024), and he ranked 64th among 65 qualified backs in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Still in his prime at age 27, a bounce-back season is possible, especially with Dowdle gone and unproven Jonathon Brooks as his competition for touches. Hubbard should be considered a flex/bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dak Prescott was held to just 175 passing yards in the season opener for the Cowboys.  Dak did toss two touchdowns, but he also threw a costly interception before the end of the first half, which led to a Giants touchdown. Despite a porous secondary, the Giants kept the star wideouts for the Cowboys in check, leaving Dak with an uninspiring output. Prescott will look to rebound in Week 2 versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dak Prescott tossed four touchdowns last game in a virtuoso performance for the Cowboys. Prescott completed 26-of-31 throws for 279 yards and the four scores in the dominant 37-20 win over the Commanders. Prescott has six touchdowns and just one pick through the first two games of the young season. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dak Prescott threw for 276 yards and a touchdown in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens last game. Dak has passed for at least 275 yards through the air in each of the last two contests for the Cowboys, while also failing to toss a single interception over that span. In Week 4, the Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Prescott is entering his 11th NFL season following a successful 2025 campaign in which he led the NFL in completions and ranked no lower than fourth in dropbacks, pass attempts, passing yards and passing TDs. Prescott appeared in all 17 games and has now finished no worse than 11th in fantasy points during all seven seasons in which he has played at least 16 games. Last season, his nine top-10 fantasy weeks were tied for third most at the position. Prescott is no longer much of a threat with his legs, but he should continue to put up big passing numbers with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens at his disposal. The 33-year-old is a fringe QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jason Myers will look to remain perfect this season when the Seahawks visit Arizona in Week 2. Myers made his lone PAT try and both field-goal attempts in a season-opening win over New England, though his FGs were relative chip shots from 30 and 26 yards. Myers made nine field goals from 50-plus yards out each of the previous two seasons, however, so he has plenty of leg to convert from that distance when called upon. The Cardinals aren't expected to be a top NFL defense this year, but they performed well in limiting the Chargers to 14 points in a Week 1 victory.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jason Myers has provided Seattle with a steady boot this season heading into a Week 3 matchup against Washington. The veteran kicker has made all three of his field-goal tries and all five of his PAT attempts through two weeks. However, he hasn't yet been asked to hit from distance, as none of his FG tries have been from 40 yards or greater. The Commanders have yielded a whopping 30.5 points per game through two weeks, so Myers could get plenty of opportunities to kick in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jason Myers enters Seattle's Week 4 clash against the Chargers having not missed a kick so far this season. Myers handled only relatively short kicks over his first two games, but he showed off his leg with a 57-yard field goal against Washington in Week 3. The veteran kicker is now 4-for-4 on FG tries and 9-for-9 on extra-point attempts this season. Opponents have gone 6-for-7 on field-goal attempts against the Chargers so far this year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Terry McLaurin had a rough Week 1 for the Commanders. On only four targets, McLaurin caught a mere two passes for 14 yards in the 24-22 loss to the Eagles. Meanwhile, both Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams found the end zone in their respective debuts for Washington. It will be interesting to see if the presence of Diggs in particular impacts McLaurin, as Diggs more than doubled McLaurin in targets with nine. Both wideouts should see plenty of action in Week 2 versus a poor Cowboys defense, though. Dallas allowed 229 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air to Jaxson Dart in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Terry McLaurin led the Commanders in targets last game with nine opportunities. Unfortunately, Scary Terry could only cash in two of those chances for 50 yards in a loss to the Cowboys. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, and veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for McLaurin and the rest of the Washington offense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Terry McLaurin is coming off his best game of the season for the Commanders. Scary Terry had six catches for 77 yards and a touchdown in the shocking 33-31 victory over the Seattle Seahawks. McLaurin has posted nine targets in back-to-back contests.  McLaurin caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: McLaurin is eyeing a bounce-back campaign following a lost 2025 season in which both he (seven missed games) and quarterback Jayden Daniels (10 missed games) were sidelined for extended periods. The dud season came after Daniels helped McLaurin to a career year in 2024, which included 13 touchdowns (second most among WRs) and a seventh-place finish in fantasy points. McLaurin's target ceiling remains a concern (he's been in the 21-25% target share range each of his seven seasons), but with his quarterback healthy and his role as a vertical threat in new playcaller David Blough's offense, McLaurin is certainly poised for a rebound. The 30-year-old is best valued as a mid-to-back-end WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Jones is primed to lead Minnesota's backfield in Week 2 at Chicago. Jones (29 of 65 offensive snaps) and Jordan Mason (30 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps in Week 1, but Mason led the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Jones still remained heavily involved, as he logged 12 rushes for 40 yards and one touchdown. This week and beyond, Jones will be set to lead the backfield with Mason on IR for a thumb injury. Jones will look to make the most of his likely increased opportunities against a Bears defense that allowed 33.7 PPR points to Panthers running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Jones should continue to have a high-usage role as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 2 with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 23 times for 105 yards. The veteran running back should continue to have a huge role in the coming weeks, while questions remain with the passing game under returning quarterback Kyler Murray. Jones will face a Buccaneers defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 19.5 PPR points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Aaron Jones should remain a high-volume option as the Vikings play Miami in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 3 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 17 times for 58 yards and recording five catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield doesn't look to be changing with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Miami defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (32.9) to running backs so far this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Jones is back for a third season in Minnesota after an injury-plagued 2025 campaign limited him to 747 yards (his fewest since his rookie season in 2017) and three touchdowns in 12 games. Jones remained fairly busy (11.0 carries and 3.4 targets per game) but didn't perform well, ranking dead last among 65 backs with 50-plus carries in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Jones failed to record a single top-10 fantasy outing. Now 31 years old, Jones remains a starter and will get some run, but he's well past his prime and unlikely to return to consistent fantasy output. Jones is best valued as a bench player with occasional flex appeal.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bhayshul Tuten is likely to get the majority of touches in Jacksonville's backfield in Week 2 against the Broncos, just as he did in the season-opening win over the Browns. Tuten turned 16 touches into 88 yards in Week 1, while Chris Rodriguez and Ameer Abdullah combined for 55 yards on 11 touches, though Rodriguez siphoned some valuable goal-line work. Denver's defense gave up the second-fewest rushing yards in the NFL last season but just allowed Chiefs RBs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson to combine for 259 scrimmage yards and two TDs in a Week 1 loss. Tuten has RB2 upside given his prominent role in a high-powered Jaguars offense, but he's more of a flex/RB3 for Week 2 against a talented Broncos defense searching for a rebound in their home opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bhayshul Tuten emerged as the clear No. 1 option in Jacksonville's backfield heading into a Week 3 home game against the Patriots, ahead of Chris Rodriguez and pass-catching specialists LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah. Through the first two games of his sophomore season, Tuten turned 28 carries and three targets into 150 scrimmage yards and one TD. The speedster is a viable RB3/flex for Week 3, though expectations should be tempered against a New England defense that's off to an elite start, having allowed just 16 points through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bhayshul Tuten is averaging 80 scrimmage yards and takes a two-game touchdown streak into Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals. Tuten is locked in atop the running back depth chart in one of the league's best offenses, which makes him a reliable fantasy RB2, even with Chris Rodriguez, LeQuint Allen, and Ameer Abdullah siphoning touches here and there. Cincinnati has been better than average against the run, but the Bengals have allowed a league-high 141 receiving yards to RBs, so Tuten is likely to make some plays as a pass-catcher even if running room is hard to come by.

player.seasonOutlook: Tuten is positioned to take over lead-back duties in Jacksonville following the offseason departure of Travis Etienne Jr. Tuten played sparingly as a rookie, totaling 83 carries and 14 targets in 15 games. He cleared 10 touches in only one game (a 15-touch, 74-yard effort in Week 11), but he did find the end zone in all four games in which he had at least eight touches. The 2025 fourth-round pick will see some scoring regression (seven TDs on 93 touches), but he flashed in limited work, can contribute as a rusher and receiver, is working in a good offense and has only journeyman Chris Rodriguez Jr. and passing-down specialist LeQuint Allen Jr. as his competition. Tuten is still unproven, but the 23-year-old has a path to a breakout season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Harold Fannin and the Browns visit the Buccaneers in Week 2, facing the 30th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (25.1) to TEs. The second-year pro managed two catches on three targets for 21 yards during Cleveland's 34-10 loss in the season opener. Fannin has the perfect chance at a rebound performance against Tampa Bay, as Cincinnati's Mike Gesicki cooked their defense with five receptions for 78 yards and a TD in Week 1. Even with poor quarterback play, Fannin has the talent and opportunity as the focal point of an offense that might not be good but will be forced to throw the ball plenty while playing from behind.
outlooksByWeek.3: Harold Fannin and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3 for their 2026 home opener. He finished Cleveland's 23-19 win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with five catches on six targets for 54 yards. Fannin is still searching for his first TD of the season after collecting six as a rookie, as fellow tight end Blake Whiteheart was on the receiving end of a 17-yard score from Deshaun Watson. Fannin looks to find the end zone against Carolina's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (9.0) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns host their division rival Steelers in Week 4 for an AFC North clash between two 2-1 teams. He caught seven of nine targets for 51 yards and two TDs during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3, including the game-winning score. Fannin led the team in receptions and yardage while tying KC Concepcion for first in targets. He now has a 12-126-2 line on 18 targets across three contests as one of Deshaun Watson's favorite receivers. Fannin will have a tough matchup against Pittsburgh's seventh-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (9.3) to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Fannin is a rising star at the tight end position after overcoming the presence of David Njoku and a quarterback merry-go-round to produce a 72-731-6 receiving line (plus 7-13-1 rushing) as a 21-year-old rookie last season. The third-round pick's 108 targets rank eighth all time by a rookie tight end, and he finished no lower than eighth at the position in catches, yards, touchdowns and fantasy points last season. Fannin figures to see some touchdown regression (seven TDs, 3.8 expected, three end zone targets) and Cleveland still has quarterback question marks, but with Njoku gone, Fannin has a path to improve a bit on what was already a healthy 22% target share. He's a solid TE1 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Evans had a strong 49ers debut last Thursday versus the Rams and will next face Miami in Week 2. Evans caught six passes for 49 yards and a touchdown in the season opener, with his score coming on a two-yard connection with quarterback Brock Purdy. The veteran wideout tied with Deebo Samuel for the most targets among SF wideouts, so he looks to have already established a good rapport with Purdy. Evans could be in for another strong performance Sunday against a Titans defense that allowed three passing touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Evans picked up a hip injury in San Francisco's win over Miami on Sunday, but early indications suggest he'll be fine for a Week 3 matchup versus the Cardinals. Evans has established a nice rapport with QB Brock Purdy so far this season, as the veteran wideout has caught nine of 10 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown. San Francisco's WR corps has been thinned by the season-ending injury to rookie De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) and Demarcus Robinson's more recent ankle injury, which will likely sideline him for Week 3, so Evans' availability as a reliable target for Purdy has taken on increased importance. Arizona was crushed by star wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-155-3 receiving line) in Week 2 and has given up four total receiving TDs to wideouts through two games.
