outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Evans' status for San Francisco's Week 4 game against Denver is cloudy due to injuries to his ribs and oblique. Evans was injured in the second quarter of Sunday's win over Arizona and wasn't able to return to the contest. He had gotten off to a strong start prior to the injury, catching three passes for 34 yards and a touchdown. If he's able to suit up against Denver, he'll face a tough challenge against star cornerback Patrick Surtain and a defense that has allowed the NFL's second-lowest catch rate (50.9%) to WRs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Evans signed with the 49ers after spending his first 12 NFL seasons with the Buccaneers. The future Hall of Famer famously opened his career with 11 consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, but that streak ended when he missed nine games due to injury last season. Even when active, Evans wasn't his usual, productive self, delivering only one weekly fantasy finish better than 23rd and none better than 11th. Now 33 years old, Evans is past his prime, but he's in line for a decent chunk of the targets, especially near the goal line, in Kyle Shanahan's high-scoring offense. Evans is best valued as a touchdown-dependent WR3/flex with more value in non-PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Colston Loveland will look to get more involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Loveland disappointed in Week 1 against the Panthers, failing to bring in either of his two targets, even though it was the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The second-year tight end's output was hopefully a fluke, especially as he was still on the field for 86 percent of Chicago's offensive snaps. Loveland will also face a Minnesota defense that allowed five catches for 115 yards to Green Bay's tight ends in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Colston Loveland will look to turn things around as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Loveland disappointed again in Week 2, catching just one of three targets for three yards against the Vikings. The second-year tight end now has just one catch on the year, which is nowhere near the breakout season managers were projecting. He'll likely be thrown to by Tyson Bagent against Philly defense that's allowed the fewest PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season (5.1).
outlooksByWeek.4: Colston Loveland will look to improve his role even more as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Loveland finally saw more than a chalked role against the Eagles in Week 3, reeling in all four of his targets for 31 yards. This output is far from what was expected of the second-year tight end heading into the season, but it's still optimistic for the future. He'll face a New York defense that's ceded a top-ten 8.0 fantasy points per game to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: After averaging 4.1 targets and 8.5 fantasy PPG during his first 14 NFL games, Loveland leaped to 12.0 targets (10-plus in each) and 20.0 fantasy PPG during his final four games of 2025 (including the playoffs). For perspective, there have been only 12 instances of a tight end seeing at least 10 targets in four consecutive regular-season games in NFL history (and only one was a rookie). Loveland's overall efficiency was terrific, as he ranked eighth or better among tight ends in YPR, YPT and YPRR. With DJ Moore gone, the 2025 first-round pick enters his age-22 season all but locked into a massive workload alongside Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III. Loveland's ceiling is lofty, and midrange fantasy TE1 should be his floor.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel in Week 2 to face the Patriots, who have the ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.0) to RBs. He rushed 10 times for 46 yards and caught five of six targets for 27 yards in Pittsburgh's 20-13 win against Atlanta. Warren lost a fumble, but he still out-touched fellow RB Rico Dowdle 15-10 and had much better results from those opportunities. If the Steelers continue to favor the passing game against New England, or if they're forced into it via game flow, Warren would carry a bit more value in what looks to be a true timeshare.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers welcome the Bengals to town for a Week 3 AFC North matchup. He rushed 11 times for 43 yards and brought in two of four targets for 34 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to New England. Warren handled 11 of 20 carries from backs in this one, but the Steelers weren't able to get much going on offense. It looks like he's the 1A out of the backfield, and although it's not by a substantial amount, Rico Dowdle is considered questionable to suit up on Sunday with a toe injury. Warren faces a 14th-ranked Cincinnati defense in fantasy points allowed (19.0) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to take on the Browns for an AFC North clash in Week 4. He rushed 17 times for 127 yards and caught three of four targets for 49 yards during Pittsburgh's thrilling 30-27 victory in Week 3. Warren handled a workhorse role with Rico Dowdle (toe) out, and it looks like that could again be the case with a short turnaround for Week 4's Thursday Night Football showcase in Cleveland. He'll face a tough matchup as the Browns rank sixth in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs and are one of seven teams yet to surrender a TD to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Warren reached career-high marks in touches (251), yardage (1,291) and touchdowns (eight) last season, his fourth in the league. The former undrafted free agent put up 13.6 fantasy points per game (19th among backs) and PFF tracked him with 56 forced missed tackles (seventh). Pittsburgh swapped out Kenneth Gainwell for Rico Dowdle as Warren's running mate, and the two are expected to split work in a Mike McCarthy offense that rarely deploys its backs in the passing game. Warren is capable and effective as a rusher and receiver, but his ceiling figures to be limited in this committee. He's likely to cap out as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dalton Kincaid will look to match a career outing when the Bills face the Lions in Week 2. Kincaid had a personal-best 130 yards in his season debut but, more importantly, played 77% of the team's snaps after topping 50% just three times last year. If Kincaid remains on the field at this rate, he's likely to soar past his previous season's output. He'll face a defense on Thursday night that allowed 87 yards and two touchdowns to tight ends in Week 1, suggesting his statistical surge can continue.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dalton Kincaid brings momentum into the Bills' Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. After a 130-yard opener, Kincaid posted seven catches for 95 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 against Detroit, playing on 66% of the offensive snaps. Opportunity, not talent, has been an issue as he hasn't played over a 50% snap share since Week 5 in 2025. The Chargers were dominated by Tre McBride in Week 1 but rebounded against the Brock Bowers-less Raiders tight end room last week. Kincaid's big numbers are poised to continue in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dalton Kincaid will seek to rebuild momentum when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. After gaining 225 yards in Weeks 1 and 2, Kincaid had just two catches for 38 yards in Week 3. Part of the decrease in volume could be DJ Moore's return to health, but Buffalo remains run-heavy, limiting Kincaid's looks. He recorded a 67% snap share, more than usual, so opportunity remains. Facing a Patriots defense that has defended the tight end position well dampens hope, having allowed only 84 total yards to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Kincaid is perhaps fantasy's biggest wild card among tight ends. The 2023 first-round pick has occasionally flashed a high ceiling (he actually led qualified tight ends in YPT and YPRR last season), but he also has missed substantial action (nine games the past two years) and has disappeared way too often (he failed to clear 13.1 fantasy points in any game in 2024, and never cleared six targets in a game in 2025). Kincaid was limited to a 37% snap share when active last season, and he has yet to finish a season better than 14th in fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old has TE1 upside, but he's tough to trust and has added target competition (WR DJ Moore) in 2026. Consider Kincaid only in the mid-to-late rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jameson Williams will seek to convert on more of his looks as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Williams garnered nine targets against the Saints in Week 1, but he reeled in just four of them for 45 yards. The fifth-year wide receiver will need to keep his catch rate well above 50 percent if he hopes to record a third-straight 1,000-yard campaign, but he'll luckily face a Bills defense that allowed the seventh-most PPR points (40.0) to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jameson Williams will look to do more as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Williams' output has been disappointing so far this season, with just six catches for 78 yards across two games. The fifth-year wideout has also reaped no benefits from Detroit's struggling defense, with Amon-Ra St. Brown currently carving out a monopoly in the wide receiver room. Williams will face a New York defense that's allowed 27.2 PPR points per game to its first two opponents, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jameson Williams has yet to find the end zone heading into the Lions' Week 4 game at Carolina. Williams totaled a season-high 49 yards against the Jets in Week 3, but he's now recorded four or less catches for 50 or fewer yards in every game this year. The fifth-year wideout will seek to get more out of Detroit's offensive success against a Panthers defense that's allowed a top-five 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season.

player.seasonOutlook: The slow start to Williams' career is a thing of the past after the speedster delivered 1,000-plus-yard campaigns each of the past two seasons. After breaking out with a 22nd-place fantasy finish (25th PPG) in 2024, Williams set new career highs in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns en route to a 12th-place finish (19th PPG) last season. A lack of goal-line work (eight career end zone targets) and some drop woes (NFL-high eight in 2025) are drawbacks, but Williams' explosive-play ability has led him to finish sixth or better in yards per reception and yards per target each of the past two seasons. The 25-year-old remains one of Jared Goff's top targets in Detroit's high-scoring offense and is a fine fantasy WR3 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Luther Burden will look to stay highly involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. While Week 1 was the highest-scoring game in NFL history, Burden and Chicago's pass-catching corps were overshadowed by a dominant ground game. The second-year wideout's five catches for 63 yards wasn't bad, but he definitely has potential to be more dominant moving forward. He'll take on a Minnesota defense that gave up a 6-147-2 receiving line to Christian Watson and 6-95-0 to Matthew Golden in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Luther Burden will aim to get things going as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Burden has had a slow start to his sophomore campaign, with just eight catches on 12 targets for 95 yards across two games. He could also be in for even worse output, given the unknowns that come with Tyson Bagent starting under center in place of Caleb Williams (hamstring). Burden will take on a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Luther Burden will aim to build on an impressive performance as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Burden had his first big time of the season against the Eagles in Week 3, turning 11 targets into seven catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wideout had a solid connection with veteran Case Keenum, who is likely to fill in under center for at least one more week, if not more. This bodes well for the future of Burden, but he will have to face a New York defense that's allowed the eleventh-least fantasy points per game (28.2) and fourth-least receiving yards (337) to wide receivers across three outings.

player.seasonOutlook: Burden enters his second NFL season as one of the most popular breakout candidates in fantasy. The 2025 second-round pick played sparingly during most of his rookie season, but flashed elite efficiency when called upon, ranking in the top five among wide receivers in catch rate (77%), yards per target (10.8), RAC (7.3) and YPRR (2.9). Burden is obviously an unproven commodity (he has two career top-20 fantasy outings, after all), but with DJ Moore no longer on the roster, he's a lock for a larger role and very well could lead Chicago in targets. He could cost a pretty penny on draft day, but Burden, 22, is a fine WR3 target with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Etienne is expected to remain New Orleans' top running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Despite Alvin Kamara (knee) being sidelined for the Week 1 overtime loss, Etienne only received nine carries, tying Kendre Miller for the most on the team. However, Etienne was busy as a receiver, catching seven of nine targets for 46 yards, which is a positive sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. He could be in for another productive week, as Baltimore's defense allowed 28.1 PPR fantasy points to running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Etienne is expected operate as New Orleans' top running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Despite signing a big contract with the Saints this past offseason, Etienne saw just 10 opportunities in the Week 2 win over the Ravens. He still leads the team in carries (17) but saw less work through the air, with Alvin Kamara (five catches on six targets) returning to the lineup. With Kamara back, Etienne may struggle to be fantasy relevant without finding the end zone against a Raiders defense that's allowed just 17.5 PPR fantasy points per game to RBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Etienne signed with the Saints after spending the first five seasons of his pro career with the Jaguars. The 2021 first-round pick has produced at least 1,399 scrimmage yards in three of the past four seasons and scored a career-high 13 touchdowns in 2025. A capable rusher and receiver, Etienne has already reached 1,000-plus rushing yards three times and has 35-plus catches in each of the past four seasons. Even if the Saints retain Alvin Kamara as a situational player, Etienne will have a clear path to feature-back duties in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough. That will be enough to position the 27-year-old for his third top-15 fantasy campaign in four years. Consider Etienne a solid RB2 target with backend RB1 upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Stafford and the Rams will look to bounce back from a rough season-opening loss when they face the Giants in Week 2. Stafford threw for just 155 yards with no TDs and one interception against San Francisco last Thursday. He did still manage to connect with favorite target Puka Nacua five times for 74 yards, but no other Rams pass catcher had more than 26 yards in the defeat. A matchup with the Giants awaits, but New York had good results against Dallas' passing game in Week 1, holding QB Dak Prescott to 175 yards with one interception, albeit with two TDs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Stafford will look to replicate a huge Week 2 performance when the Rams face Denver in Week 3. On Monday Night Football, Stafford threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns with one interception against the Giants. The reigning NFL MVP didn't have star wideout Puka Nacua (hip) for that contest, so he turned to veteran Davante Adams, who logged eight catches for 195 yards and two of Stafford's TDs. Denver could pose a more potent threat, as the Broncos have a talented secondary and have limited QBs to a 74.5 passer rating, fifth-best in the NFL, through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matthew Stafford will look to help guide the Rams to a much-needed win in Week 4 against Philadelphia following a disappointing 1-2 start to the season. Stafford threw for 390 yards and two touchdowns in Week 3 against Denver, but he also tossed two costly interceptions, including a pick-six. The reigning NFL MVP already has four interceptions on his ledger through three contests after logging just eight interceptions across 17 regular-season games last year. The Eagles have yet to pick off a pass this year, and they just got torched by Bears QB Case Keenum for 247 passing yards and two touchdowns.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL MVP, Stafford returns for his 18th NFL season and his fifth with the Rams. The 38-year-old is fresh off an elite season in which he led the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns, which allowed him nine top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for third most at the position). Stafford's third-place finish in fantasy points per game was his first top-10 finish since 2019, and some regression is likely due to a complete lack of rushing (65 or fewer rushing yards in five straight seasons and one rushing touchdown since 2017). Stafford still has receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams and a strong offensive line at his disposal, so another big passing season is possible. That's just enough to keep him in the fringe QB1 mix.

Brian Flores' blitz-happy defense has managed exactly 49 sacks, fourth-most in the league, in each of the past two seasons, playing a big part in the team finishing among the position's top seven in fantasy scoring in each of those years. Though Jonathan Allen and Jonathan Greenard are no longer with the team, the Vikings' draft selections of DTs Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange should at least keep them competitive up front. That said, the Vikings face a brutal opening schedule (GB, Week 1; @CHI, Week 2) and have one of the toughest second-half schedules in the league. Be prepared to pivot if this D/ST starts slowly.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rhamondre Stevenson will look for a heavier workload when the Patriots face the Steelers in Week 2. Stevenson notched 23 touches to open the year, and despite the potential return of TreVeyon Henderson (ankle), Stevenson should handle early-down work at a minimum. He's mainly an accumulator, averaging 4.0 yards per carry or less in two of the previous three seasons and just 2.8 to open 2026. But volume is king, and Stevenson likely has that since he also catches passes out of the backfield. Pittsburgh was vulnerable in Week 1 to receiving backs, plus Stevenson likely handles goal-line work, making him intriguing even in a difficult spot against a defense that allowed 3.8 yards per carry to open the year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rhamondre Stevenson's opportunities are questionable as the Patriots prepare for the Jaguars in Week 3. After a 23-touch season debut, Stevenson lost a fumble early in Week 2, an issue that's plagued him throughout his career, and ended with just seven touches. In a split backfield with Treveyon Henderson, New England will likely ride the Week 3 hot hand. Facing a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing rusher to go over 39 yards, both backs could be running uphill.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rhamondre Stevenson's role in the Patriots offense is declining ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Bills. The return of TreVeyon Henderson limited Stevenson to 13 rushes in Weeks 2 and 3, and unfavorable game flow and poor quarterback play are limiting his receiving opportunities. Buffalo is allowing the fifth-most fantasy points per game to opposing backs, but more receiving touchdowns (three) than rushing (two). Without certainty for double-digit touches, Stevenson comes with risk against a defense allowing a frugal 3.9 yards per carry.

player.seasonOutlook: Stevenson will battle with second-year back TreVeyon Henderson for touches in the New England backfield. The duo shared the backfield at times last season, but it was the veteran Stevenson who usually operated as the lead back. He earned the role, ranking fifth among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF, second in yards after contact (2.82) and first in yards per target (9.1). Stevenson, who is entering his sixth season, did miss three games (he has missed time three seasons in a row), and his overall volume was limited (9.3 carries and 2.7 targets per game), which led to a 25th-place finish in fantasy points. Now 28 years old and with Henderson still very much in the mix, Stevenson, who has one top-20 fantasy campaign to his name, is a low-upside bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: TreVeyon Henderson could make his season debut in Week 2 when the Patriots host the Steelers. Henderson missed last week due to an ankle injury but has returned to practice ahead of the matchup. Pass-blocking concerns were rumored to be an issue during the preseason, and facing a Steelers defense that rushes the passer well may keep Henderson on the sideline more than managers would like, in addition to a potentially limited role in his first game back. Pittsburgh allowed a mere 3.8 yards per carry in Week 1 but did allow 90 receiving yards to running backs, albeit that was Bijan Robinson. Split touches in a likely low-scoring game would require Henderson's patented big-play ability for him to be fantasy relevant.
outlooksByWeek.3: TreVeyon Henderson will look to build on an impressive debut when New England faces Jacksonville in Week 3. After missing Week 1 due to an ankle injury, Henderson shouldered 16 carries in Week 2, putting up 76 yards and a touchdown. While he wasn't targeted in the passing game, Henderson showed his elite big-play ability. Rhamondre Stevenson was an afterthought after losing an early fumble, but with New England struggling to pass the ball effectively, this has the look of a run-first, split backfield. Jacksonville is allowing just 3.2 yards per carry and 110 total rushing yards through two weeks, which will keep Henderson's Week 3 expectations in check.
outlooksByWeek.4: TreVeyon Henderson remains mired in a split backfield for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Henderson's snap share dropped from 60% to 35% in Week 3 as the Patriots played from behind, forcing Rhamondre Stevenson into a pass-blocking role. With only one catch through two games, Henderson isn't getting many opportunities to create his signature big play. Facing a defense that's allowing just 3.9 yards per carry while being more vulnerable to receiving backs, Henderson figures to be a boom-or-bust option.

player.seasonOutlook: Henderson enters Year 2 after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which he delivered three huge fantasy performances (28-plus points in all three) but otherwise played second fiddle to Rhamondre Stevenson (8.3 points per game in his other 14 games). Though his role was limited, Henderson was effective, averaging 5.1 yards per carry (eighth best) and catching 83% of his targets while scoring 10 touchdowns. The 2025 second-round pick is a candidate for a similar role in 2026, but it's unlikely that Stevenson will completely disappear after he also had a strong 2025. Henderson is safest as a bench option, but there's upside for a lot more if the 23-year-old is promoted to a lead role.

No team has as soft a schedule on the defensive side of things than do the Ravens; only the Cowboys (Week 3), Bengals (7 and 17) and Bills (8) stand out as particularly challenging matchups. That's a good thing, considering this unit finished a disappointing 21st in scoring last season. The Ravens still have stars on the defensive side, and the change in head coach to Jesse Minter and defensive coordinator to Anthony Weaver should fuel a rebound to some degree.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Likely scored twice in his debut for the Giants in Week 1, leading a stunning victory over the Cowboys. Likely caught all eight of his targets for 78 yards and the two scores to lead the Giants in receiving. Especially in the red zone and on third down, quarterback Jaxson Dart leaned heavily on his new tight end, something that should continue in Week 2 versus the Rams. Los Angeles allowed 205 passing yards and three touchdowns in its dismal season-opening loss to the 49ers, while also losing star acquisition Myles Garrett to a knee injury. Aaron Donald will make his return from retirement to help out the defensive line, though.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in both receptions and targets last game. Despite seeing 10 opportunities, though, Likely caught five passes for just 33 yards in the dismal loss to the Rams. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Likely will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaiah Likely's breakout season likely came to a crashing halt with the injury to Jaxson Dart. Likely managed just two catches for 13 yards in the win over the Titans last game. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which has limited the opportunities for Likely.  Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Likely signed with the Giants after four years of backing up Mark Andrews in Baltimore. Likely is reuniting with coach John Harbaugh and is finally expected to play a consistent offensive role. During his time in Baltimore, Likely was limited to 50% of the team's offensive snaps and never finished a season better than 20th among tight ends in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards or fantasy PPG. His only extensive stretch with Andrews sidelined came back in 2023. During the seven-game span, Likely posted a 23-356-6 receiving line on a 16% target share and averaged a solid 13.5 fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old is obviously unproven, but his receiving skills in New York's ascending offense are enough to put him on the TE2 radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Caleb Williams will look to build off a monster performance as the Bears take on the Vikings at home in Week 2. Williams delivered for Chicago in the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The third-year quarterback completed 21 of 29 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns while carrying the ball 10 times for 65 yards and two more TDs. Williams will have more of a challenge this upcoming Sunday, given that the Vikings allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (14.3) to quarterbacks in the 2025 season. Still, Minnesota's secondary is susceptible, as they ceded 387 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception to Jordan Love this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Caleb Williams is not expected to play in Week 3 as the Bears take on the Eagles. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is slated to get the start versus an Eagles defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks across two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Caleb Williams is unlikely to play in Week 4 as the Bears take on the Jets. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Case Keenum is slated to get the start again versus a Jets defense that gave up 269 passing yards and two touchdowns to Jared Goff in Week 3.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams enters his third NFL season after a solid rookie campaign in 2024 followed by a big leap forward in 2025. Williams finished last season no lower than 11th among QBs in pass attempts, completions, pass yards, passing TDs, carries, rush yards, rush TDs and fantasy points per game. While Williams' completion percentage was one of the worst in the league (58%), his dual-threat ability and turnover avoidance (seven INTs both seasons) has led to solid fantasy output. The 2024 No. 1 draft pick has a good supporting cast in playcaller Ben Johnson and a trio of young pass catchers in Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland. Williams is a fringe QB1 with upside for another leap.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdown passes in the first 33 minutes of Jacksonville's lopsided Week 1 win over the Browns before the Jaguars took their foot off the gas. He has 22 touchdown passes in his last eight starts, but the surging QB could face a stiffer test in a Week 2 road game against the Broncos. They boasted the NFL's third-stingiest scoring defense last season but just gave up 31 points to the Chiefs in Week 1. Lawrence has been effective enough recently to warrant starting in fantasy despite the daunting matchup, but he's unlikely to give managers a top-five performance in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trevor Lawrence crashed back down to earth with 189 passing yards and no TDs in the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver after tossing four touchdown passes in the season-opening win over Cleveland. Lawrence and the Jaguars return home for a Week 3 showdown with the Patriots, who have allowed just 16 total points in two games. The daunting matchup drops Lawrence to the QB1/QB2 borderline, so this could be the week to plug in an alternative option if available. Lawrence threw 22 touchdown passes in the eight starts preceding his Week 2 dud, so the 2021 first-overall pick maintains elite upside.
outlooksByWeek.4: Trevor Lawrence has thrown at least three touchdown passes in two of three games this season but is averaging just 205 passing yards per game. He'll maintain an elite ceiling in Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals, who have allowed the third-most passing yards. Cincinnati just gave up three passing TDs to Aaron Rodgers in Week 3 but hadn't allowed a touchdown pass prior to that game this season. Lawrence has been a fantasy QB1 more often than not since Parker Washington emerged as his go-to receiver in the second half of last season, and that looks unlikely to change in Week 4.

player.seasonOutlook: Lawrence is entering his sixth NFL season after a breakout 2025 in which he ranked no lower than seventh among quarterbacks in pass attempts, completions, yards and touchdowns, as well as top 10 in carries, yards and TDs. He reeled off seven consecutive top-10 fantasy outings to finish the season. Lawrence's efficiency has been fine, at best, but he continues to generate big volume, having finished in the top 10 among QBs in pass and rush attempts in each of his four full seasons. With a strong, deep group of pass catchers and Liam Coen back as playcaller, the 26-year-old is well positioned for mid-to-back-end QB1 production.

outlooksByWeek.2: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are in New England to face the Patriots in Week 2. The veteran wideout corralled four of 10 targets for 40 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 win against the Falcons. He led the team in targets by four but finished third in receiving yards. Metcalf has a hypothetical advantage over Michael Pittman after playing last year with Aaron Rodgers, and there's a good chance he'll be his favorite target against New England's 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (33.1) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: DK Metcalf and the Steelers host the Bengals for a Week 3 divisional clash. He caught four of a team-high nine targets for just 27 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to the Patriots. Metcalf finished fifth in yardage despite tying Germie Bernard and Pat Freiermuth for second in receptions, and he now has an 8-67-0 receiving line on 19 targets through two outings. Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers offense have been underwhelming to begin the season, and they'll face a Cincinnati defense allowing 25.0 fantasy points per game (9th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: DK Metcalf and the Steelers visit the Browns for an AFC North clash between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He caught three of five targets for 31 yards and his first TD of the season during Pittsburgh's 30-27 victory in Week 3. Metcalf has an 11-98-1 receiving line on 24 targets through three contests, as he and Aaron Rodgers have had a hard time connecting in their second season together. With that being said, it'll be difficult to trust Metcalf until the duo is on the same page, even against a beatable Cleveland secondary allowing 36.7 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 26th.

player.seasonOutlook: Metcalf returns for Year 2 in Pittsburgh after a solid but unspectacular debut season. The ex-Seahawk missed two games and finished outside the top 20 receivers in targets, catches and yardage (career-low 850), but still did just enough to produce a 21st-place finish in fantasy PPG (his fifth top-25 in his last six seasons). Metcalf soaked up 11 end zone targets and is up to 107 for his career, which leads the NFL since his debut in 2019. The 28-year-old has added target competition this season in the form of Michael Pittman Jr. and rookie Germie Bernard, so while he'll certainly remain busy, a slight dip in usage is probable. Metcalf should be valued as a back-end WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rome Odunze will seek to do more as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Odunze was unable to capitalize on the highest-scoring Week 1 game ever, as he finished the game with two catches for 52 yards. The third-year receiver still figures to be a top target for Caleb Williams moving forward, especially in closer matchups where a consistent option is needed. Odunze will face a Minnesota defense that ceded the second-most PPR points to WRs (55.2) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rome Odunze will look to remain a top look in Chicago's passing offense in Week 3 against the Eagles. Odunze caught three of four targets for 43 yards against the Vikings in Week 2, and he now sits at a 5-95-0 receiving line across two games. The third-year pass catcher's unimpressive output could continue, given that Tyson Bagent is slotted to start under center in place of Caleb Williams (hamstring). Odunze will face a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rome Odunze will look to improve on modest production as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Odunze reeled in three of six targets for 44 yards against the Eagles in Week 3, adding to his already disappointing start to the season. The third-year wide receiver has been consistent, recording three or fewer catches for 52 or fewer yards in each of Chicago's first three games. Odunze will face a Jets squad that has allowed the fourth-fewest receiving yards (337) to WRs so far this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Odunze opened the 2025 season with a bang, scoring five touchdowns in his first four games and producing 15-plus fantasy points in each game. Things fell apart from there, as the 2024 first-round pick went on to deliver one touchdown and two double-digit fantasy outings over his next eight games prior to missing Weeks 14 through 18 due to injury. On the plus side, Odunze remained heavily targeted throughout the season, especially near the goal line, and he is ninth in the NFL with 24 end zone targets since he was drafted. On the other hand, his connection with Caleb Williams needs work, as his 48% catch rate ranked near the basement at the position. Odunze, 24, is still ascending and has a clearer path to targets with DJ Moore out of the mix. He's a candidate for a Year 3 leap and should be valued as a WR3 with upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Golden should remain a top look in Green Bay's passing offense in Week 2 against the Jets. Golden led the Packers in routes (40) and targets (12) in Week 1 against Minnesota, and he converted six catches for 95 yards. He already looks to have a big enough role for a second-year jump, and the pass-heavy nature of Green Bay's offense helps his case even more. He'll face a Jets secondary that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Golden will remain a top option for Jordan Love as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Golden led Green Bay in receiving yards against the Jets in Week 2, catching four of six targets for 58 yards. The second-year wide receiver is also now set to take on a larger role, at least in the short term, with Jayden Reed looking to miss some time with a neck injury.  Golden will look to expand on his 10-153-0 receiving line against an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matthew Golden will aim to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Golden led Green Bay in receiving yards and targets in Week 3 against the Falcons, catching five of 12 targets for 100 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wide receiver is in the middle of a breakout season, outpacing more than half of his 2025 output in just the first three games of this year. He'll take on a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-ten 25.4 fantasy points per game to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Golden is eyeing a Year 2 leap following a disappointing rookie season in which he was limited to 39 touches and failed to find the end zone in 14 regular-season games. Golden was limited to 53% of the snaps and never cleared six targets in a single outing. Some optimism was generated from Golden's 4-84-1 receiving line in the playoff loss to Chicago, but even with Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks gone, it's unclear if he will actually see a big boost in usage in Matt LaFleur's offense considering that no Green Bay receiver has cleared a 21% target share since Davante Adams' departure prior to 2022. The speedy Golden, who also contributes as a rusher, is a recent first-round pick entering his second season. He's worth a speculative middle-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drake Maye will hope to clean up mistakes when the Patriots host the Steelers in Week 2. Maye threw three interceptions in the season opener while under constant pressure, and Pittsburgh's defense, led by T.J. Watt, recorded four sacks last week. While the chemistry was still developing, Maye is now also without No. 1 WR A.J. Brown (ankle) for the immediate future, leading to questionable receiving options. While Maye remains a dangerous runner that will keep his floor reasonable, this likely low-scoring game may not be ideal for a true bounce-back performance.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drake Maye will look to get on track when the Patriots face the Jaguars in Week 3. He is averaging just 183 passing yards through two weeks, with only one touchdown pass and four interceptions. Maye was picked off just eight times all last season. Opponents seem to be pressuring Maye, though Jacksonville is middling at getting after the passer. However, they've allowed only two touchdown passes while limiting quarterbacks to 44 rushing yards. With A.J. Brown still sidelined, Maye will be challenged to exhibit his 2025 form.
outlooksByWeek.4: Drake Maye's confidence appears shaken in the face of pressure ahead of the Patriots' Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Maye has a 1:6 TD:INT ratio through three games, completing just 14 passes in each of his last two games while posting a season-high of 208 yards in Week 2. While he remains dangerous with his legs, he's been held to 18 yards or fewer in Weeks 2 and 3. Buffalo's defense is allowing the seventh-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks, giving up seven touchdowns with just one interception. The game could be high-scoring or at least force the Patriots to try and match points, but Maye didn't throw a touchdown pass against this unit a year ago.

player.seasonOutlook: Maye is entering his third NFL season and second full season as New England's starter. The 2024 No. 3 draft pick is fresh off a breakout 2025 campaign in which he finished in the top five among quarterbacks in pass completions, yards and TDs, as well as rush attempts and yards. Maye, who led the league in completion percentage (72%) and yards per attempt (8.9), trailed only Josh Allen in fantasy points (351.9), fantasy points per game (20.7) and top-10 fantasy weeks (10). The NFL MVP runner-up will need to overcome a tougher schedule, but he has a better supporting cast (including A.J. Brown) and the 24-year-old's combination of passing talent and rushing ability have him well positioned for another top-five fantasy campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Shough will lead the Saints' offense into a tough Week 2 matchup against the Ravens, whose defense gave up just 12.7 fantasy points to quarterbacks in Week 1. Despite a poor first half, Shough threw for 410 yards and three touchdowns in last week's overtime loss, making him the league's leading passer. However, Shough was prone to turnovers, throwing two interceptions and losing a fumble, which is something Baltimore could capitalize on. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup, as the Ravens allowed just 166 passing yards in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Shough will lead the Saints' offense into a Week 3 matchup against the Raiders, whose defense has allowed just 17.4 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season. Shough has been one of the NFL's most productive QBs through two weeks, leading the league in passing yards (662) while producing five total touchdowns. Despite throwing the ball 90 times in his first two contests, Shough remains one of the league leaders in completion percentage (68.9 percent). He's in for a difficult Week 3 matchup, however, with the Raiders' allowing just one passing touchdowns this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Shough is expected lead the Saints' offense into a Week 4 matchup against the Falcons, whose defense allowed just 14 points to the Packers in Week 3. Shough continued his stretch of impressive play in the Week 3 loss to the Raiders, throwing for 255 yards, four touchdowns and an interception. Head coach Kellen Moore continues to put his faith in Shough, as the Saints' are throwing the ball 44 times per game through three weeks. Expect Shough to remain one of fantasy's best quarterbacks in Week 4 against a Falcons defense that's given up 21.6 fantasy points per game to the position this year.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the surprise second-half breakout players of 2025, Shough scored 17-plus fantasy points in seven of his nine full games, including six straight to end the season. The 2025 second-round pick was a solid producer with his arm (250.1 passing yards per game) and his legs (19.3 rushing yards per game and three TDs). Shough didn't show a high ceiling (he never reached 22 fantasy points in a game), though that can be traced to a shaky supporting cast. That's an area that should be better in 2026 with Travis Etienne Jr. and No. 8 overall pick Jordyn Tyson (once healthy) joining the team. He's still unproven, but Shough enters Year 2 (same as coach Kellen Moore) as an intriguing fantasy breakout candidate. He's worth a look in the later rounds.

The Texans led the league with 13 weeks as a top-10 scoring defense, allowed the fewest yards and second-fewest points and totaled the third-most interceptions and seventh-most sacks, last season. Edge rushers Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter and cornerback Derek Stingley were among five Pro Bowlers from their roster, which largely returns the same personnel for 2026. The Texans make a compelling case to be the first D/ST picked, with one caveat: Their tricky September schedule includes the Bills (Week 1), Bengals (2) and Cowboys (4) and will probably demand fantasy managers seek fill-ins for those matchups.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Coker (ankle) will look to continue shining in Carolina's Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Coker has shown out in the Panthers last two games (including their wild-card loss to end last season), having recorded a combined 17 receptions for 272 yards and three touchdowns. He's outproduced 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year Tetairoa McMillan and looks to be a major part of Carolina's offense going forward. However, Coker is dealing with an ankle issue and could struggle against a tough Falcons defense that gave up just 5.0 yards per pass attempt in Week 1, the fourth-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of Bryce Young's favorite targets in Carolina's Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Coker has been incredibly productive, leading the Panthers in receptions (16) and yards (204) while being tied for first in targets (18) through two weeks. Across his last three games (including playoffs), the third-year pro has caught 25 of 30 targets for 338 yards and two touchdowns, emerging as one of the NFL's top young wideouts. He's in for a very favorable matchup in Week 3 as well, as the Browns' defense has surrendered 7.2 yards per pass attempt this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jalen Coker (quadriceps) is expected to operate as one of the Panthers' top targets if active for the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Coker has dealt with three separate injuries through three weeks this season (ankle, hamstring and quadriceps). Despite this, the third-year wideout has amassed 222 receiving yards and two touchdowns on 18 catches, leading the Panthers in yards and touchdowns. If Coker is able to suit up in Week 4, he's in for an incredibly favorable matchup, as Detroit's defense has allowed a whopping 31.7 points and 39.0 PPR fantasy points per game to the WR position this season.

player.seasonOutlook: After missing nearly the entire first half of 2025, Coker passed Xavier Legette and took on a larger offensive role opposite Tetairoa McMillan. From Week 8 onward (11 games, including the playoffs), Coker played 73% of the snaps and handled a 17.8% target share. The fantasy output was inconsistent (below 11.5 points in seven games), but he peaked down the stretch (more than 14 points in four of his final six, including a 9-134-1 showing against the Rams in the playoffs). Coker's strong finish is encouraging, though his rookie season went similarly (14-plus points three times, but under 11 in the other nine games). A healthy 2026 could get Coker to the next level, but flex production is his likely ceiling as long as McMillan is commanding one-quarter (if not more) of the targets in Carolina's Bryce Young-led offense.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ka'imi Fairbairn remains locked in as a starting fantasy kicker in Week 2, when the Texans host a Bengals team that allowed the third-most points in the NFL last season. Fairbairn led the league in both made and attempted field goals last season. He was limited to one field-goal attempt in Week 1 as the Texans scored four TDs, but the standout kicker showed off his mix of power and accuracy by converting a go-ahead 58-yard field goal in the fourth quarter, though that ultimately wasn't enough to beat the Bills.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ka'imi Fairbairn had a rare miss on a difficult 58-yard field-goal attempt in Houston's Week 2 loss, but he remains one of the NFL's best kickers after leading the league in both made and attempted field goals last season. Fairbairn is locked in as a high-end fantasy starter for a Week 3 road game against a Colts team that has been the NFL's worst defensively. Indianapolis is allowing 37.0 points and 514.5 yards per game, both league highs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ka'imi Fairbairn is just 4-for-5 on field-goal attempts through three games for the 0-3 Texans. It's a less-than-ideal start for the standout kicker, but Fairbairn remains a hold for fantasy purposes considering the Texans bounced back from a 0-3 start last season while supplying Fairbairn with enough opportunities to lead the league in both field goals made (44) and field goals attempted (48) during the 2025 regular season. He has a golden opportunity to break out in Week 4, as the Texans shouldn't have as much trouble moving the ball against the Cowboys, who are allowing 387.0 yards and 27.3 points per game, both of which are among the league's 10 most generous totals.

outlooksByWeek.2: Stefon Diggs had more than double the targets of teammate Terry McLaurin in Week 1 for Washington. Diggs was targeted a team-high nine times, though managed only four catches. However, he gained 55 yards and also found the end zone, though had a costly celebration penalty on the score that cost Washington a chance to go for two and tie the game late. Still, it was an extremely promising start for Diggs, who will have a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus Dallas. The Cowboys allowed 229 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air to the Giants in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Stefon Diggs has scored three times in two games as a member of the Commanders. Diggs snagged five passes for 47 yards and two touchdowns in Washington's loss to Dallas last week. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Diggs and the rest of the Washington offense, though the newly acquired wideout does seem to have a knack for finding the end zone thus far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Stefon Diggs finished second in targets for the Commanders last game. Diggs caught four balls on seven looks, though managed just 33 yards in the surprising win over Seattle. Diggs was also held out of the end zone for the first time this season. Diggs caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Diggs signed with the Commanders in August after he was released by the Patriots earlier this offseason. Successful in his return from an ACL tear suffered midway through 2024, the veteran receiver's lone season in New England resulted in 85 catches (ninth among wide receivers) and his seventh career 1,000-yard campaign. Diggs paced the position with an incredible 83% catch rate (second highest all time for a receiver with 100-plus targets) and ranked fourth in yards per route run (2.8). Not used much near the goal line, however, Diggs was limited to four touchdowns and finished 23rd in fantasy PPG. He obviously still has something left in the tank, but is now 32 years old and his usage is trending downward. He has a path to a substantial offense role in Washington and can be viewed as a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Wilson will look to break through against a tough Seattle secondary for Arizona in Week 2. Wilson performed well in a season-opening win over the Chargers, catching five of seven targets for 56 yards. He outproduced presumed No. 1 wideout Marvin Harrison, though newcomer Kendrick Bourne led the WR corps with an 8-75-0 line. All three figure to be challenged by a Seahawks defense that ranked 10th in passing yards allowed last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Wilson faces a tough challenge in Arizona's Week 3 matchup in San Francisco. Wilson was quiet against Seattle this past Sunday, catching just two of seven targets for 18 yards. However, he was still the Cardinals' second-leading receiver in a game during which QB Jacoby Brissett threw for just 95 yards. The 49ers have surrendered only 15.6 fantasy points per game to wideouts, the ninth-best mark in the league threw two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Wilson appears to be Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett's favorite wideout target heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Giants. Wilson got a whopping 17 targets this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, recording 11 catches for 89 yards and a touchdown. Meanwhile, Marvin Harrison posted a quiet 3-40-0 line on five targets. Of course, star TE Trey McBride will consistently draw plenty of Brissett's attention, but it looks like Wilson is in line for lots of looks in the team's offense. He could thrive against a Giants defense that is giving up 23.6 fantasy points per game to WRs, ninth-most in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: After averaging 4.3 targets and 7.6 fantasy points per game during his first 38 NFL games, Wilson broke out with Jacoby Brissett under center during the final eight games of 2025, averaging 11.0 targets and 21.2 fantasy PPG. The stretch also coincided with Marvin Harrison Jr. dealing with health issues, and it's worth noting that Wilson's receiving lines in the four games Harrison was active weren't quite as good (3-40-0, 3-61-0, 4-34-0, 3-36-0). A healthy Harrison (along with TE Trey McBride) figures to lead to a return to earth for Wilson, but the 26-year-old did enough late last season to warrant WR4/flex consideration in drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tony Pollard got just eight touches in the season opener as the Titans fell behind against the Jets and abandoned the run. Negative game scripts could be a recurring problem for Pollard, and the Titans will be substantial Week 2 underdogs at home against the Eagles. On the bright side, Pollard recorded at least 1,288 scrimmage yards in each of the previous two seasons, even as the Titans posted a 3-14 record both years. Pollard's status as the team's starting running back keeps him in the Week 2 flex/RB3 conversation.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tony Pollard could be worth plugging into Week 3 fantasy lineups as a high-end RB3/flex option for the Titans' road matchup with a Giants defense that has struggled to contain RBs in the early going. Javonte Williams scored two TDs against the Giants in Week 1, then Kyren Williams and Blake Corum each exceeded 90 scrimmage yards against the Giants in Week 2, with Williams tacking on a TD. Pollard has reprised his role as the 1A option in Tennessee's backfield over Tjyae Spears. The former Cowboys RB has averaged 77 scrimmage yards per game since joining the Titans prior to the 2024 campaign, but Pollard has been limited to 99 yards through two games to begin this season. Negative game scripts are often a problem for the Titans, but Tennessee is likely to stay within striking distance and keep Pollard involved on the ground against a Giants team that's missing starting QB Jaxson Dart (knee).
outlooksByWeek.4: Tony Pollard has increased his yardage total in each of Tennessee's first three games heading into a Week 4 road game against the Ravens, who are allowing 99 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Pollard had just 34 scrimmage yards on eight touches in a lopsided Week 1 loss to the Jets, but he recorded 65 yards on 15 touches in Week 2 and 96 scrimmage yards on 21 touches in Week 3 as the Titans managed to stay within striking distance before falling to the Eagles and Giants, respectively. With second-year QB Cam Ward struggling to move the ball through the air, the Titans will likely try to continue featuring their Pollard-led ground game, though there is a substantial risk of Lamar Jackson and the Ravens pulling away and forcing Tennessee into a more pass-heavy game plan. Given Pollard's status as the lead back in a low-octane offense, he has a decent floor as a flex play but isn't the most exciting Week 4 RB option.

player.seasonOutlook: Pollard has handled a hefty 67.2% of the Titans' designed rushing attempts since his arrival two seasons ago (15.2 per game) and, even with solid efficiency, he has finished 22nd and 30th in fantasy points per game. The culprits? Tennessee's struggling offense (Pollard has exactly five TDs in both seasons) and a limited receiving role when Tyjae Spears has been healthy (Pollard's targets fell from 3.5 per game in 2024 to 2.5 per game in 2025). Barring a major leap from quarterback Cam Ward, Pollard is unlikely to deliver only the second top-20 fantasy campaign (in points per game) of his career. The 29-year-old, entering his eighth NFL season (third with Tennessee), is a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Carnell Tate tied for the team lead in receiving yards during his NFL debut, but he had just 38 yards on six targets as Titans QB Cam Ward threw for a meager 140 yards. Tennessee's passing game is likely to struggle again in Week 2 against Philadelphia's excellent secondary, led by cornerback Quinyon Mitchell. Tate is likely to maintain a prominent role on the rebuilding Titans after being drafted fourth overall out of Ohio State, but the rookie WR is hard to trust as anything more than a fantasy WR3 or flex play until Tennessee's offense shows some life.
outlooksByWeek.3: Carnell Tate is off to an uninspiring start, with seven catches for 65 yards on 11 targets through two games with the Titans. A Week 3 road game against the injury-riddled Giants presents a nice opportunity for the rookie fourth overall pick out of Ohio State to break out, as the Giants just allowed 195 receiving yards and two TDs to Rams WR Davante Adams. Tate leads his team in targets through two games, but the Titans have struggled to move the ball through the air. Given Tate's draft pedigree and matchup, he's a high-ceiling fantasy WR3 for Week 3, though it's fair for fantasy managers to be hesitant given the highly touted rookie's lackluster production so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Carnell Tate has 20 targets through three games heading into the Titans' Week 4 road game against the Ravens, turning that decent volume into a pedestrian 13 catches for 123 yards, averaging 41 yards per game. Tennessee's entire passing game is tough to trust given the struggles of QB Cam Ward, but Tate has the most upside among the team's pass catchers. A Week 4 breakout is possible against a Ravens defense that has given up the second-most catches to WRs, especially if the Titans fall behind and are forced to air it out, but Tate can't be trusted as anything more than a flex option until Ward shows signs of progress.

player.seasonOutlook: Tate was selected by the Titans with the fourth overall pick of April's draft. He didn't see a ton of volume at Ohio State, but he was efficient, averaging 13.1 yards per target (first in this rookie WR class) and 3.06 yards per route run (third) in 2025. He also paced the class in YPT for his career (11.6) and caught an impressive 75% of his targets during the 39-game span. Tate underwhelmed in the 40-yard dash at the combine (4.53 at 192 pounds), but he measured in with big hands and a large wingspan. Wide receivers selected in the top 10 handle, on average, one-quarter of their team's targets and generally deliver WR2/3 fantasy production. Cam Ward's development will be key here, but Tate's combination of talent and projected target volume is enough to make him an appealing WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tucker Kraft should continue to have a big role in Green Bay's offense as they face the Jets in Week 2. Kraft reeled in three of six targets for 65 yards against the Vikings in Week 1, but he was definitely a huge focus of their defensive scheme. The star tight end will luckily face a New York defense that should be less menacing this Sunday, as they ceded a lower-half 15.4 PPR points per game to tight ends in the 2025 campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tucker Kraft will look to get more involved as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Kraft was held to just two catches for 15 yards in Week 2, but Green Bay's passing attack was lacking for most of the game. The bruising tight end will seek to re-establish himself as a top outlet for quarterback Jordan Love. Luckily, an Atlanta defense that's allowed 20.7 PPR points per game to tight ends so far this season, 29th in the league, could be a great place to start.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tucker Kraft will seek to bounce back as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Kraft brought in four of eight targets for 26 yards against the Falcons in Week 3, with some drops that are usually caught. The fourth-year tight end has now posted a 9-106-0 receiving line on 17 targets across the first three games of the season, which is underwhelming considering his start to last year. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's been tough on all but tight ends, allowing a bottom-10 183 receiving yards to the position this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Kraft's steady career progression had him on the cusp of a full-on breakout last season, but all was derailed by a torn ACL in Week 9. Prior to the injury, Kraft had seen 10 targets in consecutive games, one of which included a career-high 33.3 fantasy points. Through Week 8, only Jake Ferguson had more fantasy points. Granted, Kraft took advantage of a super easy schedule and was way over his head in the TD department (six TDs with an expected total of 1.8 and only two end zone targets), but his boost in usage and terrific RAC skills (he has led the position in the category each of his three seasons) were enough to get him into the weekly TE1 mix. Kraft's recovery will need to be monitored, but even if he's ready for Week 1, a dip in production is possible in his first year back from the major injury. He's a risky middle-round target.

This already highly regarded defense only got stronger in June with the acquisition of two-time Defensive Player of the Year (2023, 2025) Myles Garrett. He wasn't their only addition, as CBs Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson were brought in from the Chiefs. Expect another productive season from this unit, though it does face one of the tougher early-season schedules, with the 49ers (Week 1), Broncos (3), Eagles (4) and Bills (5) among their first five opponents. The Rams' second-half schedule is one of the easiest, meaning they might be a better in-season trade target than a draft-day pickup.

outlooksByWeek.2: Deebo Samuel will look to build upon a strong season-opening performance when the 49ers face Miami in Week 2. In Samuel's return to San Francisco following a one-year hiatus, he caught six of seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in last Thursday's win over the Rams. Samuel and Mike Evans finished with nearly identical receiving lines, suggesting that both veteran wideouts can thrive with QB Brock Purdy. The Dolphins were beat handily by the Raiders in Week 1 while giving up three TDs through the air (though two were to RB Ashton Jeanty).
outlooksByWeek.3: Deebo Samuel is coming off a quiet game heading into San Francisco's Week 3 matchup against the Cardinals. Samuel caught three passes for 31 yards and rushed once for four yards in Sunday's rout of Miami. However, fellow wideouts Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Mike Evans (hip) both exited that contest due to injury, and though early reports suggest Evans should be fine for Week 3, Samuel could see more looks come his way given his comparatively good health. Arizona has given up the sixth-most fantasy points per game to wideouts so far this year and was just torched by Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-155-3 receiving line) on Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Deebo Samuel could take on the 49ers' No. 1 WR role in Week 4 against Denver if Mike Evans (ribs/oblique) is unable to play. Though Evans left in the second quarter in this past Sunday's win over Arizona, Samuel ended the contest without seeing a target. However, he still had a good fantasy line thanks to an 80-yard TD on a hook-and-ladder play, and Samuel also gained 14 yards on two carries. Should Evans be unable to suit up against Denver, Samuel could face the daunting task of trying to beat star cornerback Patrick Surtain.

player.seasonOutlook: Samuel reunited with the 49ers in July after solid yet unspectacular lone season in Washington. The former second-round pick cleared 85 touches and 800 scrimmage yards for the fifth consecutive season and finished 25th among receivers in fantasy points -- his third-career top-30 fantasy campaign. Samuel's role as a short-area target and occasional rusher gets the ball in his hands plenty (he's ranked in the top 15 among WRs in touches and RAC five years in a row), but it doesn't allow him much scoring upside (10 TDs over the last two years, and he's never cleared five end zone targets in one season). Now 30 years old, Samuel figures to resume his role as a short-area playmaker in Kyle Shanahan's highly-efficient offense. He's a fine late-round flier with WR3/flex upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bryce Young will look to stay hot in the Panthers' Week 2 matchup against the Falcons, whose defense allowed just 14.8 fantasy points to quarterbacks in Week 1. Despite Carolina's defensive struggles, Young threw for 361 yards, the third-most in the NFL during Week 1, and led the offense to 37 points. Additionally, he added a touchdown on the ground as the Panthers offense looked more aggressive than in 2025. Young is also in for a favorable matchup, as he threw for 569 yards and accounted for four total touchdowns in two games versus the Falcons in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bryce Young will look to stay hot in the Panthers' Week 3 matchup against the Browns, whose defense has surrendered 22.1 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season. Young has been one of the most productive QBs in the NFL through two weeks, as he's tied for the most touchdown passes in the league (six) while ranking second in passing yards (648). He's also threatened defenses with his legs, adding 16 yards and a score on the ground. Young could very well finish as one of fantasy's top quarterbacks again in Week 3 while playing a Browns defense that's allowed five touchdown passes this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bryce Young is expected to lead the Panthers' offense into a Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Despite a Week 3 loss, Young remained productive, throwing for 291 yards, one touchdown and an interception. Through three weeks, the Alabama product has accounted for eight total touchdowns and two turnovers while leading Carolina's offense to 29.7 points per game. He's dealing with injuries to Jalen Coker (quad) and Xavier Legette (knee), which could result in the Panthers leaning more on the ground game in Week 4. Regardless, Young should be in for a favorable matchup against a Lions defense that's given up the most fantasy points per game to opposing QBs (35.3) this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Young has yet to find his way to any sort of fantasy relevance during his first three NFL seasons. The 2023 No. 1 draft pick has yet to finish a season better than 20th in passing yards, 10th in rushing yards or 24th in fantasy points per game. Efficiency has been a problem, as last season's career-high 6.3 yards per attempt was barely up from 2024 and still among the worst in the NFL. Young's 47.6 QBR last season ranked 22nd among 28 qualified quarterbacks. Perhaps the 25-year-old will make a leap in top target Tetairoa McMillan's second season and Brad Idzik's debut as the offensive playcaller, but it will be asking a lot to expect QB1 production. Young is best viewed as a fringe QB2 in 12-team leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Downs is hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league flex for the Colts' Week 2 trip to Kansas City. His four targets in the Week 1 loss to Baltimore tied for fourth on the team with Jonathan Taylor, as Daniel Jones threw more frequently to Alec Pierce, Keenan Allen and Tyler Warren. In 17 appearances since the start of last season, Downs is averaging a pedestrian 35.5 receiving yards per game in the Colts' run-heavy offense.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Downs is poised to work as the Colts' top wide receiver in Week 3 against the Texans, making him a solid WR3 or flex option in fantasy. Alec Pierce (heel) is expected to sit out, and the Colts lack viable alternatives, with over-the-hill veteran Keenan Allen and recent signing Darius Slayton representing the top options behind Downs in the wide receiver room. Downs caught seven of nine targets for 72 yards to lead the Colts in all three categories during the Week 2 loss to the Chiefs, which Pierce exited in the first half. Downs figures to see plenty of star Texans CB Derek Stingley, but the 25-year-old WR should get plenty of targets from Daniel Jones despite the tricky matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Josh Downs has exceeded 70 receiving yards in each of the Colts' last two games while racking up 20 targets over that span. With fellow Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) on IR, Downs is a recommended Week 4 starting option since he is poised to see plenty of targets from Daniel Jones against a weak Washington secondary that has allowed the most catches (46) and touchdown receptions (six) to WRs, as well as the third-most receiving yards (573) to the position. Downs, TE Tyler Warren, and WR Keenan Allen accounted for 20 of Jones' 24 completed passes in Pierce's absence against the Texans in Week 3.

player.seasonOutlook: Downs has settled in as a serviceable slot receiver, which has helped him to finish in the 35-to-45 range among WRs in total fantasy points in each of his three NFL seasons. Downs peaked with a 72-803-5 receiving line in 2024, but took a step back in a crowded offense last season, and failed to deliver a single fantasy week better than 15th at the position. The undersized Downs isn't an option near the goal line, as he hasn't cleared five touchdowns or three end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old has a path to a slightly larger role in 2026 with Michael Pittman Jr. gone, leaving Alec Pierce, Tyler Warren and Keenan Allen as his primary target competition. Downs is a sleeper for flex production in PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Addison will look to record his first reception of the year as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Addison ran the second-most routes for Minnesota in Week 1 against the Packers, but he was unable to convert on either of his two targets. Veteran quarterback Carson Wentz, who filled in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion), relied more on tight ends T.J. Hockenson and Josh Oliver behind Justin Jefferson. This could make Addison's role remains small as long as Wentz remains under center. With that being said, the Bears' defense did allow the fourth-most PPR points to wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1, which could open up Minnesota's passing game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Addison will seek to ramp things up as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Addison bounced back from a zero-catch performance in Week 1 this past Sunday, logging two catches for 21 yards against the Bears. Still, his output is nowhere near sufficient for fantasy owners, especially since he's put up WR2 numbers many times throughout the last three seasons. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed 24.9 PPR points per game against wide receivers this season, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Addison will look to build off a big game as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Addison saw an uptick in looks after the departure of Justin Jefferson (ankle) in Week 3, finishing the win with five catches for 90 yards and a touchdown on nine targets. While Jefferson very well could return to the field in the coming week, Addison did prove to be a solid option for Kyler Murray. Addison has proven to be an asset for Minnesota alongside Jefferson when being thrown to by a competent quarterback, which could be showcased even against a Miami defense that's ranked top-five (24.2 fantasy points per game) against WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: After impressing with a 70-911-10 receiving line on 108 targets as a rookie in 2023, Addison has seen his target, reception, yardage and touchdown totals decrease each of the last two seasons. A few missed games were partially to blame for the dips, but Minnesota's quarterback woes were the main culprit in 2025, as Addison went from 10 TDs and a 65% catch rate in both 2023 and 2024 to three TDs and a 53% catch rate last season. Addison already has a pair of top-25 fantasy campaigns to his name, but it may be a stretch for him to get there in 2026 with Kyler Murray leading the Minnesota offense, not to mention Jauan Jennings' addition to the lineup. The 24-year-old is best valued as WR4/flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jayden Daniels overcame a slow start to nearly lead the Commanders to a comeback win against the Eagles in Week 1. Daniels finished the contest with 164 yards passing and two touchdowns, along with an additional 31 yards rushing for the game. Daniels will look to build some momentum in Week 2 versus an extremely suspect Dallas Cowboys defense. Dallas allowed the most yards in the NFL last season, and the supposedly revamped defense was trounced by the Giants in their 2026 opener. The Cowboys allowed 394 scrimmage yards and four total touchdowns in an ugly 28-20 loss to Jaxson Dart and company.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jayden Daniels dislocated his elbow against the Cowboys in Week 2, the same elbow he injured last year for the Commanders. While the elbow is not fractured, Daniels is almost certain to miss Week 3 vs. the Seahawks. Veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start versus a devastating Seattle defense that is allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jayden Daniels is set to practice with the Commanders as the squad heads to London for Week 4.  Daniels is unlikely to play versus the Colts due to his dislocated elbow, though, and especially since backup Marcus Mariota just led an improbable victory over the defending Super Bowl champions. Mariota tossed three touchdowns in the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. Whoever lines up under center in Week 4 will have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Colts pass defense. Indianapolis is allowing 276 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Daniels is looking to bounce back after appearing in only seven games due to injury last season. The 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year began his career with a bang, tossing 25 touchdowns and adding 891 yards and six scores with his legs in his first season. He wasn't quite as dominant when healthy last season (16.3 points per game, compared to 20.9 in 2024), but he remained a major factor with his legs (58-278-2 in seven games, three of which were partial appearances). Daniels' supporting cast is underwhelming and he'll be working with a new playcaller (David Blough), but the dual-threat ability supplies the 25-year-old with elite upside. He's a strong QB1 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jadarian Price is set for his second NFL start when Seattle travels to Arizona in Week 2. Price was efficient in his professional debut last Wednesday versus New England, rushing 10 times for 52 yards while catching both of his targets for six yards. George Holani was given eight carries in the win, which helped limit Price's workload. The split between the two going forward remains to be seen, but there's certainly a chance that Price's touches will increase as the season progresses. The Cardinals' run defense looked good against the Chargers in Week 1, holding Omarion Hampton to 43 yards on 12 carries.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jadarian Price injured his shoulder in the Seahawks' Week 2 win over Arizona, and it's unclear if he'll be able to play in Week 3 against Washington. The rookie RB was injured in the fourth quarter versus the Cardinals and finished the game with 13 carries for 52 yards and one catch for eight yards. Should Price not be able to play in Week 3, Emanuel Wilson would be he lead candidate to take over as the Seahawks starting RB. The Commanders have been awful against the pass but decent against the run this season and are yielding just 3.79 YPC against running backs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jadarian Price heads into Seattle's Week 4 matchup against the Chargers with potentially a lot on the line. After fumbling early in Sunday's Week 3 win over the Commanders, the rookie ended up logging just five totes for 15 yards while adding one catch for seven yards. Meanwhile, Emanuel Wilson (nine carries) and George Holani (three carries and five catches) each out-touched Price, casting uncertainty about the Seahawks' backfield plans moving forward. Price would benefit from a productive (and fumble-free) performance against the Chargers, who rank 19th in the league in giving up 17.2 fantasy points per game through three weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Price was selected by the Seahawks with the No. 32 overall pick of April's draft. Price managed only 280 career carries while stuck behind Jeremiyah Love at Notre Dame, but he showed well, posting a 4.13 YAC (second best in this rookie class) and 3.6 forced missed tackle rate (third best). He wasn't a factor as a receiver, however, totaling 15 receptions in 41 games. Price has a path to an immediate feature role in Seattle's run-first offense, though he may eventually defer substantial work to Zach Charbonnet (ACL recovery). Value Price as a flex, though he should land on the weekly RB2 radar while Charbonnet is sidelined.

outlooksByWeek.2: Courtland Sutton was held in check along with the rest of the Broncos' offense in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, catching two of five targets for just 11 yards. Quarterback Bo Nix couldn't connect with either of his top two wideouts, as Jaylen Waddle also had a poor showing in his Denver debut, and new offensive coordinator Davis Webb may need to go back to the drawing board quickly to get his passing game going. Sutton should face a softer matchup in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Courtland Sutton has had a slow start to the season as the focus of the Broncos' passing game has shifted to Jaylen Waddle. Through two games, Sutton has posted only nine targets, catching five for a meager 36 yards. He still has plenty of existing chemistry with quarterback Bo Nix, and the duo could rekindle it once defenses begin shifting more attention to Waddle, but Sutton figures to be hard-pressed to reach 1,000 receiving yards in 2026 for a third straight season. He'll take on a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, though three of them have gone for touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Courtland Sutton continues to fade into a support role in the Broncos' passing game following the acquisition of Jaylen Waddle. His seven targets in a Week 3 win over the Rams were a season-high, and through three games, he's managed just an 8-82-0 line on 16 total looks from Bo Nix. Sutton should see more volume once new play-caller Davis Webb settles in, but he'll have an uphill battle to produce his fourth career 1,000-yard season. He'll face a 49ers secondary in Week 4 that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: After producing one season with 1,000 yards and a top-20 fantasy finish during his first six NFL campaigns, Sutton has achieved both in each of the past two years. The 2018 second-round pick's target share actually dipped from 24% in 2024 to 21% in 2025, but he remained heavily involved near the goal line and has now ranked in the top 12 among receivers in TDs each of the last three seasons. In fact, Sutton has now finished in the top 10 at the position in end zone targets four years in a row, tying for third with 56 during the span. Sutton will remain one of Bo Nix's go-to targets, but now 30 years old and with added target competition in Jaylen Waddle, he's best valued as a fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jared Goff will look to build off a season-opener win as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2.
