Goff's performance and Detroit's overall in Week 1 weren't pretty, but he got the job done, finishing with 206 passing yards and two touchdowns. The game also showed that the Lions will continue to have a high-volume air attack, as the veteran ended with 39 pass attempts. Goff will now turn his focus to a Bills defense that ceded 274 passing yards and two touchdowns to C.J. Stroud in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jared Goff will look to keep his high production rolling as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. Goff benefited from playing from behind in Week 2 at Buffalo, racking up 327 passing yards and four touchdowns on a 68.4 percent completion rate. The veteran quarterback has now totaled 533 passing yards with a 6:0 TD:INT across his first two games, and Detroit's lacking defense has only helped his output so far. Goff will take on a Jets defense that's allowed a top-10 fantasy points per game (14.2) to quarterbacks in the first two games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jared Goff will continue to benefit from a high-powered offense as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. Goff kept it rolling in Week 3, throwing for 269 yards with two touchdowns and zero interceptions. The veteran quarterback has completed 70.6 percent of his passes for 802 yards and eight touchdowns with no interceptions across three games. He'll face a Carolina defense that's allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per game (23.5) to QBs so far this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Goff is entering his 10th NFL season, including his sixth with the Lions. The 2016 No. 1 draft pick has been extremely successful through the air over the past three seasons (4,500-plus yards and 30-plus touchdowns in all three), which has helped him to fantasy finishes of seventh, sixth and ninth. Of course, there's some survivorship bias here, as Goff's per-game finishes during the span are 15th, seventh and 12th. The reason for the limited fantasy output is a lack of rushing, as Goff has never cleared 108 rushing yards in a season and was held to 45 yards in 2025. Playing at his absolute ceiling as a passer and still no more than a fringe QB1, the 31-year-old is just a solid backup/occasional streaming option in fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Jacobs is unlikely to play in the Packers' Week 3 matchup against the Falcons. Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List at this point in the season, with no current indications of when he'll be back in action. A committee of MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson will continue to provide Green Bay's rushing attack while the veteran is absent.

player.seasonOutlook: Jacobs' 2025 season can be split in two parts: pre-injury and post-injury. While healthy during his first nine games, Jacobs picked up where he left off from a terrific 2024 debut season with Green Bay, averaging 21.1 touches and 19.6 fantasy points while scoring 11 TDs. After missing all but 11 snaps during Weeks 11 and 12, Jacobs returned and wasn't quite the same, averaging 14.6 touches and 11.3 points while totaling three touchdowns in his final five games. But Jacobs, 28, was still effective overall (PFF's fourth-highest-graded back) and has a clear grasp on lead-back duties in a good Green Bay offense that has afforded him 30 touchdowns (fifth most in the NFL) in 32 games. He's a fine back-end RB1 when active, but a likely suspension makes him less valuable on draft day.He's worth a mid-round flier until the dust settles.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Little got off to an accurate start by converting both of his field-goal attempts and all four extra points in Jacksonville's Week 1 win. He made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season, so there are no concerns about his leg strength. Getting into scoring range will be tougher than usual for the Jaguars in Week 2 against a Broncos defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the league last season, though 70 yards could be within Little's realistic range in the thin Denver air. Little's upside is high enough to maintain fantasy starter status, even given the tricky Week 2 matchup for Jacksonville's offense.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Little had a rare miss in Week 2 but has been one of the NFL's best kickers since entering the league in 2024. Through 36 games with the Jaguars, he has converted 61 of 68 field-goal attempts, including an NFL-record 68-yard field goal. He's a little riskier than usual in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that's allowing just 8.0 points per game, but Little is probably too good to bench regardless of the opponent.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Little narrowly missed setting an NFL record in Jacksonville's Week 3 win over the Patriots, as his 70-yard field-goal attempt squeaked just wide right. Little already holds the record for the longest made field goal in a regular-season game with a 68-yarder last season, but the powerful kicker has converted just 4-of-6 field-goal attempts in 2026 while having hit all 10 of his PAT tries. Despite Little's pedestrian start, his impressive range coupled with Jacksonville's ability to move the ball effectively give Little starter-level upside each game, and a Week 4 road matchup against a Bengals team that's allowing 21.0 points per game is no exception.

outlooksByWeek.2: Harrison Butker was perfect in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, connecting on all four of his extra points and converting his only field-goal attempt from 28 yards. The offense looked more potent with a healthy Patrick Mahomes under center, Kenneth Walker as the new bell-cow back, and a returning Eric Bieniemy as offensive coordinator, and Butker should see his opportunities rise if that trend holds. He could be busy in Week 2 against a Colts team that just got routed by the Ravens and was tied for 20th in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Harrison Butker missed a 51-yard field-goal attempt in the second quarter of Week 2, but he made up for it by converting the rest of his opportunities, including a 40-yard FG that gave Kansas City the overtime win over the Colts. The veteran kicker has been busy in the early going with six FG attempts and seven PATs, and a resurgent offense led by a healthy Patrick Mahomes and new bell-cow back Kenneth Walker should continue to supply Butker with volume. He'll face a Dolphins team in Week 3 that's giving up 31.0 points a game in the early going.
outlooksByWeek.4: Harrison Butker missed a field goal for a second straight game in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins. A resurgent offense under a healthy Patrick Mahomes has given the veteran kicker a solid floor in terms of PATs, and he's a perfect 10-for-10 to begin the year with at least three in each contest. Butker's two FG misses have also been from 50-plus yards, and he's a perfect 8-for-8 from shorter distances. He may not be able to squander any chances in Week 4 against a Raiders team that's allowed 18.0 points a game, seventh in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mark Andrews and the Ravens host the Saints and their defense, which ranks 13th in fantasy points allowed per game (11.3) to TEs, in Week 2. Andrews caught four of his six targets for 49 yards during Baltimore's 41-23 win in the season opener. He tied with Zay Flowers (hamstring) for the team lead in targets and finished second behind him in receptions. With Flowers and a host of other receivers dealing with injuries, Andrews could be in line for additional looks as a safety net for Lamar Jackson.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mark Andrews and the Ravens look to rebound from an upset defeat when they visit the Cowboys in Week 3. He caught six of seven targets for 49 yards during Baltimore's 24-17 Week 2 loss, making it two straight outings with exactly 49 receiving yards for the 31-year-old. Andrews draws a favorable matchup versus a Dallas defense that surrendered eight receptions for 78 yards and two TDs to Isaiah Likely in the season opener. The Cowboys rank 26th in fantasy points allowed (16.9) and are one of two teams with a catch rate of 100% to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mark Andrews and the Ravens welcome the 0-3 Titans to town for a Week 4 showdown. After missing some time with a hand injury during Baltimore's 34-31 Week 3 win, Andrews returned and ultimately finished with three catches for 24 yards on five targets. He's still in search of his first TD of 2026, but he's been consistently involved on offense, totaling 18 targets across three contests. Andrews could find it difficult to break through in the scoring department against the Titans' third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (7.4) to TEs, as they're one of nine teams yet to surrender a receiving touchdown to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: One of fantasy's biggest mysteries, Andrews' usage has dipped substantially over the past two seasons. After finishing in the top five in fantasy PPG five seasons in a row from 2019 to 2023, Andrews slipped to eighth in 2024 (it would've been much worse if not for 11 touchdowns on 68 targets) and fell even further to 24th last season. Andrews appeared in all 17 of Baltimore's games but ranked 18th among tight ends in targets and outside the top 20 in catches and yards. The combination of a new coaching staff, a healthy Lamar Jackson and the departure of Isaiah Likely could lead to a rebound season for Andrews, but we now have two straight seasons of underperformance. The 31-year-old remains a force near the goal line (top 10 in end zone targets seven years in a row), but he's now more of a fringe TE1 than a fantasy star.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cameron Dicker didn't get many chances to hit the scoreboard in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, converting both his extra points but failing to see a field-goal attempt. The team's offense didn't quite look in sync yet under new coordinator Mike McDaniel, and top wideout Ladd McConkey was knocked out of the game early with a rib injury, so scoring drives could be tough to come by for the club in the short term. Dicker will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Raiders team that finished 25th in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cameron Dicker has had a rough start to the season as the Chargers adjust to a new offensive scheme under Mike McDaniel. The fifth-year kicker has converted all four of his PATs through two games, but his only field-goal attempt so far came from 58 yards out, and he clanked it off the upright. Better days should be ahead for Dicker and the offense, but his streak of seasons with 40-plus FG attempts could be about to come to an abrupt end. Dicker could be a little busier in Week 3 against a Bills team that's allowed 31.0 points a game in the early going, tied for the third-worst total in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cameron Dicker has had a shaky start to the season as the Chargers struggle to put points on the board. The fifth-year kicker has seen just five extra points in three games, converting all five, and he's connected on just three of five FG attempts, with all three makes coming in a Week 3 loss to the Bills. That volatility isn't fantasy-friendly, and until the team's skill players begin to get the hang of new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme, Dicker's volume is likely to remain limited. He probably won't be able to afford to squander any chances in Week 4 against a Seahawks team allowing just 16.7 points per game, tied for third in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Ferguson was surprisingly quiet in Week 1 for the Cowboys versus the Giants. Ferguson finished with just two catches for six yards in the 28-20 loss. Meanwhile, fellow tight ends Brevyn Spann-Ford and Luke Schoonmaker both gained more yards through the air. However, the Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no pass-catcher with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Ferguson scored twice last game for the Cowboys. Ferguson caught four passes for 43 yards and the two scores in the 37-20 win over Washington. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL. In addition, the Ravens have given up just two passing touchdowns through two tilts.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jake Ferguson found the end zone again for the Cowboys last game. Ferguson caught three passes for 23 yards and the touchdown in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Ferguson has three touchdowns over his last two contests, all coming within the red zone. However, Ferguson has yet to gain even 45 yards in a single outing, making him a touchdown-dependent option in Week 4 versus the Texans. Houston has yielded five touchdowns through three tilts, which is tied for 16th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Ferguson has emerged as a reliable target for Dak Prescott in the high-scoring Dallas offense, which has led to solid fantasy production. Ferguson, who has handled a 17% target share each of the past three seasons, is fresh off a career year in which he ranked third among tight ends in receptions, touchdowns and end zone targets (10). His nine top-12 fantasy weeks tied for second, though it's worth noting that his production dropped off substantially with a healthy CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on the field during the second half of the season (under 12.0 fantasy points in each of his final eight healthy games, 7.3 PPG during the span). The 27-year-old's role as a short-range target (4.7 aDOT last season) limits his yardage upside, but he sees just enough work, including near the goal line, to allow fringe-TE1 production. Don't call him "Joke Farterson" ("Fantasy Football Now" viewers get it); Ferguson is vying for his third top-10 fantasy campaign in his past four seasons.

outlooksByWeek.2: J.K. Dobbins wasn't a big part of the Broncos' game plan in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, as the veteran running back had only eight carries for 36 yards. RJ Harvey's volume was similar, with seven touches to Dobbins' eight, but turnovers and game flow played a part in limiting their opportunities. Dobbins averaged over 80 scrimmage yards last season in the 10 regular-season games he was healthy, so better days should be ahead for Denver's lead back, although they may not come right away. In Week 2, he'll face a Jaguars defense that ranked third in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: J.K. Dobbins' workload has been limited to begin the season, with just 18 carries for 72 yards through the Broncos' first two games. The veteran back also has yet to see a target, as RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman have been prioritized as pass-catchers. Dobbins picked up a minor hamstring injury in Week 2's win over the Jaguars, but the issue isn't expected to keep him out of the lineup in Week 3. The same can't be said for Harvey, however, who didn't play at all in Week 2 due to his own hamstring strain. Dobbins could split touches with Coleman again in Week 3 against a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: J.K. Dobbins is coming off his largest workload of the season in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams. He had 17 carries and 18 total touches but turned them into just 53 scrimmage yards. Dobbins has struggled out of the gate, averaging just 3.5 yards per carry, but he should continue to handle the majority of the early-down work while rookie Jonah Coleman is on IR. RJ Harvey, who compiled 47 scrimmage yards on just eight touches against the Rams, remains the primary passing-down back. Dobbins will look for his first touchdown of 2026 in Week 4 against a 49ers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Dobbins re-signed with Denver and will attempt to fend off sophomore RJ Harvey for the team's lead-back job. With both active during Weeks 1-10 last season (10 games), Dobbins handled 153 carries (60% team share) and 15 targets (4%), compared to 50 carries (20%) and 29 targets (9%) for Harvey. Dobbins ran well (5.05 yards per carry) when healthy, but he was limited to four touchdowns and was a nonfactor as a receiver (37 yards on 15 targets) en route to averaging 11.6 fantasy points (27th). Dobbins enters his age-27 campaign having yet to play a full season in his career (seven-plus missed games in four of the past five years) and without much value even when active (he has never produced a top-20 fantasy campaign). Dobbins is an underwhelming flex option with added value in non-PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Eddy Pineiro heads into a Week 2 matchup versus Miami on the heels of making two field goals in San Francisco's season-opening victory against the Rams. Pineiro's makes came from 20 and 56 yards out, though he also missed a 52-yarder. The veteran kicker made a career-high six FGs from 50-plus yards out last year, so San Francisco is clearly comfortable relying on his leg from that distance. The 49ers could put up plenty of points in Week 2, as the Dolphins just gave up 27 points to Las Vegas in a Week 1 loss.
outlooksByWeek.3: Eddy Pineiro remains a solid fantasy kicker option heading into the 49ers' Week 3 matchup against Arizona. Pineiro didn't attempt a field goal Sunday against the Dolphins, but he converted all five of his extra-point tries. San Francisco has averaged 31.0 points per game through two weeks, so Pineiro figures to see frequent opportunities to kick, though that won't always result in field-goal chances. Arizona's opponents have attempted just one FG through two weeks, but the Cardinals gave up a hefty 31 points to Seattle in a Week 2 loss.
outlooksByWeek.4: Eddy Pineiro will look to get his consistency back on track for San Francisco in Week 4 versus the Broncos. Pineiro missed a pair of extra-point tries Sunday in a win over Arizona, but he also nailed a 57-yard field goal. The veteran kicker hadn't previously struggled with PATs, making all eight over his first two games of the campaign, so his erratic boot may have just been an aberration. Denver has yielded eight field-goal attempts and seven extra-point tries through three weeks.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Pittman and the Steelers travel for a Week 2 tilt against the Patriots. The former Indianapolis Colt secured all three targets for a team-high 58 yards in his debut for Pittsburgh. Pittman finished sixth in targets but still did plenty of damage with his opportunities, and if the Steelers want to throw the ball 40-plus times a game, he could develop into a reliable fantasy receiver. New England's defense ranks 21st in receiving yards allowed to WRs (161), but they will be playing at home with a rest advantage.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Pittman and the Steelers host the Bengals in Week 3. After dealing with a foot injury during training camp and the preseason, he suffered a new foot ailment that forced him to miss Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss in New England. Pittman will have to practice in some capacity in order to return for Sunday's contest, but it sounds like his status for Week 3 is very much in question. Consider him doubtful to suit up until we hear otherwise.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Pittman and the Steelers travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He returned from a one-game absence and caught two of five targets for 16 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. Pittman tied for second on the team in targets but was unable to make much of an impact, as Aaron Rodgers continued spreading the ball around on offense by hitting nine different receivers. However, he has an opportunity to break out against Cleveland's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (36.7) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Pittman was traded to the Steelers after spending his first six NFL seasons with the Colts. The 2020 second-round pick handled a hefty 23.6% of Indianapolis' targets during his tenure, which helped him to four top-20 fantasy campaigns. Pittman has reached 800 receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while primarily operating as a short-to-intermediate target. The role has limited his scoring (he has 25 TDs in 95 games) and that may not change much with DK Metcalf on the other side in Pittsburgh. Of course, Pittman will be a featured target in an offense led by Aaron Rodgers. That's enough to put the 28-year-old squarely in the weekly WR3 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dallas Goedert was the leading receiver for the Eagles in Week 1. Goedert snagged four passes for 77 yards and two touchdowns in the 24-22 win over Washington. Goedert was targeted five times. With A.J. Brown no longer in the fold, Goedert could see even more touches in the red zone. In Week 2, the Eagles will face the Tennessee Titans.  Tennessee was a tad frisky against the pass in Week 1, allowing just 215 yards passing to the Jets.  In addition, the Titans did not allow a passing touchdown for the game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dallas Goedert suffered a knee injury last game for Philadelphia and did not return, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus Chicago. Goedert is set to undergo testing to determine the nature and extent of the issue. Johnny Mundt caught two apsses in Goedert's place, and would be the next man up if Goedert cannot suit up. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dallas Goedert did not suit up last game for the Eagles due to a knee injury, and his status remains very much in question for Week 4 versus the Rams. In his place, Zach Ertz and Johnny Mundt combined for just two catches for 13 yards. Even if Goedert can suit up, the Rams have been rather stingy against the pass so far in 2026. Los Angeles is allowing just 171.2 passing yards per contest, which is fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Goedert enters the 2026 season as the poster boy for inevitable touchdown regression to the mean. After scoring 24 touchdowns in his first seven seasons (3.4 per year), Goedert inexplicably leaped to 11 scores in 15 games in 2025. Goedert's expected TD total was 5.1, and he saw only five end zone targets (12 tight ends saw more). Goedert is a solid fantasy tight end -- he has finished 12th or better in PPG each of the past seven seasons -- but he often misses games (at least two in each of the past six years) and has never finished in the top eight at the position in targets or catches. The 31-year-old is likely to deliver fringe-TE1 numbers in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Pitts will look to rebound for a disappointing Week 1 performance in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Pitts failed to haul in his lone target during last week's loss, with Bijan Robinson and Drake London combining for a 73.6% of Cooper Rush's targets. Despite this, Pitts could very well rebound against a Panthers defense that just allowed a whopping 59 points in Week 1, as they also gave up 11.5 PPR fantasy points to tight ends. His rebound could depend on Atlanta's quarterback situation, with both Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) looking to return from injury in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyle Pitts will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Pitts has really struggled along with the majority of Atlanta's offense throughout the first two weeks, catching just one of four targets for 15 yards. However, he could really benefit from the return of Michael Penix as the team's starting quarterback heading into Week 3. While Penix was healthy during the 2025 season, Pitts averaged 4.2 receptions and 41.7 yards per game -- a vast difference from his 2026 production thus far. He's also in for a favorable matchup, as the Packers' defense has allowed 12.0 PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyle Pitts will look to bounce back from a disappointing start in the Falcons' Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Despite Michael Penix returning to the field in the Week 3 win over the Packers, Pitts' role remained limited, catching just one of two targets for five yards. He was overshadowed by Drake London (9-194-0) and appears to be operating as the Falcons' No. 3 pass catcher, also behind Bijan Robinson (16 targets to Pitts' six). However, Pitts could rebound in Week 4, as the Saints' defense has allowed 20.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Right when it seemed like Pitts might never live up to the hype, the 2021 No. 4 pick put together the best season of his career. Pitts finished second among tight ends in routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy points, setting career highs in all but the yardage category. He scored five touchdowns and has increased his total in that category (by exactly one) each season in the league. Pitts did a big chunk of his damage with Kirk Cousins under center (some with WR Drake London sidelined), which is notable as Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. are set to battle for the Atlanta QB job. There's some obvious risk here considering Pitts finished 17th or lower in PPG three straight seasons before 2025, but he nonetheless enters his age-25 season as a priority target in the Atlanta offense. Consider him a midrange TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Monangai will look to be a big contributor once again for the Bears in Week 2 against the Vikings. While Monangai still took a back-seat role to D'Andre Swift in Week 1 against the Panthers, he still finished the game with 10 carries for 100 yards and a touchdown, along with 24 yards off two catches. The second-year ball carrier should still have plenty of a share in Chicago's rushing game to be fantasy relevant, especially given how much potential their offense showed for the season. Monangai will face a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but the Bears have a much superior RB room as of now.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyle Monangai should remain a high-volume RB2 as the Bears take on the Eagles in Week 3. Monangai saw double-digit carries once again in Week 2, but he totaled just 47 yards on the ground and tacked on 11 yards off two catches. The second-year running back has now seen 12 touches in each of Chicago's two outings this year, and he could see even more with Tyson Bagent slated to start under center. Philly has also ceded 216 rushing yards to RBs this season, a bottom-10 mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyle Monangai should remain the complementary option in Chicago's backfield in Week 4 against the Jets. Monangai logged his third straight showing with 10 carries in Week 3 versus the Eagles, but he converted them for a season-low 31 rushing yards. The second-year running back also garnered no targets in the passing game, which came as a letdown after he posted a 4-35-0 receiving line leading up to the Monday Night win. He'll look to improve on his consistent volume against a New York defense that's allowed an eighth-most 24.1 fantasy points per game to RBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Monangai heads into his second NFL season following an impressive rookie campaign in which he quickly forced his way into a committee with D'Andre Swift. The 2025 seventh-round flier played 41% of Chicago's offensive snaps and averaged a healthy 4.6 yards per carry on 169 attempts. Monangai was limited to 7.7 fantasy PPG during the 16 weeks Swift also played, but he showed his insurance value with a 29-touch, 198-yard effort in the one game Swift was sidelined (Week 9). The 24-year-old could see a slight boost in usage this season, but that usage and production will be limited as long as Swift is also healthy.

The NFL's leading sack-getter the past two seasons, the Broncos D/ST lost DE John Franklin-Myers during the offseason but otherwise return largely the same front for 2026. Led by Zach Allen, Nik Bonitto and four-time Pro Bowl cornerback Patrick Surtain II, the Broncos scored 15-plus fantasy points on four occasions last season and finished third in the category. Their early-season schedule presents some challenges (@KC, Week 1; LAR, Week 3; @SF, Week 4), but overall theirs is one of the most favorable, especially across a nine-week span beginning in Week 7 (@ARI, KC, @CAR, bye, LV, @PIT, MIA, @NYJ, @LV).

outlooksByWeek.2: Bo Nix was held in check by the Kansas City defense in the Broncos' season opener, completing 17 of 28 passes for just 131 yards and a touchdown. He also threw an interception and committed three fumbles, losing one of them, while getting sacked four times. Nix also wasn't able to take advantage of his newest asset, as Jaylen Waddle logged only three targets and caught one of them for two yards. It was a hugely disappointing effort from Nix and the reigning AFC West champions, but they'll look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked 18th last season in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bo Nix rebounded from a sluggish opener to lead the Broncos to a comeback win over the Jaguars in Week 2. The third-year QB has a meager 2:2 TD:INT through two games and has yet to add any production on the ground, but his 288 passing yards In Week 2 were more than double the Week 1 total, and his completion rate jumped from 60.7% to 71.0%. Nix also began establishing some chemistry with new top wideout Jaylen Waddle, who erupted for an 8-138-0 line on 10 targets. Nix will face a Rams defense in Week 3 that has held opposition QBs under a 60% completion rate to begin the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bo Nix engineered an impressive second-half comeback in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, producing two passing TDs and one rushing score despite completing just 50.0% of his passes. The third-year quarterback hasn't had a statistically impressive start to the season, posting a 4:3 TD:INT ratio and passing for barely over 200 yards a game, but Nix has led his team to a 2-1 record. He'll take on a 49ers defense in Week 4 that's been stingy to begin the year, ranking eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Nix enters his third NFL season after finishing exactly seventh among quarterbacks in fantasy points during each of his first two campaigns. Nix's passing efficiency has a ways to go (career 6.5 yards per attempt), but his dual-threat ability has kept him in the weekly QB1 mix. Nix has finished both seasons no lower than 11th in pass attempts, completions, passing TDs, carries, rushing yards and rushing TDs. Last season, he provided a solid floor (11 games with 15-plus fantasy points), but his ceiling was low (four top-10 weeks). In 2026, he'll have a new playcaller in Davis Webb and an upgraded group of pass catchers with Jaylen Waddle added to the mix. The 26-year-old is a fringe QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Braelon Allen will look to build on a solid opener when the Jets face the Packers in Week 2. Allen had 10 carries in Week 1 under new OC Frank Reich, after totaling 18 carries in four games before injury in 2025. The volume resulted from the Jets playing with a lead, a game script that's unlikely to repeat in Week 2. Allen remains a secondary option to Breece Hall, so patience is warranted, particularly against a defense that allowed only 3.7 yards per carry in Week 1 and is more vulnerable through the air.
outlooksByWeek.3: Braelon Allen's usage remains questionable as the Jets prepare to face the Lions in Week 3. After a run-heavy Week 1 where Allen had 10 attempts, that number was cut in half in Week 2. He has also only seen two targets through two games. Breece Hall remains the workhorse, and the Lions' vulnerability to chunk plays in the passing game could further phase Allen out of meaningful touches, despite Detroit allowing 5.2 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.4: Braelon Allen is poised for an expanded role in Week 4 when the Jets face the Bears due to Breece Hall's thigh injury. The rushing game has struggled over the last two weeks, averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry, but the Jets have remained committed to running while also involving their backs in the passing game. With volume seemingly secure, Allen could shine against a defense that's allowing 4.9 yards per carry.

player.seasonOutlook: Hopes were high for Allen entering 2025, but a slow start was followed by a season-ending knee injury in Week 4. During Weeks 1-3, Allen played 28% of the Jets' snaps and totaled 67 yards and one touchdown on 16 touches. The 2024 fourth-round pick has shown he can contribute as both a rusher (110 career carries) and receiver (32 targets), but he's simply not going to see the field much as long as feature back Breece Hall is healthy. Allen, 22, has some late-round insurance stash appeal, as he'd likely start over Isaiah Davis in the event of a Hall injury and would thus find himself on the flex radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top receiving options in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Johnson paced New Orleans' tight ends in yards (53) during the Week 1 overtime loss but trailed Noah Fant in receptions (three to four) and targets (seven to eight). Despite this, Johnson was on the field for 72 of the Saints' 90 offensive snaps, where Fant played just 37. Thus, Johnson is expected to remain New Orleans' top TE option against a Ravens defense that allowed just 10.3 PPR fantasy points to the position in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of New Orleans' top receiving options in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Despite a dip in snap rate and route share compared to Week 1, Johnson paced the Saints' tight end corps in receptions, targets and yards in Week 2. He ranks third on the team in targets and yards, which is a positive outlook for his value going forward. However, Johnson is in for an unfavorable matchup, as Las Vegas' defense has allowed just 10.3 PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top weapons in the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Johnson has been New Orleans' second-most productive receiver this season, catching 15 of 19 targets for 173 yards and three touchdowns. With head coach Kellen Moore's offense throwing the ball an average of 44 times per game through three weeks, Johnson is expected to remain one of fantasy's top tight ends going forward. Additionally, he's in for a terrific Week 4 matchup against a Falcons defense that's allowed 17.2 PPR fantasy points per game to the TE position this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson's impressive progression continued in 2025, as the converted wide receiver posted career-high marks in targets, catches, yardage and fantasy points (all four were eighth or better among tight ends). Johnson produced nine top-12 fantasy weeks, which tied for second at the position. He has finished in the top 12 in aDOT each of the past four seasons but hasn't been much of an option near the goal line (no more than four TDs or end zone targets in each of the past three seasons). The 29-year-old has added target competition, including eighth-overall pick Jordyn Tyson (once healthy), but he very well could settle in as high as third in target priority in the Saints' Tyler Shough-led offense. Johnson is a fine TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jakobi Meyers maintains a high floor, though he's a low-ceiling fantasy WR3 or flex play for Jacksonville's Week 2 home game against Denver's elite defense. Meyers has posted at least 39 receiving yards in all 10 of his games with the Jaguars since coming over in a midseason trade last year, including 40 receiving yards and a TD in the Week 1 win over Cleveland. Parker Washington and Brian Thomas have more downfield playmaking capability, but Meyers should see his share of short targets with Trevor Lawrence likely looking to get the ball out quickly to counter a Broncos pass rush that led the league with 68 sacks last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jakobi Meyers has been targeted just three times through Jacksonville's first two games. That lack of volume makes him hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league dart throw in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that held the Seahawks and Steelers to a combined 16 points. Parker Washington (18 targets), Brian Thomas (11 targets), and even TE Brenton Strange (five targets) have all been higher on Trevor Lawrence's priority list than Meyers. To the veteran wide receiver's credit, Meyers's 28-yard effort on one target in the Week 2 loss to Denver marked the first time in 11 games as a member of the Jaguars that he failed to record at least 39 receiving yards. Therefore, he could rebuild a solid fantasy floor if Lawrence starts looking Meyers's way more frequently.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jakobi Meyers led the Jaguars with seven catches for 64 yards and a touchdown on eight targets in Week 3 against the Patriots after catching all three of his targets for 68 yards and a TD across Jacksonville's first two games. The veteran wideout has been playing alongside Parker Washington in two-WR sets and working ahead of Brian Thomas, as Meyers' 79% snap share this season is nearly double Thomas' mark. Washington is the clear No. 1 receiving option for the Jaguars, but Meyers is shaping up as the team's next-most reliable pass catcher, which is enough to be deployed as a WR3 or flex option in Week 4 against the Bengals, who didn't allow a touchdown pass through Week 2 before giving up TDs to three separate Steelers wideouts in Week 3.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the league's most underrated players, Meyers is entering his first full season with Jacksonville after being acquired via trade in November. The 2019 UDFA has produced 800-plus receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while operating primarily as a short-to-intermediate target. More of a solid producer than a high-ceiling contributor, Meyers has finished no lower than 32nd in fantasy points over the last five seasons, but has yet to do better than 19th. The 29-year-old isn't much of a touchdown scorer (23 TDs in 78 games since 2021) and has substantial target competition via Parker Washington, Brian Thomas Jr., Brenton Strange and Travis Hunter. Meyers is a good player, but is likely to cap out as a flex option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Justin Herbert struggled in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, completing 17 of 27 passes for 209 yards and one touchdown with one interception, while adding 29 rushing yards on five carries. Injuries along the offensive line were once again an issue for the club; the interior of the line, with rookie Jake Slaughter at center, wasn't able to hold up, and new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel didn't seem to have many answers. Ladd McConkey also suffered a rib injury in the game, which could make things even more difficult for Herbert if the top wideout misses any time. Herbert will look to rebound in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justin Herbert has had a rough start to the season with Mike McDaniel as his new offensive coordinator. Through two games, he's completed less than 60% of his passes with a 2:3 TD:INT ratio and barely over 200 passing yards per game. Ladd McConkey was his only reliable target in the Chargers' opener, but the third-year wideout was limited by a rib injury in Week 2's loss to the Raiders, and no one else stepped up. As in years past, Herbert's protection has also been decimated by injuries. An offensive line that was already missing starting center Tyler Biadasz was down to a third-string left guard against Las Vegas in Week 2, and the team also lost its two best blocking tight ends, Charlie Kolar and David Njoku, over the course of that contest. Herbert could be in for another long day in Week 3 against a Bills defense that has seven sacks through two games, tied for fourth in the league, but which has been vulnerable through the air when the opposing QB has found some time.
outlooksByWeek.4: Justin Herbert continues to struggle in new Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The veteran quarterback has yet to throw multiple touchdowns in a game this season, while his 59.1% completion rate would be a career-worst mark. Herbert is also dealing with his usual protection issues and has been sacked eight times in three contests, a pace that would see him get brought down more than 40 times for a third straight year. His top target, Ladd McConkey, should be healthier as he puts a rib injury further behind him, but as yet none of his other pass catchers have made any kind of impact. Herbert's rough year could get worse in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that's tied for third in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Herbert enters his seventh NFL season following a solid 2025 campaign in which he ranked just inside the top 10 quarterbacks in pass attempts, yards and touchdowns. Herbert added serious value with his legs, ranking fifth at the position in carries and second in rushing yards (career highs in both). He finished 10th among quarterbacks in fantasy points, but that's a bit misleading, as his inconsistent production led to five top-five weeks but no other finishes better than 13th. Herbert has finished between 11th and 15th in fantasy points per game in each of the past four seasons, though it's fair to expect a leap forward in 2026 with star tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater healthy and a new playcaller in Mike McDaniel. Herbert is safest as a QB2, but there's upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Marvin Harrison will look to get going in Arizona's Week 2 tilt against Seattle. Harrison notched just one catch on three targets in a season-opening win over the Chargers, though that reception did go for a robust 33 yards. With that said, the fact that he drew such a small amount of QB Jacoby Brissett's 37 targets provides some cause for concern, especially with newcomer Kendrick Bourne getting a healthy eight targets and No. 2 wideout Michael Wilson drawing seven. The Cardinals' wideout corps as a whole faces a tough challenge in the Seahawks, who didn't allow any Patriots pass catcher to exceed 51 yards in a Week 1 victory.
outlooksByWeek.3: Marvin Harrison will look to bounce back from his Week 2 goose egg when the Cardinals face San Francisco in Week 3. Harrison was targeted by QB Jacoby Brissett just once Sunday in a loss to the Seahawks and finished without a catch. The third-year receiver concerningly has just one catch for 33 yards through two weeks, and perhaps even more distressingly for his fantasy managers, he's drawn only four targets to Michael Wilson's 14 so far. The 49ers rank in the top 10 through two weeks by giving up only 247 receiving yards to wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.4: Marvin Harrison heads into the Cardinals' Week 4 matchup against the Giants having yet to get going this season. Harrison did record a campaign-best three catches and 40 yards this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, but he was far outshined by fellow wideout Michael Wilson, who posted an 11-89-1 line on a massive 17 targets. Star tight end Trey McBride also continued to shine with a 9-75-0 receiving line, so Harrison appears to be QB Jacoby Brissett's third option in the passing game at the moment. The Giants could present an opportunity for Harrison to get into the end zone, as they've given up four receiving TDs to wideouts so far this year, tied for fifth-most in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Harrison's pro career is off to a slow start after he was selected with the No. 4 overall pick back in 2024. The Ohio State product was serviceable as a rookie (885 yards and eight TDs), but he missed five full games and was limited in others en route to a 41-608-4 receiving line in 2025. Harrison has finished 41st and 39th, respectively, in fantasy PPG despite a massive role near the goal line (he's third in the NFL in end zone targets since he was drafted and finished both seasons in the top five). Harrison is only entering his prime at age 24 and perhaps he'll make a Year 3 leap with new coach Mike LaFleur calling the plays and with Kyler Murray no longer under center. Harrison performed better with Jacoby Brissett under center last season and has the raw talent to make him well worth post-hype consideration in the middle rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jacory Croskey-Merritt found the end zone in Week 1 for Washington.  Bill served as the primary ballcarrier, toting the pigskin 16 times for 63 yards and the score. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White had seven carries for only 22 years. In Week 2, Croskey-Merritt will have a favorable matchup versus the Cowboys. Dallas allowed 165 yards rushing and one score on the ground to the Giants in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jacory Croskey-Merritt took 12 carries for 43 yards in Washington's loss to Dallas last game. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. Croskey-Merritt looks like the preferred back between the tackles, with White acting as the pass-catching or third-down option. The timeshare will likely continue against a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. In addition, Seattle has yet to allow a rushing touchdown to the opposition, and the Commanders will be without their starting quarterback, Jayden Daniels due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jacory Croskey-Merritt was perhaps predictably stymied by the Seattle Seahawks last game. However, the touches were a silver lining, as Croskey-Merritt garnered 20 opportunities in the 33-31 win over the defending champions. Bill rushed 19 times for 36 yards, while also catching a seven-yard pass out of the backfield. However, fellow running back Rachaad White  averaged more than double Croskey-Meritt's yards per carry, while also finding the end zone through the air. However, there could be plenty of room to roam in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been dreadful against the run in 2026, allowing 141.3 yards per contest on he ground, which is 29th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the most hyped-up players entering the 2025 fantasy season, Croskey-Merritt didn't quite live up to lofty expectations, but he was certainly very busy for a seventh-round rookie. "Bill" played 39% of Washington's offensive snaps but, while he finished 23rd among backs in rushing yards, he wasn't much of a factor in the passing game (3% target share). Croskey-Merritt will now compete with newcomer Rachaad White in what appears to be setting up as a committee in Washington. The 25-year-old has shown to be an effective rusher (4.60 yards per carry, 2.19 YAC), but he'll need a big boost in receiving work to find his way into the RB2/flex discussion. He's worth only a late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 matchup against the Patriots. He rushed eight times for 15 yards and caught two of five targets for another six yards during Pittsburgh's Week 1 20-13 win over Atlanta. Dowdle's backfield partner, Jaylen Warren, was much more efficient with his 15 touches, which he turned into 73 scrimmage yards. It will be difficult to trust Dowdle in a tilt versus New England's 14th-ranked defense, which has allowed 84 rushing yards to the position.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Bengals and their 14th-ranked run defense in Week 3. He finished Pittsburgh's loss last week with seven carries for 22 yards and caught both targets for 22 yards. Dowdle left the game in the second quarter with a toe injury, was cleared and returned to play in the second half but then left for good after appearing to re-injure the same toe. Keep an eye on his status in practice this week, as there's a good chance he'll be limited, thus leaving his status for Sunday's contest against the Bengals in question.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns for a Week 4 road tilt. He sat out Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory with a toe injury he sustained in Week 2, and it looks like he's in real jeopardy of missing a second consecutive contest. Dowdle didn't practice at all last week and was not present at Monday's walkthrough session, which isn't a great sign for his availability on a short week. He'll have to practice in some capacity if he hopes to face Cleveland's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Dowdle signed with the Steelers after nearly identical campaigns with the Cowboys in 2024 (1,328 yards and five TDs on 274 touches) and Panthers in 2025 (1,373 yards and seven TDs on 275 touches). He was effective as a rusher (4.57 yards per carry) and fairly busy as a receiver (50 targets both years) en route to finishing just inside the top 25 in fantasy points per game both seasons. Now in Pittsburgh, the 28-year-old is expected to share work with Jaylen Warren. Earning lead-rusher duties could get Dowdle into the weekly flex discussion, but the ceiling will be low and he'll likely need an injury in order to find his way to consistent fantasy output. Consider him for your bench.

outlooksByWeek.2: Xavier Worthy captured three of his six Week 1 targets for only 18 yards. The workload was low, but Kansas City QB Patrick Mahomes completed only five passes to wideouts in the Monday night opener. The third-year pro has the speed to stretch the field, but he's generally used more underneath, along with occasionally carrying the ball. Worthy is a Week 2 flex option when the Chiefs host the Colts. Indianapolis was one of five defenses to allow over 300 yards passing in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Xavier Worthy scored his first touchdown of the season in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, snagging a one-yard toss from Patrick Mahomes in the second quarter. Worthy has notched steady target volume early in the season, with 13 total looks, but that has resulted in just an 8-43-1 line, and he has yet to get a carry. With Mahomes spreading the ball around and the offense prioritizing Kenneth Walker and the run game, Worthy will need some big plays to make a real fantasy contribution. The third-year speedster will face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Xavier Worthy has struggled to break free for a big gain for Kansas City this season. The third-year speedster has managed just a 10-63-1 line on 15 targets, and surprisingly, he has yet to get a carry, perhaps to keep him healthy. Patrick Mahomes has also spread the ball around effectively, as Worthy, Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets, so a big volume increase isn't likely. Worthy faces a tough matchup in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and has yet to allow a TD to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: After impressing as a rookie with 101 touches and 12 touchdowns in 20 games (including the playoffs), Worthy had the look of an emerging star. Things didn't go as planned in Year 2, though, as the 2024 first-round pick was injured on his third snap of the season and wasn't productive or utilized as much as expected upon his return. Worthy was limited to one touchdown (Week 6) and reached 12 fantasy points once in 14 games (Week 4). The speedy Worthy is still only 23 years old, so a Year 3 breakout is certainly possible, especially with Rashee Rice and 36-year-old Travis Kelce as his only legit target competition. He's worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Blake Corum was one of few Rams players to have a good game on offense in their season-opening loss, and he'll look for more success in Week 2 against the Giants. Corum led Los Angeles with 54 rushing yards on just 10 carries versus San Francisco last Thursday, averaging 5.4 YPC after putting up an average of 5.1 YPC during the regular season last year. Kyren Williams remains the Rams' lead back, but there's little doubt that Corum has forced his way into a substantial role as well. The Giants held Dallas' No. 1 RB Javonte Williams to 3.4 YPC on 12 totes in Week 1, though Williams did score a rushing TD and put up a 5-31-1 line through the air.
outlooksByWeek.3: Blake Corum should continue to be a big part of the Rams' backfield versus the Broncos in Week 3. Against the Giants on Monday Night Football, Corum racked up 79 yards on 12 carries while adding a 13-yard reception. Through two weeks, Corum has 22 carries to Kyren Williams'  23, so the pair appear to be headed for a pretty even workload in 2026. Denver could be vulnerable to both ball carriers, as the Broncos have given up a whopping 5.40 YPC to RBs this season -- third worst in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Blake Corum will look to bounce back following a quiet Week 3 performance when the Rams visit Philadelphia in Week 4. Corum was held to season-low marks of six carries and 15 yards this past Sunday versus Denver while Kyren Williams put up 158 total yards. Though some expected Corum to challenge Williams for touches even more this season, the latter has emphatically cemented his No. 1 RB role with his strong early-season performance. Both Corum and Williams may need to rely on their work on the ground against the Eagles, who have given up the fewest receiving yards to running backs so far this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Corum has spent his first two NFL seasons as Kyren Williams' backup, and that's expected to be the case again in 2026. The 2024 third-round NFL draft pick played well in the role last season, averaging a healthy 5.1 yards per carry (seventh among RBs) and scoring six touchdowns on 145 carries. However, Corum played only 29% of the Rams' snaps and remained a nonfactor as a receiver (36 yards on 14 targets). The 25-year-old has no standalone fantasy value, but he's an elite insurance stash, as he'd launch into the fringe-RB1 mix in the Rams' high-powered offense should Williams miss time.

outlooksByWeek.2: RJ Harvey's workload was limited in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City. He gained 18 rushing yards on three carries and caught all four of his targets for 23 yards. That volume was comparable to J.K. Dobbins, who got eight touches-all carries-to Harvey's seven. Turnovers and game flow played a part in limiting their opportunities. Harvey's role as the primary pass-catching back still bodes well for his production in his second NFL season after posting a 47-356-5 line on 58 targets over 17 regular-season games in 2025. He'll get a potentially tough matchup in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked third in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: RJ Harvey wasn't able to suit up in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to a hamstring strain, putting his availability for a Week 3 matchup against the Rams in question. The second-year back was expected to be the pass-catching complement to J.K. Dobbins for the Broncos, but rookie Jonah Coleman handled that role and didn't look out of place. If Harvey misses too much time, Coleman could take his job, but Dobbins' own checkered injury history could leave Denver patching together a backfield from whoever is healthy.
outlooksByWeek.4: RJ Harvey returned from a one-game absence due to a hamstring strain in Week 2 to contribute to the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, gaining just six rushing yards on two carries but producing a 6-41-0 line on seven targets. The second-year back is secure in his role as Denver's top pass-catcher out of the backfield while J.K. Dobbins is the main option on early downs. Rookie Jonah Coleman could challenge both once he's back from IR. Harvey will look to make a bigger impact in Week 4 against a 49ers defense that's already given up 17 catches to RBs this season, 28th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Harvey will go into his sophomore campaign looking to overtake J.K. Dobbins as Denver's lead back. In the 10 games in which both backs were active last season, Harvey handled 50 carries (20% team share) and 29 targets (9%), compared to Dobbins' 153 carries (60%) and 15 targets (4%). With Dobbins sidelined for the team's remaining nine games (including the playoff run), Harvey handled 115 carries (55%) and 41 targets (13%). He averaged 10.0 fantasy points with Dobbins and 14.2 without, though his 3.3 yards per carry during the final nine games was very poor. The entire Denver backfield is set to return in 2026, so similar deployment (which would include receiving specialist Tyler Badie) could be in the cards, though fourth-round rookie Jonah Coleman could factor in eventually as well. Harvey, 25, has a slight bit of breakout potential, but the committee setup suggests he's safest viewed as no more than a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Harrison Mevis is coming off a quiet season opener as the Rams prepare to face the Giants in Week 2. Los Angeles' offense was held by the 49ers to just seven points last Thursday, and Mevis didn't get the opportunity to attempt any field goals. The Rams figure to be much more prolific on that side of the ball most weeks, so Mevis should be more active moving forward, though last year he attempted 39 PATs to just 13 field goals. The Giants' defense put up a good performance in a Week 1 win over Dallas, with star kicker Brandon Aubrey getting no field-goal tries.
outlooksByWeek.3: Harrison Mevis is still searching for his first field-goal conversion heading into the Rams' Week 3 clash against Denver. Mevis didn't try a FG in Week 1, and he missed his only attempt -- a 43-yarder -- on Monday Night Football. Mevis did make all four of his extra-point tries and figures to kick a lot of those given the Rams' explosive offense. Kickers have gone 3-for-4 on field-goal attempts against the Broncos so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Harrison Mevis is coming off a career-best four FGs ahead of the Rams' matchup versus Philadelphia in Week 4. After going 0-for-1 in field-goal tries over the first two weeks of the campaign, Mevis was asked to attempt four FGs versus Denver in Week 3 and made every try, including a 48-yarder. With that said, the Rams' explosive offense doesn't frequently end drives with field-goal attempts, so Mevis may struggle to see such volume moving forward. Opponents have been successful on five of six field-goal attempts versus the Eagles so far this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Denzel Boston and the Browns travel to battle the Buccaneers in Week 2. The rookie pass-catcher corralled two of four targets for 59 yards and a TD during Cleveland's 34-10 season-opening loss. Boston's touchdown was a 46-yard dime from Deshaun Watson, and he finished as the team leader in receiving yards. He draws a tough matchup against Tampa Bay, which ranked fourth in receptions allowed to WRs (8).
outlooksByWeek.3: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the Panthers in a Week 3 clash between 1-1 teams. The rookie followed up his 2-59-1 receiving line in the opener with an even better outing against the Buccaneers, tallying five catches on seven targets for 95 yards and another TD. Boston led the team in yardage and targets, as he's quickly becoming Deshaun Watson's preferred target, particularly downfield. He faces a vulnerable Carolina defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points allowed (30.3) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the Steelers and their eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (28.0) to WRs in Week 4. The rookie wideout caught two of four targets for 41 yards and scored on a two-point conversion during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3. Boston finished second on the team in yardage behind Harold Fannin Jr. (51) as he continues to develop chemistry with QB Deshaun Watson. He's shaping up to be a boom-or-bust fantasy option but offers plenty of upside as the Browns' deep option for an improving offense.

player.seasonOutlook: Boston was selected by the Browns in the second round of April's draft. He is a big receiver with terrific ball skills and touchdown-scoring upside. He's not the fastest, but that didn't stop him from producing 62-plus receptions, 830-plus yards and nine-plus TDs during both of his seasons as a starter at Washington. He handled 45% of his team's air yards in 2025 (highest in this rookie class). Boston dropped only four of 209 career targets (1.9% drop rate is fourth best in this WR class) and has the look of a reliable possession receiver. He'll begin his career battling Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie KC Concepcion for targets in a Cleveland offense yet to sort out its quarterback situation. Boston is a fine late-round-upside flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brian Thomas tied for second on the Jaguars with 40 receiving yards on three targets in the season opener, as Trevor Lawrence threw just 21 passes in a lopsided win over the Browns. Fellow WRs Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers both got into the end zone, while Thomas failed to score. Thomas also left the game to be evaluated for a shoulder injury, though he managed to return. There are a lot of mouths to feed in Jacksonville's passing game, and the team's entire offensive output could be limited in a Week 2 road matchup against a Denver defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the NFL last season and employs star CB Patrick Surtain. Given that context, Thomas is a boom-or-bust fantasy WR3 for Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brian Thomas has notched exactly three catches for 40 yards in each of his first two games this season, providing a baseline expectation for the 2024 first-round pick's production in Jacksonville's Week 3 home game against the Patriots. Thomas is certainly capable of more, considering he averaged over 75 receiving yards per game as a rookie and scored 10 TDs that year, but has only two TDs in 16 games since then and is unlikely to score against a Patriots defense that has allowed only one touchdown this season. Perhaps breakout teammate Parker Washington will draw attention from top Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez to free up some space for Thomas to operate, but Thomas' lackluster production since the start of last season coupled with the tricky matchup make him a low-end flex play at best for Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brian Thomas has played fewer than 40% of Jacksonville's offensive snaps in two of the team's first three games while totaling just 88 yards. He has been outperformed by Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in the Jaguars' WR room, which leaves Thomas as a risky fantasy option in Week 4 against the Bengals. Benching the struggling Thomas is a defensible move, though he still maintains starter-worthy upside here considering Thomas flashed elite talent en route to an 87-1,282-10 line as a rookie in 2024, and the Bengals just allowed three different Steelers wideouts to score in Week 3.

player.seasonOutlook: Thomas is one of the biggest wild cards in fantasy after a roller-coaster start to his career. The 2024 first-round pick was fantasy's No. 4-scoring wide receiver as a rookie, but only played at that WR1 level with Mac Jones under center. Thomas averaged 5.8 targets and 14.4 fantasy PPG with Trevor Lawrence under center that season, and was even worse with Lawrence in 2025 (6.2 targets, 9.9 PPG). With Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Travis Hunter in the mix, Thomas was utilized as more of a vertical threat in 2025 (his 14.4 aDOT was fourth highest), which led to a big dip in catch rate and touchdowns, as well as more drops. The Jaguars offense is suddenly very crowded, so Thomas is more likely to be a boom/bust flex than he is the superstar we expected one year ago. The 23-year-old's raw talent makes him worth middle-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenneth Gainwell is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Gainwell was thought to be Tampa Bay's top receiving back heading into the season. However, he was overshadowed by Bucky Irving in Week 1, who caught all seven of his targets for 48 yards, while Gainwell was targeted just once. He will likely need more receiving work to be fantasy relevant in a Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed just two receptions for 22 yards to RBs last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenneth Gainwell is expected to play as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Gainwell was thought to be Tampa Bay's top receiving back heading into the season, but he's caught just three of four targets through two games, which is far less than Bucky Irving (11 receptions on 11 targets). Additionally, Gainwell has been relatively inefficient, averaging just 2.9 yards per touch. He's set to face one of the best defenses in the NFL in Minnesota, who have allowed just 3.4 yards per carry this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kenneth Gainwell is likely to remain Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Gainwell has logged just 10 rush attempts for 21 yards through three games this season, confirming he's firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield. The first-year Buccaneer has yet to score a touchdown as well, and he'll likely struggle finding fantasy value without a score. Despite this, Gainwell is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Packers defense that's already given up six rushing touchdowns this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Gainwell signed with the Buccaneers following a second-half breakout with Pittsburgh last season. After playing sparingly during the first four-and-a-half years of his career, Gainwell averaged 13.3 touches, 85.0 yards and 17.8 fantasy points from Week 8 on last season (eight games). Only five backs scored more points than Gainwell after Week 10. He did most of his damage as a receiver (top six among RBs in targets, catches and receiving yards) and will now look to earn a similar role alongside Bucky Irving in Tampa Bay. Gainwell's strong season suggests he'll have a role, but the 23-year-old Irving is likely to operate as the lead back. Gainwell is best valued as a bench/insurance stash with some flex appeal in deep PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyler Murray's status is up in the air as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Murray went down early in Week 1 against the Packers after taking a hard hit to the head. Before his exit, Murray completed three of five passes for 18 yards and one interception, tacking on two rushes for nine yards on the ground. The veteran is now under evaluation for a concussion, which could very likely keep him sidelined for an extended period. Backup quarterback Carson Wentz delivered the win for Minnesota, and he's set to assume QB duties once again. The Bears gave up 361 passing yards, three touchdowns and one interception to Bryce Young in Week 1, so big output could definitely be in the cards for whoever lines up under center for the Vikings.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyler Murray will return to the field as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Murray has cleared concussion protocol after suffering a nasty hit early in Week 1. The veteran quarterback will finally get the chance to prove himself, especially given that he completed just three of five passes for 18 yards and one interception before his opening-game departure. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.4 fantasy points per game to QBs across its first two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyler Murray will aim to build on a serviceable performance as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Murray returned to the field in Week 3 versus the Buccaneers, completing 15 of 29 passes for 168 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT ratio, along with rushing the ball twice for 17 yards. The veteran quarterback also lost star wideout Justin Jefferson in the first half, so his final output and delivery of a win were more impressive. Miami has been much more favorable against quarterbacks than Tampa so far this season, allowing the seventh-most fantasy points per game (23.7) to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Murray signed with the Vikings after spending his first seven seasons with the Cardinals. The change comes after a disappointing and injury-shortened 2025 season in which he failed to clear 18.3 fantasy points in any of his five appearances. Murray has settled in as an accurate but conservative passer and continues to add value with his legs (78-572-5 in 17 games in 2024). Prior to the 2025 dud, Murray had finished each of his first six NFL seasons as a top-12 fantasy QB (points per game). Now that he beat out J.J. McCarthy for Minnesota's starting job, he'll have the luxury of working with Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson. Add that to his rushing ability, and the 29-year-old certainly could find his way into the weekly QB1 mix. Consider Murray in the middle to late rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rachaad White found himself on the losing end of the timeshare out of the backfield in Week 1 for Washington.  White had seven carries for 22 yards, while fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt managed 16 carries for 63 yards and a touchdown. White only had one more reception than Croskey-Merritt as well. In Week 2, Washington has a favorable matchup with the Cowboys, as Dallas allowed 165 rushing yards on the ground to the Giants in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rachaad White recorded 13 touches for 83 yards out of the backfield last game for the Commanders. White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. White remains in a timeshare for touches with Jacory Croskey-Merritt, though, and will face a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3.  The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rachaad White found the end zone last game for Washington. White caught a six-yard touchdown pass from backup quarterback Marcus Mariota during the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. White also doubled up starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt in terms of yards per carry. However, Bill out-touched White by a margin of 20-9 for the game. Nevertheless, both backs should remain involved in Week 4 versus a suspect Colts defense. Indianapolis is allowing the most yards per game in the NFL through three contests.

player.seasonOutlook: White signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons with the Buccaneers. The 2022 third-round pick operated as a feature back in 2023 (he finished in the top five among backs in touches, yards and fantasy points), but he played a situational role during his other three seasons. White is fine as a rusher, but he's a standout as a receiver. He's the only back in the NFL with 40-plus catches in each of the past four seasons, and his 89.1% career catch rate is easily best in NFL history among players with 100-plus targets. The 27-year-old is the favorite to lead the Washington backfield, but Jacory Croskey-Merritt and perhaps others will be involved. White will find himself on the weekly flex radar as long as he remains atop the depth chart.

outlooksByWeek.2: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain an important part of the Saints' offense in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Vele saw nine targets in the Week 1 overtime loss, tying his career high and trailing only Chris Olave in the Saints' receiving corps. Vele should continue to benefit from the absence of Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) and is expected to see consistent volume until Tyson returns. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup for Vele, however, as the Ravens' defense has given up just 4.8 yards per pass attempt this season, which is tied for the second-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain the Saints' No. 2 wideout in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders, whose defense has given up just 15 receptions to WRs through two contests. Vele has clearly positioned himself as one of New Orleans' top receiving options early in the season, catching 12 of 16 targets for 133 yards and one touchdown thus far. He's expected to continue benefitting from the Saints' high volume of pass attempts, as Tyler Shough has already thrown the ball 90 times in two games, the second-most in the NFL. Despite this, Vele is in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Las Vegas defense that has yet to allow a receiving touchdown this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Devaughn Vele is likely to remain the Saints' second option at wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. While Jordan Tyson (hamstring) has been sidelined, Vele has been very fantasy-relevant, catching 15 of 22 targets for 172 yards and a touchdown (12.7 PPR points per game). Vele has almost no competition outside of Chris Olave in the Saints' WR room, which bodes well for his fantasy outlook going forward. Additionally, New Orleans' offense is averaging 44 pass attempts per game, which suggests Vele will continue having scoring opportunities. He's in for a favorable Week 4 matchup, as Atlanta's defense has allowed 604 receiving yards to wideouts this season, the most in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Vele is expected to open the season as New Orleans' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave until Jordyn Tyson returns from injury near midseason. Vele's first season with the Saints was marred with injuries. The 2024 seventh-round pick, who posted a 41-475-3 receiving line with Denver as a rookie, barely played throughout most of 2025 prior to taking on an every-down role during Weeks 10-15. In those five games (one of which he left hurt), he averaged 5.6 targets per game, but reached 12.0 fantasy points once (an 8-93-1 effort in Week 13 against Miami). The 28-year-old has yet to show he can be relied on for consistent targets and fantasy production, but he'll play an every-down role early on, which makes him a sleeper for flex value in deep leagues. He'll be worth a roster spot until Tyson returns.

outlooksByWeek.2: Wan'Dale Robinson had at least a share of the team lead in targets, catches, and receiving yards in his Titans debut, though he had a modest five catches for 38 yards on six targets. Tennessee's passing offense may not improve much, if at all, in Week 2 against an Eagles defense that allowed just six touchdowns to wide receivers last season, which tied for the fewest in the NFL. Robinson relies on target volume to make up for a lack of downfield playmaking capabilities, and the Titans may not throw often or effectively enough for him to make much of a fantasy difference. He's a low-end flex option for Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Wan'Dale Robinson is off to a slow start with the Titans, but he'll try to recapture his magic from last season with the Giants when he faces the Giants in Week 3. The shifty WR was peppered with short targets during his last couple seasons with the Giants, racking up 140 targets apiece in 2024 and 2025. After exceeding 1,000 receiving yards in 2025, Robinson signed a four-year, $78 million contract to join former Giants head coach and current Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll in Tennessee. Robinson is on pace for just 60 targets with his new team, so his involvement is likely to grow moving forward. It will be tough to trust Robinson until Tennessee's passing game shows some signs of life, but there is some deep-league fantasy flex appeal here for Week 3, especially in PPR formats, against a banged-up Giants secondary.
outlooksByWeek.4: Wan'Dale Robinson stepped up against his former team in Week 3 with seven catches for 57 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets against the Giants, but he had just 47 yards on seven targets in his first two games with the Titans. The 5-foot-8 wide receiver gets almost all of his production on short passes, but Robinson is a viable Week 4 flex option on the road against the heavily favored Ravens. The winless Titans may find themselves in another deep hole, which could allow Tennessee's low-octane passing game to make up for a lack of quality with quantity. Baltimore has allowed the second-most catches to wide receivers this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson signed with the Titans after catching 90-plus passes each of the past two seasons. The 2022 second-round pick has progressively improved his production each season in the pros, peaking with a 30% target share (ninth among WRs), 1,014 yards (13th) and 13.6 fantasy PPG (16th) in 2025. An undersized, short-range slot target, Robinson isn't positioned for many big plays and is very rarely used near the goal line (he's yet to clear four TDs in a season and has 13 career end zone targets). In Tennessee, Robinson will battle rookie Carnell Tate and Calvin Ridley for the team lead in targets, but his potential for flex production will depend on whether Cam Ward is able to make a Year 2 leap. Robinson, 25, is a low-ceiling, middle-round target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Alvin Kamara (knee) is expected to serve as one of the Saints' top running backs if active for the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Kamara was sidelined for Week 1 but is expected to return for Week 2, likely operating as the Saints' top receiving back. He could take work away from Travis Etienne, who caught seven of eight targets in last week's overtime loss. Tyler Shough attempted 56 passes in Week 1, which bodes well for Kamara's potential upside as a receiver. He's in for a solid Week 2 matchup as well, with the Ravens defense giving up 5.3 yards per touch to RBs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Alvin Kamara is expected to operate as the Saints' top pass-catching back in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. In his return from a sprained MCL in the Week 2 win over the Ravens, Kamara led the Saints' backfield in carries (nine), targets (six) and receptions (five). Despite this, Travis Etienne was more efficient with his opportunities, averaging 3.1 yards per carry compared to Kamara's 1.7. Even so, the Saints' backfield is in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Las Vegas defense that's allowed just 3.8 yards per carry thus far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Alvin Kamara will likely be in for a larger offensive role with Travis Etienne (hamstring)  sidelined for New Orleans' Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Kamara has received nine carries in each of the last two weeks after sitting out Week 1, but he's struggled with efficiency, averaging just 2.8 yards per carry. Additionally, he saw just one target in the Week 3 loss to the Raiders, suggesting he may not have the same receiving volume as in past years. Regardless, this receiving volume should increase with Etienne out for Week 4. Kamara could still struggle against a Falcons defense that's given up 13.5 PPR fantasy points per game to RBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Kamara is entering his age-31 season set to play a change-of-pace role behind Travis Etienne and is unlikely to be a fantasy option. Over the past seven seasons, only two backs age 31 or older have posted a top-30 fantasy campaign, and both required 16-plus touchdowns. (Kamara hasn't cleared nine TDs since 2020 and scored once in 2025). Injuries limited Kamara to career-low marks across the board last season (including a 10% target share, considerably worse than his previous career low of 18%), and he hasn't played a full season since his rookie year (2017). A longtime fantasy star, Kamara is worth no more than a late flier.
