The Cardinals gave up just 14 points in a surprising victory over the Chargers last weekend, though they did allow Los Angeles' No. 1 wideout Ladd McConkey to put up a 5-82-1 line in under three quarters of action before he exited with a rib injury.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashid Shaheed enters Seattle's Week 3 game against Washington on the heels of a quiet but versatile start to the season. Shaheed logged a modest three catches for 35 yards against Arizona in a Week 2 win, though he promisingly ranked second on the Seahawks with six targets, added a four-yard rush and combined for 76 yards on three punt returns and two kickoff returns. Jaxon Smith-Njigba appears set to dominate Seattle's targets for a second straight campaign, so both Shaheed and Cooper Kupp may have to settle for complementary roles on offense. Nonetheless, Seattle's WR corps as a whole could thrive in Week 3 against a Washington defense that has yielded a 73.0 percent catch rate to the position, tied for fifth-highest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rashid Shaheed has yet to make a big impact in fantasy this season with Seattle's Week 4 matchup against the Chargers coming up. Though Shaheed has been valuable as a return man for the Seahawks, he's averaging just two catches for 17.7 yards through three weeks. Shaheed also fell below a 50% offensive snap share in Week 3 against Washington, as Cooper Kupp served as the team's No. 2 wide receiver behind star Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Shaheed may need a big play or two to break out against the Chargers, who have allowed nine receptions of 20-plus yards this season, tied for 13th-most in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Shaheed re-signed with Seattle after the team acquired him at last year's trade deadline. Known primarily for his elite return ability, Shaheed made an impact at times as a receiver with New Orleans, but wasn't used much on offense after the trade. In 12 games with the Seahawks (including the playoffs), Shaheed cleared three touches in only two games and averaged 5.9 fantasy PPG. The team's financial investment in Shaheed suggests his role will expand in 2026, but he still has to fend off Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp and second-year WR Tory Horton for snaps and targets. Shaheed enters his age-28 season yet to deliver a top-35 fantasy campaign, and he's unlikely to get there this season while also focusing on special teams and working in Seattle's low-pass-volume offense.

Tyson was selected by the Saints with the No. 8 overall pick of April's draft. He is a versatile receiver with decent size who led this rookie class with a 35% target share during the nine weeks he was active in 2025. Injuries cost him time during all four collegiate seasons, but he still managed a 158-2,282-22 receiving line in 33 games, posting a strong 2.73 YPRR along the way (third best in this class). Tyson suffered a hamstring injury in August and will miss a month or two of the regular season prior to taking over as the Saints' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave. Once healthy, Tyson has a path to a substantial role in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough and could find himself on the WR3 radar. Of course, with the injury, he's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Spencer Shrader made a 58-yard field goal but also missed an extra point in a confounding performance during the Colts' season-opening loss. The big-legged kicker may not get many opportunities in Week 2 against the Chiefs, especially since the Colts are one of the league's most efficient red-zone teams thanks to the presence of star RB Jonathan Taylor. Shrader is a middling fantasy option, and you can likely find a kicker in a more appealing situation on your league's waiver wire.
outlooksByWeek.3: Spencer Shrader has made all four of his field-goal attempts and five of six extra point tries through two games this season. The Colts are averaging a robust 26.5 points per game, but their success on offense has been overshadowed by a league-worst defensive performance en route to a 0-2 start. Shrader is gaining some streaming appeal heading into a Week 3 home game against the Texans, who are allowing 28.0 points per game in the early going after giving up just 17.4 points per game last season. He's a borderline fantasy starter at this point.
outlooksByWeek.4: Spencer Shrader is coming off a heroic performance in the Colts' 19-17 Week 3 win over the Texans, as the kicker overcame an early groin injury to make all four of his field-goal attempts, including a go-ahead 53-yarder with 16 seconds left in the fourth quarter. He's off to an 8-for-8 start this season and has made kicks from as deep as 58 yards. Shrader is making a case for a starting fantasy kicker role, and he'll have a chance to showcase his skills on the international stage in Week 4, when the Colts face the Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. Scoring opportunities are likely to be plentiful for Shrader since Washington is giving up 30.7 points per game.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Boswell and the Steelers are on the road to face the Patriots in Week 2. He finished Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 win versus the Falcons 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts and 2-for-2 on PATs. Boswell's first miss of the season was from 56 yards out, but he was able to connect from 43 and 28 yards. The Steelers have several talented players on offense, but until they prove they can consistently put up 24-28 points a week, Boswell may not generate enough scoring opportunities to warrant a roster spot.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Boswell and the Steelers host the Bengals in Week 3. The 12th-year kicker went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to New England. Both of Boswell's attempts came from 50-plus yards out, and he's now 1-for-3 from that distance and 3-for-5 overall through two outings in 2026. He'll look to get back on track this Sunday versus a Cincinnati defense allowing 16.5 points per game, tied for eighth.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Boswell and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He made all three of his field-goal attempts and went 3-for-3 on PATs during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. It was Boswell's first perfect outing through three games, and his 33-yard kick just before the two-minute warning gave the Steelers the lead for good. He'll look to stay hot against Cleveland's 18th-ranked scoring defense, which is allowing 23.7 points per game thus far in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Micah Parsons' health has a bearing on the performance of this defense; it was 13th in fantasy points across the 13 games before his ACL tear, but had a negative score in four games without him. Tuck that away before diving head first into the team's soft September schedule (@MIN, @NYJ, ATL the first three weeks), though those are matchups that make this defense well worth streaming consideration.

Hill is currently a free agent after being released by Miami. One of the top fantasy players of the past decade, Hill's best days may be behind him as he enters his age-32 campaign. The former fifth-round pick was fantasy's top-scoring receiver from 2017-23, but struggled to an 18th-place finish in 2024 (31st PPG) and then suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 4 of last season. If he's able to play in 2026, Hill may still be able to hit for the occasional explosive play, but considering his age and the major injury, his ceiling is likely that of a boom/bust flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cairo Santos will aim to stay perfect as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Santos was on the field a lot in Week 1 against the Panthers, but most of his 11 points came from his eight PATs. The veteran kicker could continue to benefit from a high-scoring offense, and he'll look to continue against a Minnesota squad that allowed three field goals and an extra point to Trey Smack this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cairo Santos will aim to do more as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Santos made his first field-goal attempt against the Vikings in Week 2, but his second chance for a tie was blocked in the fourth quarter. The veteran kicker's potential for the rest of the season remains up in the air following the injury to Caleb Williams, but an inexperienced Tyson Bagent could get the field-goal team on the field more often rather than finding the end zone. Philly has allowed 6.0 fantasy points per game to kickers this year, a top-10 mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cairo Santos will aim to stay solid as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Santos nailed both of his field-goal attempts and went three-for-three on PATs in Week 3 against the Eagles. The veteran kicker has now made all but one of his field-goal tries and all 10 XPAs in the first three games of the season. He'll face a Jets squad that's allowed a top-ten 6.3 fantasy points per game to kickers.

player.seasonOutlook: Anthony Campanile's defense was one of the most surprisingly productive of 2025, finishing fifth in fantasy points, and the team was fortunate to get him back for this year. That said, the team had modest sack and fumble recovery numbers, and it did lose LB Devin Lloyd and CB Greg Newsome over the offseason. Fantasy managers can still freely select this defense, knowing it has one of the best opening-week matchups by hosting the Browns, but they'll likely need to swap them out for Weeks 2 through 6 (@DEN, NE, @CIN, PHI, HOU).

outlooksByWeek.2: De'Zhaun Stribling isn't likely to play in San Francisco's Week 2 matchup versus Miami. Stribling suffered an ankle injury during his NFL debut last Thursday against the Rams and is expected to miss at least a month of action. While he's out, Demarcus Robinson is slated to take on the 49ers' No. 3 wideout role.

player.seasonOutlook: Stribling was selected by the 49ers with the 33rd overall pick in April's draft. Stribling had a productive collegiate run, catching 44-plus passes in four of his five seasons, three of which came with different schools. That production included 52-882-6 and 55-811-6 receiving lines at Oklahoma State and Ole Miss over the past two seasons. Stribling primarily worked as a perimeter receiver and peaked with a 22% target share with OSU in 2024. His overall efficiency is pedestrian, but he has good size and speed (4.36 40-yard dash at the combine) and is a plus blocker. Stribling has plenty competition for Year 1 targets (Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey), so a slow start is possible, but it's likely he'll eventually find his way to a bigger role and fantasy relevance. He's a fine mid-round upside pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Washington hopes for more efficiency when the Dolphins face the 49ers in Week 2. Washington recorded a healthy eight targets in the team's opener, and while 17.7 yards per catch is encouraging, he caught only three balls. Washington has value as a returner in some leagues, and passing volume will likely remain high with Miami forced to throw from behind in the second half. Even so, Week 2's matchup against a defense that held more talented receivers to just 6.4 yards per target in their opener is a risky endeavor.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malik Washington brings steady volume ahead of the Dolphins' Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. With Malik Willis under center, Miami has completed just 29 passes through two games, but seven have gone to Washington, who's averaging 6.5 targets. Kansas City's rebuilt secondary has been terrific through two games, allowing just 204 yards to opposing wideouts. Washington seems unlikely to produce any massive numbers, but he also appears to be a steady cog in this limited offense, keeping him on WR3/Flex radars.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malik Washington remains heavily involved in the Dolphins' low-profile passing game heading into Week 4 against the Vikings. Washington is coming off of a season-high 10 targets in Week 3, and has collected three rushing attempts over the last two weeks while also being involved in kickoff returns, but he's yet to top 61 rushing/receiving yards per game or score. Washington's workload creates a viable floor, and Minnesota is allowing a healthy 8.2 yards per target to opposing receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Washington was a sixth-round flier back in 2024, but that didn't stop him from working his way into a substantial offensive role last season. Washington finished third on the Dolphins in targets, trailing only Jaylen Waddle and De'Von Achane. Of course, Miami's shaky group of offensive personnel was an obvious factor and Washington's efficiency wasn't very good (5.0 yards per target, 7.0 yards per reception, 0.9 yards per route run). The 25-year-old is fine as a short-range target and occasional rusher, but that's likely his ceiling with newcomers Jalen Tolbert, Chris Bell, Caleb Douglas and Kevin Coleman Jr. expected to factor in at wide receiver.

Dell is on the comeback trail after suffering a devastating knee injury late in 2024 that cost him the entire 2025 season. It was a tough break for the 2023 third-round pick, who finished 18th among receivers in fantasy PPG as a rookie. While he wasn't quite as productive the next season, he was on pace for career highs in catches and yardage. The undersized Dell is certainly a question mark off the major injury, but, with Jayden Higgins out for the 2026 season, he has a path back to a role behind Nico Collins at some point this year. The 26-year-old will begin on injured reserve, but he'll be a fine end-of-bench stash once activated.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Allgeier heads into a Week 2 clash against Seattle with a big role in Arizona's backfield. Allgeier logged 17 carries for 61 yards in a season-opening win against the Chargers, getting more totes and producing more yards than rookie Jeremiyah Love. It remains to be seen if that will hold true throughout the campaign, but for the time being Allgeier seems set to be heavily involved in the Cardinals' ground game. With that said, both Allgeier and Love could find the sledding tough in Week 2 versus a Seahawks defense that yielded the third-fewest rushing yards per game during the regular season last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Allgeier will seek to improve his efficiency on the ground during Arizona's Week 3 visit to San Francisco. Allgeier gained just 10 yards on five carries Sunday in a loss against Seattle, and he's averaging a meager 3.2 YPC through two contests. He paced the Cardinals with 17 carries in the team's season opener, but  Jeremiyah Love jumped ahead with him with nine carries Week 2 and could continue to settle in as the club's clear No. 1 RB moving forward. The 49ers have yielded 4.04 YPC to running backs so far, but that's led to just one rushing TD.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Allgeier seems to have fallen well behind Jeremiyah Love for ball-carrying opportunities heading into Arizona's Week 4 matchup with the Giants. Love carried the ball 21 times against San Francisco this past Sunday, while Allgeier handled a season-low two totes. The latter did reel in a season-best four catches, but they amounted to just 10 receiving yards. Though the Giants are struggling against the run, ranking in the bottom half of the league in allowing 18.5 fantasy points per game to RBs, Allgeier will likely need to see more opportunities in order to make an impact.

player.seasonOutlook: Allgeier signed with the Cardinals during free agency. The 2022 fifth-round NFL draft pick impressed as a rookie in Atlanta, totaling 1,174 yards on 226 touches, but he hasn't come close to those marks while playing second fiddle to Bijan Robinson over the past three seasons, and he has yet to produce a top-25 fantasy campaign. Allgeier did score eight touchdowns last season, but he remains a nonfactor as a receiver, never clearing 18 catches in a season. The 26-year-old will step into a similar role in Arizona, as the primary backup and change-of-pace option behind No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love. Same as in Atlanta, Allgeier has no standalone value, but he's a very good insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chase McLaughlin will look to remain perfect in the Buccaneers' Week 2 matchup against the Browns. McLaughlin made all five of his kicks during last week's loss, including a 51-yard field goal. With the Browns defense allowing 34 total points and 10 kicking points in a Week 1 loss, McLaughlin is likely in for lots more scoring opportunities in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chase McLaughlin could remain one of the top kickers in fantasy despite the Buccaneers' tough Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. McLaughlin remained perfect in the Week 2 loss to the Browns, as he's now converted on all six field-goal tries this season, including two from 50-plus yards. Despite McLaughlin being tied for the league-lead in field-goals made this season, he could struggle against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 6.5 kicking points per game thus far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chase McLaughlin is expected to remain one of fantasy's top kickers in the Buccaneers' Week 4 matchup against the Packers. McLaughlin remained perfect in the Week 3 loss to the Vikings, converting on all four of his kicks, including a 54-yard field goal. He's now made all nine of his field-goal tries and all five point-after attempts through three weeks. If Baker Mayfield (thumb) were to miss the Week 4 contest, McLaughlin may have fewer scoring opportunities. However, he's still in for a relatively favorable matchup with the Packers allowing 7.0 kicking points per game this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Adonai Mitchell will look to stretch the field for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. Mitchell hauled in all three of his targets to open the year, finishing with 60 yards. Green Bay allowed a mere 7.7 yards per target in Week 1, but that was largely due to facing Carson Wentz for the bulk of the game. Their secondary remains vulnerable and will likely commit multiple bodies to Garrett Wilson, setting up Mitchell for a few plays downfield in single coverage. Mitchell seems likely to continue his low-volume, high-upside role in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Adonai Mitchell hopes for a continued elevated workload in Week 3 when the Jets face the Lions. After just three targets in a run-heavy Week 1, Mitchell logged an eye-opening 12 targets in Week 2, with the Jets throwing 41 times. Detroit's defense has been a fantasy bonanza for opposing offenses, allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to wideouts. Assuming the Lions score plenty themselves, the Jets should throw heavily, giving Mitchell ample opportunities for a big play or two.
outlooksByWeek.4: Adonai Mitchell is questionable for the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears after missing Week 3 due to a finger injury. Mitchell has been a valuable secondary option opposite Garrett Wilson in his first two games, garnering 15 targets and averaging 13.7 yards per catch. With minimal options behind him and running back Breece Hall (thigh) likely to miss Week 4, Mitchell could have a stable workload against a defense that's allowing 8.5 yards per target to opposing receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Mitchell is entering his first full campaign with the Jets, having been acquired in the Sauce Gardner trade during the 2025 season. After playing sparingly during his first 25 NFL games (all with the Colts), the 2024 second-round pick handled a hefty 24.4% target share in eight games with New York last season. The usage led to two fantasy outings with 17-plus points, but he was otherwise a nonfactor (4.0 PPG). Efficiency remains an issue, as Mitchell's 44% catch rate ranks last, and his 6.0 yards per target is fourth worst among 77 receivers with 100-plus targets since he entered the league. The vertical threat will compete with rookie Omar Cooper Jr. for No. 2 duties opposite a now-healthy Garrett Wilson in the Jets' Geno Smith-led offense. Mitchell, 23, is not worth much more than late-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brian Robinson is expected to operate as the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Despite playing behind Bijan Robinson, Brian Robinson could have material fantasy value this week, as Carolina's defense allowed 291 rushing yards and six touchdowns in Week 1. Additionally, Robinson received nine carries in the Week 1 loss to the Steelers, which is solid volume for a complementary role. He could find value with the Panthers giving up 52.8 PPR fantasy points to the running back position last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brian Robinson (ankle) will operate as the Falcons' No. 2 running back if active for the Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Robinson logged 13 touches in Atlanta's Week 2 loss to the Panthers, but eight of those came in the fourth quarter -- suggesting he's still firmly the second option at RB. The Alabama product has been efficient, however, averaging 4.1 yards per carry through two weeks. He's also in for a favorable matchup, with the Packers defense allowing 22.9 PPR fantasy per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brian Robinson is expected to continue operating as the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Robinson had his best performance of the season in the Week 3 win over the Packers, rushing 10 times for 50 yards and a touchdown. Despite playing behind Bijan Robinson, Brian Robinson has managed to be extremely efficient when given opportunities, averaging 4.6 yards per touch. He's also in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a New Orleans defense that's given up 4.8 yards per carry this season.

player.seasonOutlook: After a one-year stint as Christian McCaffrey's backup in San Francisco, Robinson signed with Atlanta where he'll now operate as a change-of-pace back behind Bijan Robinson. The 2022 third-round pick soaked up 200-plus touches in each of his first three NFL seasons (all with Washington) prior to dipping to 100 touches in 2025. Robinson is a big back who can handle early-down and short-yardage work, but he's not much of a factor as a receiver (92 career targets). He's yet to post a top-20 fantasy campaign and he won't come close to that in 2026 unless Bijan Robinson suffers a major injury. The 27-year-old back is no more than a solid insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Wright's role in the Dolphins' offense is limited entering a Week 2 matchup against the 49ers. Despite being their No. 2 back, Wright played just 6% of their offensive snaps to De'Von Achane's 88%. With Miami likely falling behind early and being forced to pass, Wright is far more insurance for Achane managers than a viable fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Wright's role is limited in the Dolphins' backfield entering a Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. He has logged just seven snaps through two games and is now dealing with a stinger issue that makes him uncertain to play. With no clear immediate path to touches, Wright is an insurance policy in a matchup against a defense allowing 4.0 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Wright will have an elevated role for the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings if he's able to overcome a foot issue that kept him out last Sunday. Miami lost De'Von Achane for the season due to a knee injury, leaving just Wright and Ollie Gordon to handle carries. With the Dolphins falling behind often in most matchups, Wright has the chance to be the better pass-catching option of the two. Facing a Vikings defense that's allowing just 3.1 ypc and 11 catches to running backs to date however doesn't inspire confidence.

player.seasonOutlook: Wright will once again compete with second-year Ollie Gordon II for backup reps behind feature back De'Von Achane. Wright has barely cleared 70 touches during each of his first two NFL seasons, but he has shined at times, including a 24-107-1 rushing line in Week 14 last season. The 2024 fourth-round pick has been effective as a rusher, but hasn't been involved in the passing game (15 targets in 25 games). The 23-year-old would be worth adding only in the event of an Achane injury and even then, it's possible he would split (or be on the short end of a committee) with Gordon in a rebuilding offense that may not score very often.

outlooksByWeek.3: Jonah Coleman didn't see the ball in his NFL debut during the Broncos' opener, but his role increased in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to RJ Harvey's hamstring strain. Coleman ended up getting more touches than J.K. Dobbins, with the 2026 fourth-round pick turning 10 carries into 39 yards and his first career touchdown while also catching all three of his targets for 19 yards. It's not clear how much time Harvey might miss, but Coleman's solid showing in his first opportunity could begin the process of turning the backfield into a three-man committee, with the workload dependent on whoever happens to be healthy. Coleman could be a risky play in Week 3 against a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Coleman was selected by the Broncos in the fourth round of April's draft. He is a 220-pound back who was highly efficient during four collegiate seasons at Arizona and Washington. Coleman didn't get much pre-contact help (1.80 YBC), but he made up for it after contact (3.73 YAC ranks second in this rookie RB class) and his career 3.4 forced missed tackle rate is best in this class. Also solid as a receiver and blocker, Coleman has three-down ability, but may not get that opportunity until 2027. The rookie will begin his career behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. Coleman should be added only if Dobbins or Harvey goes down with an injury.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens host the Saints in Week 2. Despite leading Baltimore's receivers with 53 offensive snaps, he logged just one target and did not record a reception. With Zay Flowers' (hamstring) status up in the air and rookie Ja'Kobi Lane out with a fractured wrist suffered in the opener, Bateman's opportunities to contribute could increase. Regardless of who's active, he'll aim to bounce back against New Orleans' 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (37.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 3 matchup against the Cowboys. In the absence of top wideout Zay Flowers (hamstring), Bateman caught seven of nine targets for 88 yards and a touchdown during Baltimore's Week 2 loss. He'll likely slide back to a supporting role if Flowers is able to suit up this Sunday. However, if he's unable to do so, Bateman will have the chance to replicate his solid outing versus a Dallas defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game (31.2) allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens return home to host the 0-3 Titans in Week 4. He caught two of three targets for 37 yards during Baltimore's 34-31 win in Week 3, finishing second on the team in yardage. However, with Zay Flowers (hamstring) returning from a one-game absence, Bateman saw his involvement dip heavily after posting a 7-88-1 line in Week 2's loss. Flowers paced the Ravens in receptions, targets, and yardage, and as long as he remains healthy, managers can expect Bateman to see similar results against Tennessee's 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (32.9) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Bateman is entering his sixth season in Baltimore following an injury-plagued 2025 campaign in which he was limited to a career-low 224 receiving yards in 13 games. After scoring nine touchdowns on only 45 receptions in 2024, Bateman had "regression" written all over him entering last season, but it was worse than expected. The 2021 first-round pick saw his target share fall from 15.4% to a career-low 11.4% and his only double-digit fantasy effort came in Week 3. The 26-year-old remains second on Baltimore's depth chart behind Zay Flowers, but even in a new scheme and with a healthy Lamar Jackson under center, he's unlikely to produce his first top-35 fantasy campaign. Bateman isn't the most appealing late-round draft pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Daniel Jones is unlikely to post gaudy passing numbers in the Colts' run-first offense, and he doesn't appear interested in using his legs as much after tearing his Achilles in Week 14 of last season. His fantasy appeal is limited to multi-QB or superflex formats, and Jones is a low-end option even in those leagues for a Week 2 matchup against a Chiefs defense that held Bo Nix to 131 passing yards in Week 1. Jones had just 166 passing yards with a 1:1 TD:INT and one carry for four yards in the Colts' 41-23 Week 1 loss to the Ravens.
outlooksByWeek.3: Daniel Jones is averaging 188 passing yards per game heading into the Colts' Week 3 home game against the Texans. Houston gave up two touchdown passes apiece to star QBs Josh Allen and Joe Burrow, but Jones will be hard-pressed to post his first multi-TD performance of the season considering the Texans boast one of the league's best defenses, having allowed the fewest yards in the NFL last season. The Colts will continue to rely primarily on the legs of star RB Jonathan Taylor, and Indianapolis has an underwhelming group of pass catchers that's expected to be without last season's leading receiver Alec Pierce (heel) for several weeks. Jones has been a non-factor as a rusher since returning from a torn Achilles, with just 14 rushing yards this season. His mediocre passing stats make him an unappealing Week 3 fantasy option, even in multi-QB formats.
outlooksByWeek.4: Daniel Jones led the Colts to their first win since Week 10 of the 2025 season in Week 3 against the Texans, but he has just three touchdown passes and five turnovers heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. Jones, who underwent surgery to repair a torn Achilles in December, hasn't been much of a factor with his legs, rushing for just 19 yards and has yet to score a rushing TD after notching five last season. Washington has allowed a league-high 11 passing TDs, so while Jones will be tough to trust as a starter in one-QB formats with the Colts missing last season's leading receiver Alec Pierce (heel; IR), he's a viable option in superflex or multi-QB leagues.

player.seasonOutlook: Jones re-signed with the Colts during the offseason and will return as the team's starter. The 2019 No. 6 draft pick made a big leap in 2025 -- his first season with Indianapolis -- finishing no lower than seventh in completion percentage and yards per attempt. Despite the strong play, Jones was inconsistent as a fantasy option, averaging 18.8 fantasy points during 12 full games and posting three top-five weeks but no additional finishes better than ninth. Jones was effective through the air and scored five rushing TDs, but he didn't run the ball as much as in years past and might do even less of that in 2026 after tearing an Achilles in Week 14. He's likely to be ready for Week 1, but effectiveness is a concern, so he's best viewed as a midrange QB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isiah Pacheco will miss Week 2 as the Lions travel to Buffalo. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he recently underwent surgery. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle whatever RB2 duties are available behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isiah Pacheco will remain sidelined in Week 3 as the Lions take on the Jets. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he recently underwent surgery. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy as the season progresses. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle any RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isiah Pacheco will remain out in Week 4 as Detroit faces Carolina. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy as the season progresses. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle any RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs in the meantime.

player.seasonOutlook: Pacheco signed with Detroit in the offseason after a four-year stint with the Chiefs. The 2022 seventh-round NFL draft pick opened his pro career with a bang, totaling 2,139 yards and 14 touchdowns on 432 touches during his first two seasons (31 games). Injuries and a big drop in efficiency have limited him to 952 yards and three TDs on 232 touches over the past two seasons (20 games) and ultimately led to his exit from Kansas City. The 27-year-old will now get a shot to replace David Montgomery as Detroit's change-of-pace back to Jahmyr Gibbs. Pacheco might hit for the occasional touchdown, but he won't have standalone fantasy value unless Gibbs misses time. Consider Pacheco a late-round insurance flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Washington's volume was limited in his NFL debut, but he was productive, gaining 41 rushing yards on seven carries in the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins. The quality of his opposition needs to be taken into account, but it was still a strong showing from the 2026 fourth-round pick. Lead back Ashton Jeanty had a huge game, proving he was fully recovered from a preseason ankle injury, but if he has trouble staying on the field, Washington appears very capable of stepping into a larger role. He'll face a tough matchup in Week 2 against a Chargers defense that ranked second in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Washington hasn't seen much action to begin his NFL career, getting 10 carries through the Raiders' first two games and turning them into 48 yards. He also failed to bring in his only target. Ashton Jeanty is locked into the top spot in the backfield and has 54 touches, third in the league behind only Jahmyr Gibbs and Kenneth Walker, and unless he gets hurt, Washington's workload figures to be limited. The rookie will look to take advantage of the chances he does get in Week 3 against a Saints defense that ranks in the bottom four in rushing yards and rushing TDs allowed to RBs so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Washington showed off his big-play potential in the Raiders' Week 3 win over the Saints, turning one of his five carries into a 36-yard touchdown. The rookie fourth-round pick hasn't logged big volume behind Ashton Jeanty, but that could begin to change if the starting RB continues to average just 3.3 yards per carry, compared to Washington's 6.8 mark. Until his workload ticks up, Washington will be little more than a dart throw or bench stash for fantasy rosters. He'll face a Kansas City defense in Week 4 that ranks 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Washington was selected by the Raiders in the fourth round of April's draft. He's a big back with terrific speed who lit up the combine with a 4.33 40-yard dash at 6-foot-1, 223 pounds (127 speed score), while also checking in with the longest arms in this rookie RB class. His collegiate efficiency wasn't very good during stops in Buffalo and New Mexico State, but it was better in 2025 -- his lone season at Arkansas -- as he averaged 6.41 yards per carry and 3.62 yards after contact, both of which rank seventh or better in this RB class. He might not be much of an option in the passing game, as his career 4.2 yards per target is the worst in this RB class, but his traits make him an intriguing prospect. Washington will open his career as a clear No. 2 option behind Ashton Jeanty, which makes him an intriguing end-of-bench insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.3: Marcus Mariota will likely start for the Commanders in Week 3, as starter Jayden Daniels dislocated the same elbow that he previously injured last season. Mariota relieved Daniels in the second half in Week 2 versus the Cowboys, throwing for 111 yards and a touchdown. He will have his work cut out for him versus a devastating Seattle defense that is allowing just 8.5 points and 214 scrimmage yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt.
outlooksByWeek.4: Marcus Mariota led an improbable Washington victory over the defending Super Bowl champions last game. Mariota tossed three touchdowns in the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. Jayden Daniels is set to practice with the Commanders as the squad heads to London for Week 4, though he is unlikely to play versus the Colts due to his dislocated elbow.  Whoever lines up under center will have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Colts pass defense. Indianapolis is allowing 276 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: A middling, matchups-driven D/ST last season, the Buccaneers saw much change among their linebacker corps during the offseason. Lavonte David retired, and the team drafted Rueben Bain Jr. 15th overall and signed Alex Anzalone and Christian Rozeboom. Take a wait-and-see approach to how the new personnel jells, especially since the Buccaneers get a tough opening matchup in a road game against the Bengals.

outlooksByWeek.2: Emmett Johnson contributed in his NFL debut, gaining 24 yards on eight carries and catching both his targets for 44 yards in a season-opening win over the Broncos. Kansas City leaned heavily on its ground game, with Kenneth Walker having a career-best day on 26 touches. Johnson's volume may be repeatable if this proves to be the team's offensive formula in 2026 and they continue building big second-half leads. Johnson will look to take advantage of his opportunities in Week 2 against a Colts defense that was just steamrolled by Derrick Henry but ranked 11th in points per game allowed to RBs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Emmett Johnson logged only four touches as Kenneth Walker's primary backup in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, as the fifth-round rookie continues to get his feet wet in the NFL. Johnson also saw a little work as a kickoff returner as the team looks to find ways to get the ball in his hands. As long as Walker is healthy, Johnson's workload will remain limited, but he's flashed some big-play potential in the early going with 64 receiving yards on just four catches. He'll face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground so far in 2026, allowing 3.5 yards per carry, which ranks sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Emmett Johnson remains in a limited role behind Kenneth Walker in the Kansas City backfield. Through three games, the fifth-round rookie has only 20 touches-16 carries and four receptions-but has managed to turn that into 120 scrimmage yards. Coach Andy Reid has hinted that Johnson's workload will increase as the season wears on, but as yet there's been no actual sign of that happening. Johnson will be a dart throw, albeit one with big-play upside, in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that is tied for 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and has given up just one touchdown to the position so far in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson was selected by the Chiefs in the fifth round of April's draft. His career 3.4 forced missed tackle rate is fourth best in this RB rookie class and his elusiveness helped him to 1,451 rushing yards (fourth in the nation and first in this class) last season. His lack of speed -- last among 10 RBs who ran the 40-yard dash (4.56) and speed score (93) at the combine -- and size limits him after initial contact (career 2.86 YAC), but he can help out in the passing game (92 collegiate receptions). Johnson and Brashard Smith are set to handle No. 2/3 duties behind Kenneth Walker III. Smith will be worth rostering only if Walker misses action.

outlooksByWeek.3: Terrance Ferguson is coming off a big game as the Rams prepare to face Denver in Week 3. Ferguson notched six catches on nine targets for 54 yards and a touchdown on Monday Night Football, trailing only star wideout Davante Adams in receptions, targets and receiving yards. That followed Ferguson's quiet Week 1 performance, when he didn't catch his only target. Repeating Monday's big effort could be tough for Ferguson in Week 3, as he'll face a Broncos defense that limited Jacksonville's tight ends to a modest 24 receiving yards Sunday.

player.seasonOutlook: Ferguson is a potential breakout candidate in his second NFL season. As expected, the 2025 second-rounder played a situational role behind the likes of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen as a rookie. He didn't get much run, but when he did, he was used as a vertical threat to the extreme. His 17.5 aDOT is highest by any tight end (minimum 10 targets) in at least a decade. The Rams are returning the same tight end room plus second-round pick Max Klare, so while consistent production could prove elusive, Ferguson very well could emerge as the No. 3 pass catcher behind Puka Nacua and 33-year-old Davante Adams in the Rams' elite offense. The 23-year-old, who also saw five end zone targets as a rookie, is worth a late-round lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.2: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers hope to improve to 2-0 when they visit the Patriots in Week 2. He secured all five targets for 46 yards and Aaron Rodgers' lone passing TD, and finished second on the team in receiving yards while tying for first in receptions. Freiermuth led Pittsburgh's TEs in offensive snaps (49), but Darnell Washington was a close second with 43. He and the Steelers will try to scheme up a way to beat a New England defense that is tied for second in receiving yards allowed to the position (13).
outlooksByWeek.3: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers play host to the Bengals for an AFC North clash in Week 3. He paced the team's tight ends in snaps (46), receptions (4), yards (32) and targets (5) during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to the Patriots. Freiermuth appears to have the upper hand over Darnell Washington (1-7-0) in the passing game, but his fantasy floor and ceiling are relatively low in an underwhelming Steelers offense. He'll have the added benefit of facing a Cincinnati defense that allows 18.5 fantasy points per game to TEs (27th) and just got torched for 12 receptions and 140 yards by Dalton Schultz.
outlooksByWeek.4: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 4 AFC North clash against the Browns. He caught two of four targets for 30 yards and rushed once for one yard during Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory. Aaron Rodgers continues to spread the ball around, as six different Steelers receivers registered at least four targets, and four tied for the team lead in receptions with three. Freiermuth could be a sneaky play versus a Cleveland defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (14.9) to TEs and gave up eight receptions (on 12 targets) for 92 yards to the position in Week 3.

player.seasonOutlook: Freiermuth's career trajectory has been quite the head-scratcher, but the bottom line is he is yet to emerge as a consistent fantasy starter. The 2021 second-round pick flirted with TE1 status in both 2022 (11th in fantasy PPG) and 2024 (14th) but saw a dramatic dip in usage in Pittsburgh's crowded tight end room in 2025. Freiermuth posted a career-low 10% target share and finished outside the top 20 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and end zone targets, and 30 tight ends bested his 6.7 fantasy PPG. The 27-year-old figures to play more in 2026 with Jonnu Smith gone and Mike McCarthy running the offense, but Pittsburgh is also better at wide receiver with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard in the fold. Freiermuth has some sleeper appeal, but he's best valued as a back-end TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Caleb Douglas will look to build on his Week 1 emergence when the Dolphins face the 49ers in Week 2. Douglas logged an impressive five catches for 94 yards in his NFL debut, garnering seven targets. Miami will likely continue to pass while playing from behind on a weekly basis, and it appears Douglas and QB Malik Willis have a solid connection. San Francisco's defense was stingy against the pass to open the year, allowing just 6.4 yards per target, but volume can reign supreme and Douglas appears to have that potential, making him an intriguing Week 2 option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Caleb Douglas' status for the Dolphins' Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs is uncertain due to an ankle injury. Douglas played a hefty 85% of the team's offensive snaps before suffering the injury late in Week 2 but recorded just 19 yards after a 94-yard career debut. Should he play, Douglas is a speculative upside play for fantasy teams in need of Week 3 help.
outlooksByWeek.4: Caleb Douglas will need to overcome an ankle injury keeping him out of Week 3 to help the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings. After an impressive Week 1, Douglas recorded only three targets in Week 2 despite an 86% snap share. Malik Willis' play under center remains shaky, leading to inconsistency among Miami's receivers. Willis will be scrambling facing a blitz-heavy Vikings defense, but they are allowing generous 8.2 yards per target to opposing wideouts if Douglas is able to push downfield.

player.seasonOutlook: Douglas was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. Douglas is a tall, perimeter receiver with big hands and long arms who, after not seeing much work during two seasons at Florida, exploded for 60-877-6 and 54-846-7 receiving lines at Texas Tech over the last two seasons. His overall efficiency was underwhelming, including six drops and a shaky 1.81 YPRR in 2025. He impressed with a 4.39 40-yard dash at 206 pounds (111 speed score) at the combine. Douglas has a path to a large offensive role as a rookie (Malik Washington, Jalen Tolbert and fellow rookie Chris Bell are his primary competition), but life may be tough in a rebuilding Miami offense led by unproven Malik Willis. He's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Keaton Mitchell couldn't capitalize on his preseason buzz in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals. He got only four carries, turning them into a mere nine yards, and failed to see a target. The former Raven is the clear backup to Omarion Hampton in the backfield, but Mitchell may need much more favorable game scripts to get meaningful volume. He'll try to contribute in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 21st last season in points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Keaton Mitchell has taken a clear backseat to Omarion Hampton in the Chargers' backfield to begin the season, getting 10 touches to his teammate's 37 through two games. Mitchell has yet to do much to earn a larger role, averaging just 3.7 yards per carry, although he does have a 15-yard gain on his only catch. Hampton has lost a fumble in each game so far in 2026, and these ball security issues could open the door for Mitchell to get more involved. If he does see more volume in Week 3, Mitchell could hit paydirt against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.
outlooksByWeek.4: Keaton Mitchell could be moving into a bigger role in the Chargers' backfield. While the offense as a whole is struggling, the former Raven logged a season-high eight carries in Week 3 and turned them into 52 rushing yards. He also made his first trip to the end zone in 2026, getting a one-yard shovel pass from Justin Herbert on a jet sweep. Omarion Hampton is struggling to adapt to new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme, and that's opening the door for Mitchell to push his way into a timeshare in the backfield. However, neither back is likely to make a splash in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mitchell signed with the Chargers after spending his first three NFL seasons with Baltimore. The 2023 UDFA will compete with Kimani Vidal for change-of-pace touches behind starter Omarion Hampton. Mitchell has been limited to 140 touches over his first three NFL seasons, but he has been extremely productive when called upon. His career 6.34 yards per carry ranks second and his 2.50 YAC fourth among 89 backs with 100-plus carries since 2023. He has also put up 184 yards on 23 targets (8.0 YPT). Mitchell is on the small side, so his ceiling is likely capped (he has never cleared 11 touches in a game), but the 24-year-old would be worth adding should Hampton miss time.

Chris O'Leary takes the helm as Chargers defensive coordinator, a year after this unit finished 11th in fantasy points (119). With stars like Khalil Mack, Derwin James Jr. and Tuli Tuipulotu on the roster, the Chargers should again put forth solid defensive numbers, health willing. But the biggest advantage here is the team's first-two-weeks' schedule: The Chargers host the Cardinals and Raiders, two of the most favorable D/ST matchups. Just beware that things get far tougher from there (@BUF, @SEA, DEN, @KC the next four weeks).

outlooksByWeek.2: Trey Smack will look to stay solid as the Packers take on the Jets in Week 2. Smack converted all three of his field-goal attempts against the Vikings in Week 1, but he did go 1-for-2 on XPAs. Still, the perfect field-goal percentage outshines his one miss. Smack will face a Jets defense that allowed a bottom-five fantasy points (4.0) total to Titans kicker Joey Slye this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trey Smack will aim to stay perfect as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Smack went perfect in Week 2 against the Jets, nailing two PATs and two field-goal tries, including a game-winner. The rookie kicker has now gone a perfect five-for-five on field goals and made all but one of his four extra-point attempts. He'll take on an Atlanta team that's allowed 9.0 fantasy points per game to kickers on the year, a bottom-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Trey Smack will have a favorable matchup as the Packers travel to Tampa Bay in Week 4. Smack went 2-for-2 on extra-point tries in Week 3 against the Falcons, but he also had his sole field-goal attempt blocked. The rookie kicker will seek to get back on track versus a Bucs squad that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (12.3) to kickers this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Only three defenses scored fewer fantasy points than did the Bengals last season, and other than adding DT Dexter Lawrence, the team did little to upgrade the unit during the offseason. That said, few teams have as favorable a D/ST schedule than do the Bengals, so with some early promise, they could be a streaming option for matchups against the Dolphins (Week 5), Titans (8), Saints (12), Browns (13 and 18) and Panthers (15).

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Rodriguez had just six carries to Bhayshul Tuten's 15 in Jacksonville's season opener. Considering Rodriguez contributes almost nothing as a pass-catcher, with just six receptions in 36 career games, he'll be nothing more than a touchdown-dependent deep-league dart throw for fantasy purposes as long as Tuten is healthy. Rodriguez is unlikely to find the end zone in Week 2 against a Broncos defense that allowed the second-fewest rushing yards and fourth-fewest rushing TDs (eight) to RBs last season, though Denver gave up two total TDs to Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Rodriguez has notched just six rushing attempts in each of his first two games with the Jaguars. He's averaging a paltry 3.0 yards per carry and has yet to earn a target in the passing game, where Rodriguez has been a non-factor his entire NFL career. Bhayshul Tuten has 28 carries this season and is the clear lead back for the Jaguars. Rodriguez isn't an advisable fantasy play in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that's allowing a minuscule 8.0 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Rodriguez has recorded between six and eight carries in each of his first three games with the Jaguars heading into a Week 4 road tilt at Cincinnati. He scored his first TD of the season in the Week 3 rout of the Patriots, but Rodriguez will remain a touchdown-dependent deep-league option as long as Bhayshul Tuten is available. The Bengals have allowed the most receiving yards in the league to RBs, but Rodriguez almost certainly won't capitalize on that weakness, as he has yet to earn a target this year and has just six career catches in 38 games.

player.seasonOutlook: Rodriguez, a 2023 sixth-round NFL draft pick, spent his first three seasons with Washington and has primarily played a depth role, but he did hit career-high marks in touches (115), yardage (530) and touchdowns (six) in 2025. Rodriguez has handled more than 10 touches in nine career games and averaged 13.1 touches, 65.9 yards and 11.7 fantasy points with a total of seven touchdowns in those outings. Though he's an effective rusher, Rodriguez is not an option in the passing game (seven career targets). The 26-year-old's contract included a healthy $6.2 million in guarantees, so he's likely to have a legitimate offensive role as a counterpart to second-year backs Bhayshul Tuten and LeQuint Allen Jr. Rodriguez might score the occasional touchdown, but his role won't allow consistent fantasy output. He's best stashed on benches.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kirk Cousins had a bumpy Raiders debut in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, completing 21 of 30 passes for 160 yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions. The veteran quarterback is just keeping the starting job warm for 2026 first overall pick Fernando Mendoza, but the team is in no hurry to get the rookie in the lineup before he's ready, and wins will only give Cousins more job security. His passing numbers could improve once star tight end Brock Bowers is cleared to play, as his most productive connection was running back Ashton Jeanty, who was on the other end of two of Cousins' TD passes. Cousins will face a Chargers defense in Week 2 that had trouble slowing down Jacoby Brissett in its opener but finished fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kirk Cousins has had an impressive start to the season, throwing three touchdowns in back-to-back games for a Raiders team that's a surprising 2-0. The veteran quarterback hasn't played completely mistake-free football under Klint Kubiak, throwing three interceptions, but he's only been sacked twice and has completed 67.8 percent of his passes. As long as Cousins remains productive and the team is winning, there will be little incentive for Las Vegas to hand the reins to rookie Fernando Mendoza, but that switch still figures to be coming at some point in 2026. Cousins will face a Saints defense in Week 3 that has done a good job holding Jared Goff and Lamar Jackson in check through its first two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kirk Cousins is having a late-season renaissance with the Raiders. The 38-year-old quarterback has thrown exactly three touchdown passes in each of the first three games of the season, leading his new team to a 3-0 record and keeping first overall pick Fernando Mendoza firmly on the bench. Cousins has also thrown three INTs, and those mistakes could catch up against tougher competition, as two of those victories have come against the NFL's five remaining winless squads. On the other hand, that production came despite Brock Bowers missing the first two weeks, and the star tight end erupted for a 10-116-1 line in his Week 3 debut. Cousins will get his first real test of the year in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Cousins signed with the Raiders and will work as the team's starter to open the 2026 season ahead of No. 1 overall draft selection Fernando Mendoza. Cousins made eight starts for Atlanta last season and was not much of a fantasy option, averaging 12.5 fantasy points per game while reaching 18 points only once. The 38-year-old will be a bridge starter at best until Mendoza is ready and is no longer a threat with his legs (7 yards on 14 carries last season). He won't be a fantasy option, even when on the field. He should only be drafted late in superflex leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kendre Miller could operate as the Saints' No. 2 running back if Alvin Kamara (knee) remains sidelined for the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Miller was surprisingly involved in New Orleans' Week 1 gameplan, tying Travis Etienne for the most carries on the team while finding the end zone. Despite averaging only 3.3 yards per carry, Miller could have a similar role if Kamara remains out for Week 2. It's also a favorable matchup for running backs, as the Ravens defense allowed 5.2 yards per carry and two rushing touchdowns in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kendre Miller is expected to split carries with Alvin Kamara in the Saints' Week 4 matchup  against the Falcons, with Travis Etienne (hamstring) out. Miller tallied 19 yards on six touches during the Week 3 loss, playing behind both Alvin Kamara and Etienne. As Etienne deals with an ongoing hamstring injury, Miller is likely to split work on the ground with Kamara in the Week 4 contest, operating as one of the Saints' leading rushers. Despite this, Miller is in for a tough matchup against a Falcons defense that's allowed just 3.1 yards per carry this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brenton Strange was one of four Jaguars to catch a touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence in the season-opening win over the Browns, and the starting tight end should remain involved in the Week 2 game plan against the Broncos. The Broncos excelled at defending wide receivers last season but gave up the ninth-most receiving yards to TEs. Strange is a decent fantasy option in multi-TE formats or those with a tight end premium. However, with many mouths to feed in Jacksonville's passing game, Strange is tough to trust as a starter in standard single-TE leagues. Strange has exceeded 61 receiving yards just once since the start of last season while scoring four TDs in 13 appearances over that span.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brenton Strange was a non-factor during the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver, but that was the case for every member of Jacksonville's passing game except for Parker Washington, who accounted for more than half of Trevor Lawrence's 189 passing yards. It won't be easy for Strange to bounce back in Week 3 against the Patriots, who are allowing just 8.0 points per game and have limited TEs to seven catches for 52 yards this season. There are likely better Week 3 options.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brenton Strange remains a complementary piece in Jacksonville's passing game heading into a Week 4 road game against the Bengals. He's locked in atop the Jaguars' TE depth chart, but Strange has just seven catches for 72 yards and a TD on 10 targets in three games-numbers elite options at his position often reach in one game. The Bengals have allowed 23 catches (third-most) and 299 yards (second-most) to TEs, so Strange has more fantasy appeal than usual in Week 4 and is a viable option in multi-TE or TE-premium formats. Even the favorable matchup isn't enough to propel him into the starting range in most one-TE leagues.

player.seasonOutlook: Strange played well in his first season as Jacksonville's clear No. 1 tight end, but it simply didn't lead to much fantasy success. The 2023 second-round pick handled a solid 16% target share during the 12 games he was healthy, but that was only enough to lead to 9.8 fantasy PPG (18th among tight ends). Strange simply hasn't been utilized much near the goal line, as he's yet to clear three touchdowns or four end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old is a reliable target for QB Trevor Lawrence, but with the team so well-stocked at wide receiver, consistent fantasy production is a long shot. Consider Strange a low-ceiling TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Holani looks set as Seattle's No. 2 RB heading into a Week 2 matchup versus the Cardinals. Holani somewhat surprisingly logged eight carries in a tight Week 1 win over the Patriots, recording only two fewer totes than rookie Jadarian Price. However, Price was much more efficient with 5.2 YPC to Holani's 3.6. Price could get a larger share of the workload against the Cardinals, who limited the Chargers to 81 rushing yards on 21 carries in a season-opening victory.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Holani may be asked to take on a bigger offensive role for Seattle in a Week 3 matchup against the Commanders. Jadarian Price suffered a shoulder injury late in a Week 2 win against Arizona, and if he isn't able to suit up versus Washington, Holani would figure to see more work, though Emanuel Wilson would presumably take over No. 1 RB duties. As it is, Holani has gotten involved on offense in each of Seattle's contests so far, combining to produce 42 yards on 12 carries and two yards on one reception. The Commanders have been decimated through the air this season, but they haven't surrendered a rushing touchdown so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Holani appears to be settled in as Seattle's No. 3 backfield option heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Chargers. Holani logged 10 yards on three carries against Washington in Week 3, but he had by far his best game of the season as a pass catcher, recording five receptions on five targets for 48 yards. Both Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson seem to be firmly ahead of Holani in the competition for carries, so work as a receiver will likely be the key to Holani being able to make an offensive impact. The Chargers haven't been hurt much by RBs as pass catchers, yielding just 4.37 yard per target to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Holani is on the 2026 fantasy radar with Kenneth Walker III no longer on the Seattle roster and Zach Charbonnet (ACL) in doubt for the early portion of the season. Holani will compete with rookie Jadrian Price and Emanuel Wilson for touches while Charbonnet is sidelined. The 2024 UDFA has 25 carries and three targets to his name through two NFL seasons. Price figures to get the first shot at lead back duties and, even if forced into a few starts in Seattle's run-friendly offense, Holani would be working in a committee and no more than a deep league flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen McMillan (knee) will operate as one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options if active for the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. McMillan was unable to suit up in Week 1 due to a nagging knee injury, but he could have a valuable role in Tampa Bay's receiving corps once healthy. Outside of Emeka Egbuka, the Buccaneers' wideouts combined to catch seven of eight targets for 76 yards in Week 1, which suggests McMillan will have a large opportunity to contribute when available. He's in for a great Week 2 matchup as well, with Cleveland's defense allowing three touchdowns to WRs last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen McMillan will look to bounce back from a lackluster 2026 debut in the Buccaneers' Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. McMillan returned from a knee injury in the Week 2 loss against the Browns but played just seven offensive snaps. He'll likely be more involved as the season progresses, but with Tampa Bay's offensive struggles (five turnovers and two total touchdowns through two weeks), he may struggle to find fantasy relevance. Additionally, he's in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that allowed just three points to the Bears in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: McMillan is a fascinating late-round sleeper after he impressed as a rookie before missing all but four games due to injury last season. The 2024 third-round pick was featured during the final five games of his rookie season and exploded for a league-high seven TD catches (at least one in all five outings) and 19.8 fantasy PPG (more than 16.7 points in all five) in that span. He was limited in his return to action late in 2025, but did flash with a 7-114-0 performance on nine targets in Week 17. The 24-year-old has a path to a near-every-down role in 2026 with only Emeka Egbuka and 30-year-old Chris Godwin ahead of him on the depth chart. McMillan is worth the inexpensive flier on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tank Bigsby managed just one carry for the Eagles in Week 1. Bigsby rushed once for three yards in the 24-22 win over the Commanders. Meanwhile, fellow backup Will Shipley garnered three total touches for 12 yards. Both rushers remain firmly behind Saquon Barkley on the depth chart, though could see extra run in Week 2 if the game gets out of hand versus the Titans.  Tennessee allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tank Bigsby had 15 touches and a touchdown in Week 2 versus the Titans after Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger injury. Saquon missed portions of the game due to the ailment, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Bigsby and Will Shipley would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge. The Eagles will face a Bears run defense in Week 3 allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tank Bigsby returned to his backup role last game for the Eagles. With Saquon Barkley recovered from his stinger, Bigsby did not receive a carry in the dismal loss to the Bears. Barring injury, Bigsby will get little run in Week 4 versus the Rams. Los Angeles is allowing 101.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just one rushing score through the first three games of the season.

player.seasonOutlook: Bigsby was acquired by the Eagles early in the 2025 season and progressively worked his way up to primary backup duties, a role he's expected to play again in 2026. Granted, it's a small sample, but Bigsby has been extremely efficient over the last two seasons. Among 48 backs with 200-plus carries during the span, Bigsby ranks first in yards after contact per attempt (2.75) and eighth in yards per carry (4.86). In fact, Bigsby has led qualified RBs in YAC each of the last two seasons. On the other hand, he hasn't been used much as a receiver (20 career targets). With overworked Saquon Barkley entering his age-29 season, Bigsby certainly has some insurance appeal, even if he defers passing-down work to Will Shipley. Bigsby, 25, is worth consideration in the later rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns visit the Buccaneers in Week 2. They'll face the fourth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.1) to WRs. Jeudy brought in two of four targets for 26 yards in Cleveland's season-opening blowout loss, but he didn't see any looks in the second half. He tied rookie Denzel Boston for second in targets and third in receptions, while fellow rookie KC Concepcion led the way with four catches and five targets. As long as the Browns' QB play remains shaky, there's no reason to consider Jeudy in any fantasy formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3, whose defense allowed just 145 yards through the air in Week 2. He failed to corral his lone target during Cleveland's upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2, giving him a 2-26-0 receiving line on five targets through two games. Meanwhile, rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion combined for 123 yards and one TD while catching 11 of 13 targets, and they look to be the leaders in the WR room. It will be difficult to start any of them until the Browns' offense consistently proves it can sustain any fantasy-relevant players.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns play host to their division rival Steelers in Week 4. He did not record a target in Cleveland's 21-18 Week 3 victory after failing to catch his only target in Week 2's win. Jeudy now owns a 2-26-0 receiving line on five targets through three games, and it's clear he's fallen down the offensive pecking order behind rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion and TE Harold Fannin Jr. He should remain on waiver wires against Pittsburgh's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (28.0) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Jeudy's up-and-down career continues, as he has now finished outside the top 50 receivers in fantasy PPG four times in six seasons and inside the top 25 twice in the last four years. Jeudy has handled a target share in the 19-23% range all six seasons, but he hasn't found the end zone very often (17 TDs in 91 games) and has struggled with drops (32). Horrific efficiency (48% catch rate, 5.7 YPT) was a big issue last season and led to a career-low 7.1 fantasy PPG. Life might not be much better in 2026 with Cleveland's quarterback situation still unsolved and a lot more target competition (rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston join Harold Fannin Jr.). On the other hand, Jeudy, 27, is still in his prime and it has only been one season since he ranked sixth in the league with 1,229 receiving yards. He has some bounce-back potential, but Jeudy is safest as a bench player.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mack Hollins will look to capitalize on an elevated role in Week 2 when the Patriots face the Steelers. Hollins caught four of his five targets to open the year, finishing with 51 yards, and could slide into A.J. Brown's (ankle) vacated outside role. Hollins and DeMario Douglas have the trust of Drake Maye, something that can't currently be said for Romeo Doubs, suggesting Hollins will play against a secondary that's without top corner Joey Porter Jr. Hollins' size makes him a capable red zone target, which generates upside.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mack Hollins will seek a bounce back performance in Week 3 when the Patriots face the Jaguars. After a solid four catch, 51-yard opener with A.J. Brown leaving early, Hollins notched only two targets in Week 2. New England's passing game is struggling with Drake Maye completing just 14 passes in Week 2. Until he begins to bounce back, trusting any of his pass catchers appears a risky proposition even against a defense that is allowing a generous 10.3 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mack Hollins will look to lead the Patriots' receiving corps in Week 4 against the Bills. Hollins gathered a season-high nine targets in Week 3, following just seven total in the team's first two games, as the Patriots continue to search for a top option without A.J. Brown (ankle) available. Drake Maye is struggling to move this offense, but Week 4 offers the potential to match the Bills' high-scoring offense. Buffalo is allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers and an enticing 9.2 yards per target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cooper Kupp and the Seahawks travel to Arizona to take on the Cardinals in Week 2. Kupp caught two of three targets for 35 yards in a season-opening win against New England, though he would have had a bigger performance if not for a 24-yard touchdown grab that was nullified by a penalty. Of note, Drew Lock is expected to start behind center for Seattle, as Sam Darnold is dealing with a glute injury and is unlikely to suit up. The Cardinals aren't expected to field a top secondary this year, but they did a good job of holding Justin Herbert and the Chargers' offense in check in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cooper Kupp has so far had a quiet campaign heading into Seattle's Week 3 matchup versus Washington. Kupp has logged just two receptions in each of the Seahawks' first two games, registering 55 yards across the four total catches. He ranks third on the team with five targets, trailing Jaxon Smith-Njigba (22) and Rashid Sheheed (nine). As those numbers suggest, Smith-Njigba is dominating looks again this season, so Kupp and Shaheed may be left to compete for scraps throughout the campaign. With that said, there may be lots of receptions to go around against the Commanders, who have given up 27 catches to wideouts through two weeks -- tied for third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cooper Kupp is coming off his biggest performance of the season as the Seahawks prepare to host the Chargers in Week 4. Kupp logged season-best marks with four catches, five targets and 46 receiving yards against Washington in Week 3, and he got into the end zone for the first time with a seven-yard TD reception. Also of note is that Kupp logged a 67% offensive snap share after being on the field for just 43% of Seattle's offensive snaps the previous week. Kupp will look to build upon the promising effort against the Chargers, who have yielded a 67.3% catch rate to wideouts so far this season, seventh-worst in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Kupp heads into his age-33 season positioned for situational targets in Seattle's run-first offense. The longtime Rams slot man appeared in 16 games for Seattle in 2025 -- his first season with the team -- and was limited to a career-low 16% target share. Kupp was a nonfactor in fantasy, clearing 12.0 fantasy points only once (16.0 in Week 2). The veteran remains a reliable short-range target, but his ceiling is very low with Jaxon Smith-Njigba soaking up a huge share of the targets and the likes of Rashid Shaheed and Tory Horton also in the mix. Kupp is an unexciting late-round pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Mayer led the Raiders in targets with seven in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, although he turned that volume into just six catches for 32 yards. That opportunity came as Brock Bowers was sidelined following minor knee surgery, and while the third-year star isn't expected to be out long, he has yet to be cleared for Week 2. If Mayer does get the start at tight end, he'll be facing a Chargers defense that finished fifth in points allowed to TEs last year, although it couldn't contain Trey McBride to begin the current campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Mayer hasn't made much of an impact as the Raiders' top tight end through the first two weeks of the season, catching nine of 11 targets for 55 yards without scoring a touchdown. That role has come while Brock Bowers was recovering from minor knee surgery at the end of training camp, but with Bowers expected to return in Week 3, Mayer will see even his modest volume collapse. If Bowers' 2026 debut does get delayed further, Mayer will still be facing a Saints defense that has yet to allow a TD to a tight end so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Mayer's stint as the Raiders' starting TE ended in Week 3 with the return of Brock Bowers, but he stayed involved in a win over the Saints, catching all three of his targets for 32 yards and his first touchdown of the season. A lack of options at wide receiver could mean Klint Kubiak will continue to lean on both his tight ends for offense, keeping Mayer relevant even with Bowers as the clear No. 1 target for Kirk Cousins. Mayer could make a splash again in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that's been the stingiest in the league against WRs so far, but which ranks just 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mayer enters his first contract year expected to resume his role as Las Vegas' oft-utilized No. 2 TE behind Brock Bowers. The 2023 second-round pick has yet to come close to playing a full season, nor has he emerged as a reliable fantasy option. Last season, he averaged 2.9 targets and 3.4 fantasy points in nine games with Bowers, compared to 6.0 targets and 10.9 PPG in the four games in which Bowers was sidelined. A short-range target (career 5.5 aDOT) with minimal goal line work (one career end zone target), Mayer is way off the fantasy radar. He should be added to rosters only if Bowers misses time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Justice Hill and the Ravens are at home to battle the Saints in Week 2. Hill rushed six times for 18 yards and had one catch for 10 yards in Baltimore's 41-23 win. He's established himself as the clear No. 2 RB, as his 31 offensive snaps trailed slightly behind Derrick Henry's 37. Hill should continue to see opportunities as a change-of-pace back against a New Orleans defense that ranks 28th in fantasy points allowed per game (38.4) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justice Hill and the Ravens travel to face a Cowboys defense in Week 3 that ranks 25th in fantasy points per game (25.9) allowed to running backs. He tallied two carries for six yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards during Baltimore's 24-17 Week 2 loss to the Saints. As long as Derrick Henry, who accounted for 16 of 18 carries out of the backfield, is healthy, Hill's action will be limited as the No. 2 RB. However, in a contest that is expected to be high-scoring, Hill could contribute as a receiver, but he's still a risky fantasy play outside of deeper leagues.
outlooksByWeek.4: Justice Hill and the Ravens are back home to host the 0-3 Titans in Week 4. He was explosive with his five carries during Baltimore's thrilling Week 3 victory, racking up 33 yards and a 6.6 average. However, Derrick Henry handled 26 of the 31 total carries for running backs, and he remains in firm control of the Ravens' backfield. Tennessee's defense ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to RBs, and despite the possibility of Baltimore playing from ahead, Hill's involvement will continue to be limited.

player.seasonOutlook: Hill heads into his seventh NFL season positioned for a larger role following the offseason departure of Keaton Mitchell. Derrick Henry remains the team's lead rusher, but he plays only about half of the snaps, leaving plenty of opportunity for Hill, particularly in passing situations. We've seen Hill in that role recently, including a 2024 campaign in which he posted a 42-383-3 receiving line on 55 targets (11th most among backs). Of course, Hill isn't trusted with much rushing work (his career high in carries is 84), which is why he has never had a top-35 fantasy campaign in his career. The 28-year-old has a limited ceiling and would be on the flex radar in PPR formats only if Henry were to miss time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Calvin Ridley wasn't targeted in Tennessee's season opener and is off the fantasy radar completely heading into a Week 2 home game against the elite Eagles secondary. The veteran WR may be as low as fifth in the Titans' WR pecking order behind Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson, Elic Ayomanor, and Chimere Dike. Second-year QB Cam Ward has struggled to keep any of his pass catchers consistently fantasy-relevant, let alone depth options.
outlooksByWeek.3: Calvin Ridley has drawn just two targets through two games in Tennessee's underwhelming passing game. The Titans don't have a player with more than 80 receiving yards heading into a Week 3 road game against the Giants, so Ridley's fantasy value is slim to none as a depth piece behind Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson. The Giants have struggled to defend WRs, but Ridley is unlikely to get enough passes thrown his way to capitalize on facing the banged-up Giants secondary.
outlooksByWeek.4: Calvin Ridley has just two catches through three games heading into the Titans' Week 4 trip to Baltimore. The Ravens have allowed the second-most catches to WRs this season, but Ridley remains a fantasy non-factor as a depth piece in a Titans offense that has generated the third-fewest passing yards in the NFL. Ridley is firmly behind Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson on the depth chart, and the 31-year-old WR has also been outplayed by Elic Ayomanor.

player.seasonOutlook: Ridley's second season in Tennessee did not go as planned, as the veteran receiver missed 10 full games and was limited to a career-low 17 receptions. He remained a featured target when healthy (seven-plus targets in his four full games), but that led to only one double-digit fantasy performance.
