outlooksByWeek.4: Evan Engram failed to catch a pass in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, as he remains stuck in a peripheral role in the passing game. The veteran TE has notched just eight targets through three games, catching five for 60 yards and a touchdown. His workload is unlikely to significantly increase if Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton are dominating looks from Bo Nix. Engram will face a 49ers defense in Week 4 that has yet to allow a TD to a tight end this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Engram returns for his second season in Denver after an underwhelming debut campaign with the team. The veteran tight end was limited to a career-low 13% target share and finished 15th or lower among tight ends in routes, targets, catches and yardage, despite appearing in 16 games. Engram worked as a short-area target but still struggled to a poor 68% catch rate and was, as usual, a nonfactor near the goal line (one TD, two end zone targets). Engram hasn't cleared four touchdowns in a season since he scored six as a rookie in 2017. He finished 32nd among tight ends in fantasy PPG and isn't a good bet for a larger role this season, especially with Jaylen Waddle added to the offense. The 32-year-old Engram is a fantasy TE3, at best.

outlooksByWeek.2: Gunnar Helm finished third on the Titans with 28 receiving yards on six targets in the season-opening loss to the Jets. He's locked in as Tennessee's top TE heading into Week 2 against the Eagles, but Helm isn't a recommended fantasy option outside of super-deep fantasy formats given the struggles of the Titans' entire offense. Helm has recorded at least four catches in five of his last eight games, but the 2025 fourth-round pick has just two games with more than 36 receiving yards in his career and two TDs in 17 NFL appearances.
outlooksByWeek.3: Gunnar Helm is tied for second on the Titans with seven targets through two games, but he has just 41 receiving yards. The 2025 fourth-round pick is locked in as the team's starting TE heading into a Week 3 road game against the Giants, who just allowed six catches for 54 yards and a TD to Rams TE Terrance Ferguson. Helm is unlikely to match that production considering he has yet to exceed 51 receiving yards in a game while scoring just twice through 18 NFL appearances. Unless second-year Titans QB Cam Ward starts to pick up his passing production, Helm can continue to be ignored in the vast majority of fantasy formats.
outlooksByWeek.4: Gunnar Helm is third on the Titans through three weeks with eight catches and 11 targets, but the 2025 fourth-round pick has mustered a meager 55 receiving yards. His fantasy appeal is minimal for Week 4 against the Ravens, even though Baltimore's defense has allowed a TD to a TE in two of three games this season. Helm has reached 40 receiving yards in just two of 19 NFL appearances.

player.seasonOutlook: Helm quietly caught 44 passes during his rookie season, which -- believe it or not -- ranks 11th among rookie tight ends over the past decade. Impressively, the 2025 fourth-round pick hit that mark despite playing second fiddle to starter Chig Okonkwo. Helm, who caught a healthy 79% of his 56 targets, wasn't much of a fantasy option as a rookie (5.7 PPG), but with Okonkwo out of the picture, he's positioned for a much larger role in his second season. Helm will need a leap from QB Cam Ward, but if that happens, a breakout season is possible. The 24-year-old is worth a late flier in deeper leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Germie Bernard and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 battle with the Patriots. The rookie should remain on waiver wires after playing just three of Pittsburgh's 67 offensive snaps in their season-opening win. Bernard is below DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman, Jaylen Warren, Rico Dowdle, and Pat Freiermuth on the food chain, and it would take an absence or two from his teammates for him to see an uptick in playing time.
outlooksByWeek.3: Germie Bernard and the Steelers host the Bengals for a Week 3 divisional showdown. With Michael Pittman (foot) on the sidelines last Sunday, the rookie stepped into the No. 3 receiver role behind DK Metcalf and Roman Wilson. Bernard caught four of eight targets for 35 yards in the 20-3 loss, seemingly earning the trust of Aaron Rodgers rather quickly. He led the team in yardage, was second in targets, and tied for second in receptions. Bernard faces Cincinnati's 9th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (25.0) to WRs and should be considered a roster stash until we see this type of performance consistently.
outlooksByWeek.4: Germie Bernard and the Steelers travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He caught his only target for 14 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 victory in Week 3. One week after leading the team in yardage while finishing second in targets, Bernard fell victim to a Steelers offense that prefers to spread the ball around, as Aaron Rodgers completed passes to nine different receivers in the win. Cleveland's defense is susceptible through the air, as they're tied for 29th in receiving TDs allowed (5) through three games, but Bernard is off the fantasy radar for now.

player.seasonOutlook: Bernard was selected by the Steelers in the second round of April's draft. Bernard is a solid, reliable receiver with good size who can align all over the formation (55% slot in 53 collegiate games). Despite playing at three schools in four years, Bernard's production increased each season, including a strong 64-862-7 receiving line (plus 18-101-2 rushing) in 2025. He dropped only four of 240 career targets. Bernard is likely to open his career third or fourth in line at receiver behind Michael Pittman Jr., DK Metcalf and perhaps Roman Wilson. That will create a tough path to consistent rookie-season usage and production, so he's only worth draft consideration in the later rounds.

Conner is entering his 10th NFL season without a clear path to touches. For starters, we haven't seen him in a while after he suffered a season-ending foot injury in Week 3 last season. Even prior to the injury, Conner was splitting work with Trey Benson, totaling 28 touches in two full games. Conner restructured his contract during the offseason, but his days as Arizona's lead back are over after Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier were added to the roster during the offseason. Conner, who delivered four straight top-15 fantasy (points per game) campaigns prior to 2025, will need to find a new home in order to have any shot at 2026 fantasy relevance. He'll begin the season on IR.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cade Otton will likely operate as one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Otton caught just three of five targets for 26 yards in the Week 1 loss, but he was on the field for 56 of 57 offensive snaps, solidifying his role as Tampa Bay's top tight end. Additionally, Otton received the third-most targets on the Buccaneers, suggesting there's more production on the way. He's in for a favorable Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed 34 total points and 12.2 PPR fantasy points to TEs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cade Otton is expected to remain Tampa Bay's top tight end in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Through two weeks, Otton is tied for the most targets (11) and second-most receptions (eight) on the Buccaneers, which is a good sign for his outlook moving forward. He's currently on pace to finish with career highs in targets (93) and receptions (68), though is role could diminish once Jalen McMillan returns to full speed. Otton is in for a difficult matchup in Week 3, as Minnesota's defense has allowed just 9.9 PPR fantasy points per game to TEs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cade Otton is expected to remain a crucial part of Tampa Bay's offensive game plan in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Otton had his best performance of the season in the Week 3 loss to the Vikings, catching three of six targets for 56 yards. Through three weeks, Otton is the only Buccaneers tight end to record a reception, which is a positive sign for his outlook going forward. Otton could struggle in Week 4 with Baker Mayfield (thumb) set to miss time, but the matchup remains favorable, as Green Bay has allowed 11.5 PPR points per game to tight ends this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Otton re-signed with Tampa Bay after spending his first four NFL seasons with the team. Since entering the league in 2022, Otton ranks first among all tight ends in snaps (3,530) and second in routes (1,838). That simply hasn't translated to much target volume (he is yet to clear 86 in a season) or goal-line work (11 TDs and 19 end zone targets in 63 games). In fact, Otton was the only player with 75-plus targets who didn't score multiple touchdowns last season. The 27-year-old has finished 25th or lower in fantasy PPG in three of four seasons and is a poor bet for his first top-10 finish in 2026. He's well off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Omar Cooper is uncertain to play for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers due to an ankle sprain. In his NFL debut, he caught his only target for 30 yards. The Jets ran a heavy ground game to open the year, and while they will likely need to throw more in Week 2 to keep up, Cooper's role, even if healthy, is uncertain. The passing game should continue to flow heavily through Garrett Wilson, leaving Cooper's fantasy value volatile.

player.seasonOutlook: Cooper was selected by the Jets in the first round of April's draft. The Indiana product is fresh off a breakout 2025 season in which he posted a 69-937-13 receiving line after totaling 46 catches during his first three seasons with the Hoosiers. Primarily a perimeter target in limited action from 2022 to 2024, Cooper aligned in the slot on 80% of his routes last season. He is a short-area target (9.0 aDOT last season), but still posted strong efficiency numbers, including a 2.61 YPRR. He'll begin his career behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell in New York's Geno Smith-led offense and is unlikely to produce consistent flex value as a rookie.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ryan Fitzgerald is in for a favorable Week 2 matchup when the Panthers face the Falcons, who gave up 8.0 kicking points in a Week 1 loss. Fitzgerald made five of his six kicks last week, drilling his only field-goal attempt while going four-for-five on point-after tries. He's expected to continue seeing plenty of scoring opportunities in Week 2, as he averaged 11.0 kicking points per game in two games against Atlanta in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ryan Fitzgerald is expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Panthers' Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Fitzgerald has started the season strong, converting on all three of his field-goal tries and eight of nine point-after attempts. Additionally, he could continue to benefit from the Panthers' offensive success, as the team currently ranks second in points per game (35.5). Fitzgerald is in for a great Week 3 matchup as well, with Cleveland allowing 11.5 kicking points per game through two contests this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ryan Fitzgerald will look to continue building on an impressive performance in the Panthers' Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Fitzgerald was perfect in Carolina's Week 3 loss, converting on all four of his field-goal tries. On the season, he's made all seven field-goal attempts and eight of nine point-after tries. Fitzgerald expected to continue seeing plenty of scoring opportunities in Week 4, as Detroit's defense has allowed 31.7 points per game this season, despite giving up just 5.0 kicking points per game.

outlooksByWeek.2: Pat Bryant was the Broncos' surprise target leader in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, catching four of six targets for 42 yards. Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton were both taken out of the equation by the Chiefs secondary, forcing Bo Nix to look underneath for options like Bryant and tight end Evan Engram. Bryant had a solid finish to his rookie season in 2025, posting a 26-332-1 line on 39 targets over his final eight regular-season games, and his snap count and production suggest he's moved past Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin to take over the No. 3 wideout role for Denver. Bryant will look to stay involved in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Pat Bryant fell back to earth after a promising season opener, failing to catch his only target in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars. Quarterback Bo Nix made it a priority to get Jaylen Waddle going, and there wasn't much volume available for anyone else. Bryant gained 16 rushing yards on his only carry, but the No. 3 role in the Denver passing game doesn't figure to offer consistent production, and Bryant could face a challenge for the job once Marvin Mims overcomes a foot injury. Bryant will face a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, but three of them have gone for touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Pat Bryant scored his first touchdown of the season in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, connecting with Bo Nix for a five-yard strike in the third quarter. It was one of just two catches on the night for the second-year wide receiver. Through three games, he's produced a 6-86-1 line on nine targets while adding a 16-yard gain on one carry. Bryant is well behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton in the pecking order, but he seems to have secured the No. 3 role ahead of Troy Franklin. Bryant will look to build some momentum in Week 4 against a 49ers secondary that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: A 2025 third-round pick, Bryant played a situational role throughout his rookie season and is likely to do the same in 2026 after Denver added Jaylen Waddle as a running mate for Courtland Sutton. Bryant will battle the likes of Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims Jr. and Lil'Jordan Humphrey for No. 3 duties. During his rookie campaign, Bryant barely saw the field early on, but eventually passed Franklin on the depth chart and earned more work down the stretch. That led to more snaps but not much fantasy production, as he failed to clear 13.2 fantasy points in a single game and found the end zone once. The 23-year-old isn't on the fantasy radar right now, but he makes for a fine dynasty stash.

The seeds are here for the Cardinals to have a respectable pass defense -- Budda Baker, Josh Sweat and Will Johnson all return -- but a lot would need to go right for Nick Rallis' defense to become a fantasy force. As is, the Cardinals have one of the league's toughest D/ST schedules, largely due to their playing in last year's winningest division -- their three division rivals combined to go 38-13. But hey, they do have what could be a great fantasy-playoff schedule (NYJ, @NO, LV, from Weeks 15-17), if they show us anything early.

outlooksByWeek.3: Jameis Winston will take the reins of the Giants offense in Week 3 versus the Titans. Jaxson Dart suffered a serious knee injury and may not return this year. Winston's performance in relief of Dart last game left much to be desired, as he completed just 11-of-27 passes for 111 yards and an interception. Against Tennessee, at least Winston will have a week to prepare and face a lower-tier defense. The Titans are giving up 233.5 passing yards per game in 2026, which is 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jameis Winston led the Giants to an ugly victory last game against the Titans. Winston was underwhelming to say the least, though, as he passed for under 120 yards for the second-straight outing. On a positive note, he did not throw an interception, and the Giants won the contest. However, the G-Men just traded for JJ McCarthy from the Vikings, which could put some pressure on Winston to perform. Nevertheless, Winston should remain the starter for now, and the Giants have another very winnable game in Week 4 versus the Cardinals. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Winston is back with the Giants and with Russell Wilson out of the picture, he is expected to serve as the primary backup to Jaxson Dart in 2026. Winston hasn't been a full-time starter since 2019 and was limited to two starts last season. In typical Winston style, results varied, with 11.0 fantasy points against Green Bay in Week 11, followed by a 32.2-point showing against Detroit the very next week. The 32-year-old doesn't do much with his legs, but his boom/bust passing style makes him an occasional streaming option when the matchup is right. That's what he'll be, if called on for a spot start in place of Dart this season.

outlooksByWeek.4: Case Keenum is in line to get the start again as the Bears play the Jets. Keenum amazed in his first start since 2023, completing 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions, while rushing four times for six yards and another score. The veteran quarterback most definitely guaranteed another opportunity if starter Caleb Williams remains out with a hamstring injury, which is currently the likely scenario. Keenum will face a Mean Green defense that gave up 269 passing yards and two touchdowns to Jared Goff in Week 3.

outlooksByWeek.2: DeMario Douglas will seek more production in Week 2 when the Patriots face the Steelers. He logged a reasonable seven targets to open the season but turned that into just 20 yards on five grabs. Douglas has a rapport with QB Drake Maye as a safety valve, and while snaps seem safe with A.J. Brown (ankle) sidelined for the foreseeable future, Douglas topped 40 yards just four times last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: DeMario Douglas' role in New England's struggling passing offense is questionable ahead of a Week 3 game at Jacksonville. In Week 2, Douglas logged just two targets in his first full game without A.J. Brown after a seven-target opener, and he's averaging just 4.8 yards per reception to start the season. Jacksonville is allowing a hefty 10.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts, but Douglas' inability to stretch the field would require uncharacteristic heavy volume to provide a modest fantasy return.
outlooksByWeek.4: DeMario Douglas hasn't been consistently targeted in the Patriots struggling passing attack ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Douglas has just one catch in each of his last two games, and while last week's popped for 38 yards, he's averaging just 9.4 yards on his seven snags to date. Buffalo's defense has been friendly to opposing wideouts, allowing 9.3 ypt with six receivers going for 40+ yards, but with limited volume, Douglas doesn't seem destined to exploit that.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Higbee remains in a crowded Rams tight-end corps heading into a Week 2 matchup versus the Giants. Though Higbee led Los Angeles TEs with two catches in a Week 1 loss to San Francisco, he logged only 12 offensive snaps -- fourth-most among the group. The Rams frequently use three-TE sets, so Higbee figures to be involved in some capacity each week, but he could have a hard time carving out consistent production if he remains at the bottom of the pecking order in terms of playing time. The Giants held a trio of Cowboys tight ends to five catches for 32 yards in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Higbee may be in line for an upgraded role for the Rams in Week 4 versus Philadelphia. After falling below a 30% offensive snap share each of the first two weeks and producing just two catches for 12 yards, Higbee exploded for an 8-62-1 receiving line on 11 targets and a 71% percent offensive snap share in Week 3 against Denver. That was partly due to fellow tight ends Terrance Ferguson (ankle) and Colby Parkinson (shoulder) getting hurt, and at least Ferguson (and possibly Parkinson) is expected to be sidelined for Week 4. However, the Eagles have been stingy versus tight ends so far, yielding only 89 receiving yards and no touchdowns to the position through three weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Higbee re-signed with the Rams and will battle for work with the likes of Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen, Terrance Ferguson and rookie Max Klare. The 2016 fourth-round pick has a pair of top-10 fantasy campaigns in his career, but the last one came in 2022 and he's finished 24th or worse in three consecutive seasons. Injuries have been part of the issue (21 missed games over the last two seasons), but so has a lesser role and minimal goal-line work (seven touchdowns and four end zone targets over the last three years). Now 33 years old, Higbee is likely third in line for targets at his position on his own team and, thus, nowhere close to fantasy relevance.

outlooksByWeek.2: David Njoku led the Chargers' tight end group in receiving during a season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching all five of his targets for 58 yards. That far overshadowed Oronde Gadsden's two catches for 32 yards, while Charlie Kolar was predictably limited to blocking duties in new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. Top wideout Ladd McConkey did get knocked out of the game with a rib injury, however, and if he misses additional time, there could be more looks available for Njoku. He gets a potentially tough matchup in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that finished third in PPR points per game allowed to TEs last season.

player.seasonOutlook: Njoku signed with the Chargers after spending his first nine NFL seasons in Cleveland. The 2017 first-round pick was a late bloomer and has struggled with durability (he hasn't played a full season since 2018), but he has been a productive fantasy starter in recent years. Prior to a lost 2025 campaign, Njoku finished in the top eight among tight ends in fantasy PPG three seasons in a row. A force near the goal line, Njoku paced the position in end zone targets in both 2023 and 2024. At 30 years old, Njoku likely still has something left in the tank, but he has a tough path to fantasy relevance in a Los Angeles tight end room that also includes ascending Oronde Gadsden II and Charlie Kolar. Njoku will only be worth an add if he quickly takes control as the team's clear starter at the position.

Higgins is out for the 2026 season after tearing his ACL in mid August. As a rookie, the 2025 second-round pick played 58% of Houston's offensive snaps and handled a 12% target share en route to clearing 500 yards and scoring six touchdowns. Higgins averaged a lowly 7.6 fantasy PPG, but the 6-foot-4 perimeter receiver is a good bet for a larger role opposite Nico Collins once healthy in 2027. Keep him stashed in dynasty.

outlooksByWeek.2: Zachariah Branch is expected to play a depth role in the Falcons' receiving room during the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers, whose defense allowed 9.0 yards per pass attempt in Week 1, which is tied for the fifth-worst mark in the NFL. Despite not receiving a target in his NFL debut, Branch tied Olamide Zaccheaus for the third-most snaps (18) amongst Falcons receivers. Additionally, he could be more involved in the Week 2 gameplan after Atlanta's offensive struggles last week. Even so, Branch is in for a great matchup against a Panthers defense that gave up eight total touchdowns in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Zachariah Branch is expected to play a depth role in Atlanta's WR room in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Branch played just 13 offensive snaps in the Week 2 loss to the Panthers -- which is five less than he logged in Week 1. It appears as if the rookie wideout's primary role is a return man, as he's operated as Atlanta's top punt returner this season. Branch's role could grow as the season progresses, but he's unlikely to find fantasy relevance in Week 3. Additionally, the Packers' defense has given up just 175 passing yards per game this season, making it an unfavorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Zachariah Branch is expected to remain a minimal portion of the Falcons' offensive game plan in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints, Through three weeks, Branch has caught three of four targets while playing 45 offensive snaps. Despite not having much competition in Atlanta's WR room, the rookie wideout likely won't have fantasy value without finding the end zone in Week 4. Additionally, Branch could struggle against a good New Orleans secondary that's allowed just 6.2 yards per pass attempt this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Branch was selected by the Falcons in the third round of April's draft. Branch is a tiny slot receiver who posted an extremely low 5.2 aDOT during 37 collegiate games. That limited his efficiency numbers a bit, though he caught 71% of his targets and was terrific after the catch (7.9 RAC). Branch has the look of a versatile (perhaps gadget) player who will help as a rusher, slot receiver and returner. That role makes him a longshot for consistent fantasy output, but he does have a path to No. 2 receiver duties behind Drake London with the likes of Olamide Zaccheaus and Jahan Dotson his primary competition. Branch should only be drafted in dynasty.

Pearsall (knee) is out for the 2026 season after battling injuries during his first two NFL campaigns. The 2024 first-round pick's rookie season ended on a strong note (18-plus fantasy points in Weeks 17 and 18) and that momentum carried over early in 2025 (14.6 fantasy PPG during Weeks 1-3). Pearsall then suffered a knee injury and went on to average 7.5 PPG in six games the rest of the season. Pearsall holds the unfortunate distinction of having the most targets among all players who failed to score a single TD last season. Pearsall will enter 2027 - his age-27 campaign - eyeing his first fully healthy campaign and will battle for a starting job in San Francisco. He's no longer a must hold in dynasty, but he's a fine enough hold in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyrone Tracy was the third-string running back in the season opener for the Giants while Najee Harris was a healthy scratch in Week 1, though that could change quickly. While Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary look like the 1-2 duo out front, Tracy lost a fumble in the red zone that could have proven costly. Tracy had a rough camp even before the gaffe, so his time on the Giants could be coming to an end. If Tracy does suit up in Week 2, he will act mostly as depth against a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season. The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men.

player.seasonOutlook: Tracy is set to compete with Devin Singletary for opportunities in a Giants backfield led by second-year back Cam Skattebo. Tracy has produced 200-plus touches and 1,000-plus yards in each of his first two NFL seasons, but that doesn't tell the full story. Tracy got there as a fifth-round rookie in 2024 by impressing and taking New York's starting gig by Week 5. Last season, he quickly lost lead-back duties to Skattebo, but played a much larger role once Skattebo went down for the season with an injury (9.0 touches per game during Weeks 1-9, but 18.6 per game from Weeks 10-18). Tracy has no standalone fantasy value, but he's effective as a rusher and receiver. That makes the 26-year-old a solid backup who would be worth adding if Skattebo misses additional time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dominic Zvada connected on all four of his kicks in Week 1 for the Giants. Zvada made all four of his PATs during the 28-20 win for the G-Men over the Dallas Cowboys. He did not attempt a field goal for the game. In Week 2, Zvada and company will face a Rams squad that was surprisingly suspect in its season opener. Los Angeles allowed 27 points to the 49ers in a losing effort last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dominic Zvada accounted for the only points for the Giants last game. Zvada connected on both of his field goals in the 28-6 loss to the Rams. The injury to Jaxson Dart leaves Jameis Winston under center at quarterback, which could be an ugly development in terms of opportunities for points for Zvada. In Week 3, the Giants will face a Titans squad allowing 23.5 points per tilt, which is tied for 16th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dominic Zvada provided all of the offense last game for the New York Giants. Zvada connected on all four of his field goal attempts in the 12-7 triumph over the Titans. Zvada has yet to miss a field goal through three games, and could see additional opportunities in Week 4 versus Arizona. The Cardinals are allowing 27 points per tilt, which is 24th in the NFL.

Zach Ertz made his return to the Eagles last game, but it was not exactly triumphant. Signed during the week due to the injury to Dallas Goedert, Ertz managed just one catch for nine yards in the dismal 27-7 loss to the Bears.  Goedert's status remains very much in question for Week 4 versus the Rams. Johnny Mundt also had a four-yard grab and would also see some run without Goedert. Even Goedert cannot suit up, the Rams have been rather stingy against the pass so far in 2026. Los Angeles is allowing just 171.3 passing yards per contest, which is fourth in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaac TeSlaa remains a touchdown-dependent option as the Lions take on the Bills in Week 2. TeSlaa was unable to convert on his one target in Week 1 against the Saints, which only made season hopes lower for him after a subpar training camp. He also remains the fifth option in the Detroit passing game behind Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Jahmyr Gibbs and Sam LaPorta. Luckily, Buffalo gave up a whopping 40.0 PPR points to Houston wide receivers in Week 1, so this upcoming week could be TeSlaa's chance to return to relevance.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaac TeSlaa will seek to stay involved as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. TeSlaa recorded his first catches of the season against the Bills in Week 2, reeling in two of five targets for 26 yards. While his final stat line was still modest, the second-year receiver's five targets are promising. With that being said, he still hasn't done enough to be considered more than a depth option, especially against a New York defense that's been tougher on wide receivers so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaac TeSlaa will look to replicate a solid performance as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. TeSlaa started the season quietly with just two catches for 26 yards across the first two games, but he reeled in all three targets for 66 yards against the Jets in Week 3. While this output isn't enough to warrant a start and is more translatable to a stash move, TeSlaa could be in store for more looks. The Panthers have also allowed a second-least 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers on the year.

player.seasonOutlook: TeSlaa is a candidate for a Year 2 leap as the favorite for No. 3 WR duties in Detroit behind Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. TeSlaa barely played as a rookie (27 total targets), but he had a very specific role and, believe it or not, tied for 11th in the entire NFL with 11 end zone targets. That helped lead to six touchdowns, four of which came when his snaps increased during Detroit's final six games. The 2025 third-round pick has a big size edge on both St. Brown and Williams, so while consistent targets are a long shot, he's still likely to remain busy near the goal line. TeSlaa won't be more than a boom/bust situational target most weeks, but if one of the starters misses time, he'll be on the flex radar. Consider him with a late pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matt Gay was perfect in his Raiders debut, converting field goals from 30 and 47 yards and all three extra points in a season-opening win over the Dolphins. A rebuilding opponent certainly provided Gay with extra opportunities, but the Las Vegas offense could also be better than expected. New head coach Klint Kubiak and an improved quarterback situation, with Kirk Cousins steadying the ship until rookie Fernando Mendoza is ready, should help. The pending return of Brock Bowers will also help generate more scoring drives. Gay may not be able to squander any chances in Week 2 against a Chargers team that ranked ninth in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matt Gay has been busy to begin his Raiders' career, converting all three of his field-goal attempts and all six of his extra points through the first two games of the season. The outlook for the offense should improve once Brock Bowers is cleared for his 2026 debut, and while there's additional uncertainly on the horizon once first overall pick Fernando Mendoza is deemed ready to replace Kirk Cousins under center, Gay could actually benefit if the young QB struggles to get the ball into the end zone while he figures out NFL defenses. Gay will face a Saints team in Week 3 that's allowed an exact mirror to his production so far, with opposition kickers getting three FGs and six PATs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matt Gay has been both busy and perfect for the surprising 3-0 Raiders, connecting on all six of his field goal attempts and all eight of his PATs. The veteran kicker was also successful on his only attempt from 50-plus yards, as he looks to boot at least three long-range FGs for a sixth straight season. Gay has also benefited from a favorable early schedule, as all three of Las Vegas' games so far have been played indoors. The team will get a fourth straight game under a roof in a Week 4 home tilt against Kansas City, but Gay likely won't be able to afford to squander any opportunities versus an opponent that has given up just 16.7 points per game, tied for third in the league.

outlooksByWeek.3: Brycen Tremayne is expected to play a reserve role in the Panthers' receiving corps in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Tremayne was thought to have a larger role in the Panthers' offensive game plan heading into Week 2, as the team cut ties with Jimmy Horn. However, Tremayne played just nine offensive snaps and didn't receive a target, as his role remains primarily on special teams. The third-year wideout is in for a favorable matchup, however, with the Browns' defense allowing four touchdowns to WRs through two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brycen Tremayne is expected to remain a depth option in Carolina's receiving corps ahead of the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Tremayne had the most productive game of his career in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, catching four of six targets for 83 yards while Jalen Coker (quadriceps) and Xavier Legette (knee) were sidelined. Tremayne could remain a larger part of the Panthers' offensive game plan if Coker or Legette were to remain sidelined for the Week 4 contest. Regardless, he's in for a tremendous matchup against a Lions secondary that's given up 568 receiving yards to wideouts through three games this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Andy Borregales hopes his scoring chances will elevate with a bounce-back offensive performance from the Patriots in Week 2 against the Steelers. Borregales had only two opportunities as the team struggled to move the ball in Seattle, and unfortunately, Week 2's game doesn't profile as high-scoring. Perhaps that increases Borregales' three-point opportunities, and he's a reliable option from all over the field. Pittsburgh allowed four field-goal attempts last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Andy Borregales' opportunities could again be limited when the Patriots face the Jaguars in Week 3. Borregales missed his first kick of the season in Week 2, and through two games, has just four field-goal attempts and three extra points as New England's offense has struggled to sustain drives. Jacksonville has allowed just three field goals and three extra points through two games, so there are likely more reliable Week 3 options.
outlooksByWeek.4: Andy Borregales is one of many Patriots hindered by the team's struggling offense heading into a Week 4 matchup with the Bills. New England has scored just 39 points in three weeks, marginally suppressed by two missed field goals, though Borregales' opportunities have been sparse. Buffalo has allowed nine extra points and six field goal attempts through three weeks, so Borregales could be busier in Week 4. Even so, there are safer options until the Patriots offense gets in gear.

player.seasonOutlook: Heidenreich was selected by the Steelers in the seventh round of April's draft. Heidenreich is an intriguing prospect, as he's a tweener who could play running back or receiver in the pros. The Navy product never cleared 77 carries in a single season, but did post a 51-941-6 receiving line in 2025. For his career, he averaged 6.85 yards per carry and evaded one tackle for every 5.9 touches, both of which are best in this RB rookie class. He'll likely max out as a gadget player behind Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle.

The Titans finished 25th in fantasy scoring from the D/ST last season, and other than draftees Dl Keldrick Faulk and LB Anthony Hill, didn't do much to substantially upgrade during the offseason. This looks like a one-and-done streamer, as the Titans face the Jets at home, a plus matchup, but are then a no-go in fantasy for the month that follows (PHI, @NYG, @BAL, HOU, @IND).

outlooksByWeek.2: Joshua Palmer's role within the Bills' offense is minimal at best entering a Week 2 matchup against the Lions. Palmer's snap share was 29% to open the season, and while his lone catch went for a big 34-yard gain, he drew just two targets. The passing game appears to flow through newly acquired DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir, and tight end Dalton Kincaid, keeping Palmer on the fringe for production despite a terrific matchup against a secondary that allowed 410 yards in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Joshua Palmer will look to make another chunk play for the Bills in Week 3 against the Chargers. Palmer has just two catches on the year, but they've gone for 34- and 43-yard touchdowns. The Chargers are allowing 10.8 yards per target to wideouts, the third highest through two weeks, so while volume isn't likely, Palmer could still contribute.
outlooksByWeek.4: Joshua Palmer remains a low-volume option in the Bills' run-first offense ahead of Week 4's matchup with the Patriots. Palmer failed to record a target in Week 3 and has only two on the season. He's been a deep-ball specialist on those rare looks, but facing a New England secondary that is allowing just 6.6 yards per target, Palmer isn't likely to break off a big play in Week 4.

Ty Johnson looks to remain a passing-down option in Week 4 when the Bills face the Patriots. In Week 3's season debut, Johnson caught all four targets for 50 yards against the Chargers-heavy volume for playing just 15 snaps. In 28 snaps last season against New England, Johnson failed to record a reception. The Patriots have allowed eight catches to opposing running backs, rendering Johnson an unappealing, low-ceiling, low-floor option.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson has settled in as a productive change-of-pace and receiving option in the Buffalo backfield behind James Cook. Johnson enters his eighth NFL season having yet to clear 63 carries or 34 catches in a season, but his role allows for him to hit for the occasional big game (15-plus fantasy points four times over the last two seasons). Of course, those games have come at random, making Johnson an unusable fantasy commodity. Even if Cook misses time this season, it's likely that Johnson would remain in his role, with Ray Davis instead stepping into lead back duties. Johnson plays a valuable role for Buffalo, but he's not a fantasy option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Greg Dulcich will look for increased target share in Week 2 when the Dolphins face the 49ers. Entering the season opener, Miami had minimal proven pass catchers, creating optimism around Dulcich, but despite a 74% snap rate, Dulcich was targeted just twice. San Francisco allowed just four catches and 31 yards to tight ends in their opener, so even if Miami is forced to throw from behind, it doesn't yet appear Dulcich has Malik Willis' eye, suggesting there are better fantasy options.
outlooksByWeek.3: Greg Dulcich's opportunities have been limited in Miami's passing game heading into a Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. Dulcich has four total catches on five targets to open the year, tallying 35 yards. Kansas City has allowed volume to the position through two weeks, surrendering 12 catches and two touchdowns, but just 74 total yards and 4.6 yards per target. Better fantasy options are available.
outlooksByWeek.4: Greg Dulcich will look to build on Week 3's momentum in Week 4 when the Dolphins face the Vikings. After just five targets in his first two weeks, Dulcich recorded seven in Week 3, logging five receptions for 55 yards. Miami's receiving room is thin, and Malik Willis will be under constant pressure from Brian Flores' heavy-blitz scheme, allowing Dulcich to work underneath. Minnesota hasn't allowed a tight end to score, but three opposing tight ends have recorded at least 50 yards, giving Dulcich moderate Week 4 potential.

player.seasonOutlook: Dulcich is back on the fantasy radar as the top tight end on the Miami depth chart. The 2022 third-round pick for the Denver Broncos made some noise as a rookie with a 33-411-2 receiving line in 10 games, but he went on to total 16 targets during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before landing in Miami last season. Dulcich didn't see his first target until Week 9 but went on to post a 26-335-1 receiving line the rest of the way. He wasn't a regular fantasy option (one top-15 week among TEs), but he certainly has a path to a substantial target share in 2026 with minimal competition at tight end and with Miami so short-handed at wide receiver. The 26-year-old is a long shot for consistent fantasy value in an offense expected to struggle, but there's some deep-league sleeper appeal.

outlooksByWeek.4: Jalon Daniels is set to start in place of the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb) in Tampa Bay's Week 4 matchup against the Packers. In three preseason games, the undrafted rookie from Kansas accounted for 276 total yards and two touchdowns while turning the ball over just once. In college, Daniels showed incredible arm talent and scrambling ability, though he struggled with accuracy at times. He's in for a tough matchup in his first NFL start, as the Packers' defense has allowed just 18.3 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.

outlooksByWeek.3: Noah Fant is expected to play a depth role in the Saints' tight end corps during the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Fant had a surprisingly productive Week 1 outing, catching four of eight targets for 33 yards and a touchdown. However, he didn't see a target in Week 2 while playing on 45 percent of the team's offensive snaps, suggesting he remains firmly behind Juwan Johnson. Additionally, Fant is in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Raiders defense that's given up just eight receptions to TEs through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Noah Fant is expected to operate as one of the Saints' top red-zone options in the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Despite playing behind Juwan Johnson, Fant has produced in two of three contests this season, catching eight of 12 targets for 66 yards and three touchdowns. He definitely benefits from the Saints averaging 44 pass attempts per game but could struggle remaining fantasy relevant if the touchdowns dry up. However, Fant is in for a very favorable Week 4 matchup against a Falcons defense that's given up three touchdowns to tight ends this season.

player.seasonOutlook: So much is stacked against the Colts' defense at the onset of 2026. They were the second-worst scorer over the second half of 2025, in large part due to injuries to key performers, they lost CB Kenny Moore and LB Zaire Franklin during the offseason, and they have one of the most brutal opening schedules of any team (BAL, @KC, HOU the first three weeks). This is more of a wait-and-see D/ST than one to target on draft day.

McCarthy's career is off to a slow start after the 2024 first-round pick missed his entire rookie season because of an injury then struggled through 2025. McCarthy appeared in 10 games and totaled 11 passing TDs and 12 interceptions while completing an ugly 58% of his passes. McCarthy added some value with his legs (including four TDs), but his production was extremely inconsistent (18-plus fantasy points in four games, but 6.7 per game in his other six outings). The 23-year-old still has plenty of time to develop, but that will come as a backup to Kyler Murray this season. McCarthy is worth considering only in dynasty leagues.

Jeff Ulbrich's blitz-happy defense fueled 57 sacks, the league's second-best total, and a 13th best ranking in fantasy points. That approach could make this a streaming-worthy unit against weaker opposing quarterbacks, which could be the case with the Panthers (Weeks 2 and 18), Saints (4 and 17) and Browns (13). For those in deeper leagues, this could be an advantageous matchups-driven September D/ST if you wait until the end of the draft to fill the position.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kavontae Turpin managed just one catch for eight yards in the Week 1 loss for Dallas to the Giants. Turpin remains mostly utilized as a kick returner at this stage, though the Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no receiver with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: KaVontae Turpin did not even garner a target last game for Dallas. Turpin continues to be utilized largely in the return game. Meanwhile Ryan Flournoy is the clearcut No. 3 wideout behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: KaVontae Turpin continues to flash his versatility for the Cowboys. In addition to his standard role as the primary returner for Dallas, Turpin also rushed for a nine-yard touchdown and even caught a nine-yard pass. Despite this, Turpin remains a boom-or-bust candidate in an offense with so much firepower ahead of him on the depth chart. In Week 4, the Cowboys face a Texans defense allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt through the air, which is 25th in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Odell Beckham earned a spot on the roster for the Giants, completing a remarkable comeback from injury. Though the nostalgia was high, Beckham did not even record a target in the season-opening win over the Cowboys in Week 1. With Malik Nabers now healthy, new additions Darnell Mooney and Malachi Fields ahead of him on the depth chart, and Isaiah Likely looking like a blossoming star at tight end, it will be difficult for Beckham to have much of an impact on the stat sheet this season. In Week 2, Odell and company will face a Rams defense that was surprisingly poor in its first game. Los Angeles gave up 205 passing yards and three touchdowns in a dismal loss in Australia to the 49ers, and also lost star pass rusher Myles Garrett to knee surgery.
outlooksByWeek.3: Odell Beckham has yet to catch a pass through two games for the Giants. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Beckham will likely see his stock further take a hit. In Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league, though Beckham looks more like depth than anything else at this point.
outlooksByWeek.4: Odell Beckham and Braxton Berrios have been vying for the No. 4 wideout role on the Giants, though neither has a catch to date on the young season. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which has limited the opportunities for both players. Winston should remain under center in Week 3 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Returning for his third year with the Chargers, Vidal is set to compete with newcomer Keaton Mitchell for change-of-pace touches behind Omarion Hampton. Vidal had some big moments in 2025, clearing 17 fantasy points in four games, but the notable disclaimer here is that Hampton was sidelined for all of those outings. In fact, Vidal scored only 4.1 fantasy PPG in his other nine games. The 2024 sixth-round pick is a fine depth player who showed he can handle big workloads when needed, but he'll be worth rostering only should Hampton miss time and, even then, Mitchell figures to play a role.

outlooksByWeek.2: Carson Wentz could be in line to start again as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Wentz came in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion) against the Packers in Week 1, and he ended up delivering a come-from-behind win. The veteran completed 12 of 19 passes for 133 yards and three touchdowns, and he did not commit a turnover during the matchup. If Murray is unable to clear concussion protocol ahead of Sunday, Wentz will be in position to get his first start since 2025 against a Bears defense that gave up 361 passing yards, three touchdowns and one interception to Bryce Young in their opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Carson Wentz will return to Minnesota's backup role in Week 3 against the Buccaneers. Wentz performed well while leading the Vikings to a 2-0 record, completing 23 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns in that stretch. The veteran quarterback will remain a solid backup behind Kyler Murray, although anything can happen as the season progresses.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Williams' role could be elevated for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers with WR Omar Cooper (ankle) questionable. Williams logged just one Week 1 target despite playing 62% of the snaps in a game where the Jets led early and throughout-a script unlikely to materialize again in Week 2. With potential double-coverage on Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell running vertically, Williams could find ample space underneath without Cooper's presence, making him someone to consider in very deep formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaiah Williams will look to build on an expanding role in Week 3 when the Jets face the Lions. Elevated to No. 3 on the depth chart with Omar Cooper landing on IR, Williams recorded six targets last week, catching them all for just 34 yards. The Jets' offense is unlikely to score enough to sustain a third viable receiver, but if there were such a matchup, it would be Week 3 against a secondary that's already allowed 437 yards to wideouts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaiah Williams' role in the Jets' offense remains limited ahead of a Week 4 tilt against the Bears. Despite the absence of Adonai Mitchell in Week 3, Williams logged only two targets in a game where the Jets threw 37 times. While the Bears are allowing 8.5 yards per target to receivers, Williams doesn't seem likely to garner enough looks to exploit a potentially favorable matchup.

player.seasonOutlook: Sanders enters his second NFL season set to back up Deshaun Watson in Cleveland. Sanders made eight appearances during his rookie season and wasn't overly productive, scoring eight all-purpose touchdowns, throwing 10 interceptions and completing 57% of his passes. The fifth-round pick produced one weekly fantasy finish better than 18th, though it was an impressive 364-yard passing game with four total touchdowns (33.5 points). Sanders added some value with his legs, including 20-plus yards in five straight games to end the season. The 24-year-old remains a wild card and is likely to earn some starts this season, so that's enough to make him worthy off a stash in superflex/dynasty leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kendrick Bourne had a promising performance for Arizona in Week 1 and will look to be productive again versus the Seahawks in Week 2. Bourne led Cardinals wideouts with eight catches and 75 yards in a season-opening victory versus the Chargers, with only stud tight end Trey McBride outpacing his eight targets. The veteran Bourne looked to have great rapport with QB Jacoby Brissett, so it will be interesting to see how the target distribution shakes out in Week 2 and beyond. He won't have an easy matchup against Seattle, who limited New England to 178 yards through the air in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kendrick Bourne appears to have earned a key role in Arizona's passing game heading into a Week 3 matchup versus San Francisco. After joining the Cardinals in the offseason, Bourne has recorded 11 targets through two weeks, second-most among Arizona wide receivers. The veteran wideout has logged a 10-86-0 line on those opportunities, as he has established good chemistry with QB Jacoby Brissett. With that said, Week 3 could be another tough test for Arizona's air game: the 49ers have allowed just a 59.3 percent catch rate to WRs so far, ninth-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kendrick Bourne is coming off two quiet weeks heading into Arizona's Week 4 tilt versus the Giants. After posting an 8-75-0 receiving line in the season opener against the Chargers, the veteran wideout has managed a modest four catches on six targets for 33 yards combined over his subsequent two games. Bourne appears to be well behind WR Michael Wilson and TE Trey McBride, and at least marginally behind WR Marvin Harrison, in the passing-game pecking order at the moment. There could be an opportunity to make some noise against a Giants defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league in receiving yards allowed to wideouts so far this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Demarcus Robinson should again have a key role for San Francisco in Week 2 against the Dolphins. After rookie De'Zhaun Stribling hurt his ankle in a season-opening win over the Rams, Robinson stepped up as the team's No. 3 wideout and produced two catches for 50 yards and a touchdown. Stribling is expected to miss at least a month, so Robinson will likely continue to work as the 49ers third wideout behind Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel. Miami presents a good matchup after falling to the Raiders 27-13 and yielding three passing touchdowns Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Demarcus Robinson suffered an ankle injury in San Francisco's win over the Dolphins on Sunday, and his status is very much in doubt for a Week 3 matchup against Arizona. Before getting hurt, Robinson caught all three of his targets for 34 yards against Miami as the 49ers' No. 3 wideout. In the likely scenario that he can't play in Week 3, Jacob Cowing would stand to step into Robinson's place in the pecking order. Arizona has given up four receiving TDs to wide receivers through two weeks, tied for the most in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Darnell Mooney caught both of his passes in Week 1 for the Giants. Mooney had two catches for 27 yards in the shocking 28-20 win over the Cowboys. Mooney had fewer targets than rookie Malachi Fields, an intriguing development. Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely already look like the favorite targets for quarterback Jaxson Dart, though, so it could be slim pickings for Mooney and the rest of the pass-catching corps. In Week 2, the Giants will face a Rams defense that struggled against the pass in its opener, allowing 205 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air.
outlooksByWeek.3: Darnell Mooney led the Giants in receiving last game.  Unfortunately, Mooney managed just 48 yards on two catches in the 28-6 loss to the Rams. The bigger news is that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Mooney will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Darnell Mooney has two catches in each of his first three games with the Giants. Unfortunately, he has yet to find the end zone, and has not amassed more than 50 yards in any single contest. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which limits the upside for Mooney as well. Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Mooney signed with the Giants to help replace Wan'Dale Robinson as the team's No. 2 receiver behind Malik Nabers. Mooney's production has been all over the map throughout his career, having posted strong 81-1,055-4 and 64-992-5 receiving lines over the past five seasons, while also finishing in the 400-to-500-yard range the other three campaigns during the span. The 28-year-old has proven to be a serviceable starting receiver and could easily settle in second or third in line for targets in the Giants' ascending, Jaxson Dart-led offense. Mooney's ceiling isn't very high, so he's barely worth late round consideration in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ted Hurst will look to build on his solid NFL debut in Tampa Bay's Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Hurst played 75 percent of the Buccaneers' offensive snaps and caught all three of his targets for 36 yards, taking advantage of increased opportunities with Jalen McMillan (knee) sidelined. Hurst could continue being a valuable asset to Tampa Bay's offense if McMillan continues to miss time, which he very well could in Week 2. The matchup against the Browns is also great, with that defense allowing a whopping 50.6 PPR fantasy points to wideouts in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ted Hurst is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Despite the return of Jalen McMillan in the Week 2 loss to the Browns, Hurst played a career-high 45 offensive snaps -- 38 more than McMillan. Additionally, Hurst led the team with seven targets, though it led to just two receptions. Regardless, it appears as if Hurst will remain an important piece of the Buccaneers' offense as the season progresses. The rookie wideout will likely struggle but could find success against a Minnesota secondary that's allowed 12.6 yards per completion this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ted Hurst is expected to play a depth role in the Buccaneers' receiving corps during the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Hurst has proved to be a valuable part of Tampa Bay's offense just three games into his rookie campaign, catching six of 14 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown. With Jalen McMillan (knee) going down in the Week 3 loss to the Vikings, Hurst's role could continue to expand as the season progresses. He will likely see fewer opportunities in Week 4 with Baker Mayfield (thumb) sidelined, but the matchup remains favorable, as the Packers' defense allowed 14.2 yards per completion in a Week 3 loss to the Falcons.

player.seasonOutlook: Hurst was selected by the Buccaneers in the third round of April's draft. Granted he played at a small school, but Hurst ranked third in this rookie class target share (26%) and first in air yard share (45%) during his FBS career. A tall, vertical receiver, Hurst posted solid collegiate efficiency despite inconsistent QB play (only 68% of his 235 FBS targets were catchable, which is easily lowest among qualified WRs in this class). His 135-inch broad jump was best among wide receivers at the combine. Hurst will get some run at 'X' receiver as a rookie, but he's a longshot for consistent rookie-season fantasy production with Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin and Jalen McMillan in the fold.

outlooksByWeek.2: Raheim Sanders and the Browns are on the road to square off against the Buccaneers in Week 2. After Dylan Sampson (knee) was ruled out in the first half, Sanders filled in as the No. 2 RB behind Quinshon Judkins. He notched one carry for one yard and caught all three targets for 25 yards while playing 16 snaps on offense. With Cleveland expected to play from behind often, Sanders could have a fairly sizable role in the passing game, no matter who the quarterback is. Tampa Bay allowed eight catches on nine targets for 52 yards to RBs in their Week 1 loss.
outlooksByWeek.3: Raheim Sanders and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3. He tallied two carries for four yards and caught his only target for seven yards during Cleveland's first win of the season in Week 2. Quinshon Judkins handled 12 of 15 carries by running backs, and as long as he remains healthy, the workload split should remain similar. Sanders does have some upside as a receiver out of the backfield, but his role is still too limited to be relied upon in fantasy. Carolina's defense has been susceptible on the ground, allowing 36.3 fantasy points to RBs (31st), but they rank 14th in receiving yards surrendered to the position.
outlooksByWeek.4: Raheim Sanders and the Browns host the rival Steelers for a divisional clash in Week 4. He took his lone carry for 17 yards and caught four of five targets for 34 yards during Cleveland's upset win in Week 3. Sanders was highly efficient with his five touches, finishing second on the team in receptions and third in targets. He should continue operating as the third-down back and in most passing situations, but his overall involvement is difficult to trust while Quinshon Judkins remains healthy. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 20th in fantasy points (22.1) and 25th in receiving yards allowed to RBs.

outlooksByWeek.3: Tyson Bagent is set to get the start for Chicago in Week 3 versus the Eagles. With Caleb Williams currently week-to-week with a hamstring injury and doubtful against Philly, Bagent is primed to get his first start since the 2023 season. The D2 product completed five of nine passes for 54 yards in the fourth quarter against the Vikings this past week after filling in for Williams, but he was unable to deliver a win for the Bears in the end. Bagent's most notable stats trail back to 2023, when he completed 94 of 143 passing attempts for 859 yards with three touchdowns and six interceptions across five games while filling in for Justin Fields. He'll face an Eagles offense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks across two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyson Bagent will likely be Chicago's backup quarterback again in Week 4 against the Jets. Bagent didn't get the start in Week 3 after getting next-to-no practice reps with a concussion, and Case Keenum throwing for 247 yards and two touchdowns should keep it that way. The D2 product will now only face New York's defense if something were to happen to the veteran.

outlooksByWeek.2: Darnell Washington and the Steelers travel for a Week 2 showdown against the Patriots. He caught both of his targets for 18 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 win over the Falcons. Washington and Pat Freiermuth were co-starters at TE, but the latter tallied five catches for 46 yards and a TD. New England's defense is very stingy against the position, as they rank second in fantasy points allowed per game (3.3) to tight ends.

player.seasonOutlook: Though he never quite made it onto the fantasy radar, Washington was one of the most fun, surprising "breakout" players of 2025. Essentially an extension of the offensive line at 6-foot-6, 264 pounds, Washington is known mainly for his blocking. Still, the 2023 third-round pick played well enough that he was stealing snaps and targets from both Jonnu Smith and Pat Freiermuth. Washington never cleared six targets or 10.7 fantasy points in any game, but he was effective with the ball in his hands and averaged 8.5 yards per target. Though Smith has been released, Pittsburgh's offense is no longer being led by TE superfan Arthur Smith, which is likely to lead to a lesser role for Washington. Expect him to operate as a rarely targeted blocking complement to Freiermuth.

Kirk signed with the 49ers after spending his first eight seasons with Arizona, Jacksonville and Houston. The 2018 second-round pick peaked with a 12th-place finish in fantasy points in 2022, but that marks his only career top-25 finish and he's been way off the fantasy radar the last two seasons, partially due to injury woes (13 missed games). Kirk doesn't have a clear path to consistent targets in San Francisco, with Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling also in the mix (not to mention Christian McCaffrey and eventually George Kittle). The 29-year-old will begin the season on IR and is not on the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Xavier Legette is expected to play a depth role in the Panthers' receiving corps in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Legette appears to be an afterthought in Carolina's offensive game plan, as he received just two targets despite the team scoring 37 points in the Week 1 loss. He's clearly behind both Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker (ankle) in the WR room, so it's unlikely Legette will see much volume going forward. Additionally, he's in for a difficult Week 2 matchup, as Atlanta's defense allowed just 8.6 yards per completion in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Xavier Legette is expected to play a depth role in Carolina's receiving corps in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Legette had a solid Week 2 performance after putting up a goose egg in Week 1, catching two of four targets for 64 yards. The third-year pro remains firmly behind Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker in Carolina's receiving corps, as the two have combined for 26 receptions, 380 yards and a touchdown through two weeks. However, Legette could take advantage of a Cleveland secondary that's allowed 10.0 yards per target to opposing WRs heading into Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Xavier Legette (knee) is expected to operate as one of Carolina's top deep threats if active for the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Legette was sidelined for the Week 3 loss to the Browns but showcased some big-play ability the week prior, catching a 55-yard bomb from Bryce Young. Even if Legette suits up for the Week 4 contest, he'll likely play a depth role behind both Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker (quadriceps), if active. Legette could really take advantage of a struggling Lions secondary that's allowed 10.4 yards per completion this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Legette is eyeing a Year 3 leap after a boom/bust start to his NFL career. The 2024 first-round pick flashed with 521 yards and four touchdowns on 55 touches as a rookie, but fell to 363 yards and three scores on 36 touches in 2025. Legette did post a pair of big games (24.2 points in Week 7 and 18.3 points in Week 11), but was otherwise held in check (3.6 PPG in the other 13 games). Legette has struggled with the ball in his hands (woeful 2.1 RAC in his career) and is behind Tetairoa McMillan and likely Jalen Coker on the Carolina WR depth chart. The 25-year-old will see some situational targets and carries, but he'll need a big Year 3 leap to find his way to fantasy relevance. He's no more than a late-round lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drew Lock is expected to serve as Seattle's starting quarterback in Week 2 versus Arizona due to Sam Darnold's glute injury. Lock took over in the first quarter of the Seahawks' season opener and guided the team to a win, completing 16 of 22 passes for 187 yards and one touchdown with no interceptions. Lock's TD was a 45-yard connection with Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who again figures to be his top target against the Cardinals. Arizona is coming off a surprising win against the Chargers, during which they limited Justin Herbert to 209 yards and an interception.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drew Lock could have another opportunity to lead Seattle's offense in Week 3 versus Washington. Lock started for the injured Sam Darnold (glute) on Sunday versus Arizona and threw for 235 yards with three touchdowns. Darnold is reportedly making good progress in his recovery, so it's not yet clear who will helm the team's offense in Week 3. Whichever QB gets the opportunity could be in for a big game against the Commanders, who have allowed a league-high seven passing touchdowns and have no interceptions through two weeks.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyquan Thornton saw only one target in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, failing to bring in a deep ball from Patrick Mahomes, and that sums up his role in the passing game. The former Patriot will hit for big plays on occasion, as 11 of his 19 receptions in 2025 went for 20 yards or more, but he won't see enough volume to be a reliable contributor unless injuries open up more volume for him. Thornton gets a more exploitable matchup in Week 2 against a Colts secondary that ranked 30th in PPR points per game allowed to WRs last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyquan Thornton produced strong numbers in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, hauling in all four of his targets for 86 yards. The fifth-year speedster is at best fifth in the pecking order for looks from Patrick Mahomes, but his role as a deep option gives Thornton some big-play potential in the right matchup, even on limited volume. He'll face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyquan Thornton is settling in as a deep option for Patrick Mahomes. After getting blanked in Kansas City's opener, Thornton has caught six passes over the last two games on seven targets, and two of those receptions have gone for 20 yards or more. He's collected 108 yards in total, and while he's still looking for his first touchdown of 2026, it would take just one defensive breakdown to free him up for a long score. Thornton's low volume will make him a risky option in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs, and has yet to allow a TD to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: James is an intriguing insurance stash as a candidate to work as 30-year-old Christian McCaffrey's backup in San Francisco. The 2025 fifth-round pick didn't record a single touch on three snaps during a rookie campaign spent buried behind McCaffrey and a host of veterans. James wasn't utilized much as a receiver at the collegiate level and underwhelmed at last year's combine, so it's unclear what his upside will be in the pros. However, if the 22-year-old wins the No. 2 gig over rookie Kaelon Black and McCaffrey misses action, he'll be a priority add. Consider him in the final few rounds in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cole Kmet will aim to stay involved as the Bears take on the Vikings in Week 2. Kmet brought in two of three targets for 35 yards and a touchdown against the Panthers in Week 1, and he was the only tight end to record a catch. While the veteran is set to be a secondary option behind Colston Loveland this season, the high-scoring ability of Chicago could allow plenty of targets for the pair. They'll face a Minnesota defense that gave up five catches for 115 yards to Green Bay's tight ends in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cole Kmet remains a depth option as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Even though Kmet played more offensive snaps in Week 2 (69 percent) than in Week 1 (57 percent), he garnered just one target and was unable to catch it. Still, young tight end Colston Loveland has yet to do much this year, which could keep a veteran presence like Kmet relevant. He'll face a Philly defense that's allowed the fewest PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season (5.1).
outlooksByWeek.4: Cole Kmet will remain a depth option as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Kmet started off the season hot with two catches for 35 yards and a touchdown, but he's been unable to catch his sole target in each of the last two games. The veteran tight end is still a big part of Chicago's offense, but it's to be seen if this goes beyond blocking work. He'll face a New York defense that's ceded a top-ten 10.0 fantasy points per game to TEs.

AJ Dillon is expected to operate as the Panthers' No. 2 running back in the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. While backing up Chuba Hubbard in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, Dillon accumulated 14 yards on five total touches. He will likely struggle gaining fantasy relevance without finding the end zone, as Hubbard has a firm grasp on the Panthers' backfield. However, Dillon is in for a relatively favorable matchup against a Detroit defense allowing 4.5 yards per carry to opposing RBs through three weeks.

outlooksByWeek.2: Sione Vaki is poised to serve as Detroit's supplementary running back once again in Week 2 at Buffalo. While the Lions were planning to use a committee approach at RB2 this season, Vaki was the only other player at the position who saw the field behind star Jahmyr Gibbs. The third-year ball carrier recorded two rushes for seven yards and brought in his sole target for 11 yards. This makes it likely he'll be the main option behind Gibbs at least in the short term. Vaki will face a Bills defense that allowed 33.9 PPR fantasy points to RBs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Sione Vaki should remain Detroit's low-usage RB2 in Week 3 against the Jets. Vaki logged one carry for seven yards and caught one pass for 13 yards against the Bills in Week 2, showcasing that the secondary running back for the Lions is a graveyard role this year. The third-year ball carrier is still on pace to log career-high numbers given his small role so far in his career, but he's nothing more than a depth option with Jahmyr Gibbs healthy.
outlooksByWeek.4: Sione Vaki will remain Detroit's secondary running back option in Week 4 at Carolina. Vaki hasn't been able to carve out much of a role behind phenom Jahmyr Gibbs so far this season, but he did register a season-high six carries for 26 yards, along with another catch for 11 yards in Week 3. The third-year running back remains a depth option given the usage of Gibbs so far this season, so it won't matter much that the Panthers defense has allowed the third-most fantasy points per game (30.5) to RBs this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Seth McGowan had the only touch by a Colts RB other than Jonathan Taylor in the season opener. McGowan and fellow backup DJ Giddens are irrelevant for fantasy purposes as long as Taylor is available. Taylor handled 22 touches in Week 1 and is expected to maintain a workhorse role in Week 2 at Kansas City.
outlooksByWeek.3: Seth McGowan is locked in as the little-used backup to workhorse Colts RB Jonathan Taylor, having beaten out DJ Giddens (knee) for the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. McGowan has just two carries and one target through two games. With Taylor healthy for a Week 3 home game against the AFC South rival Texans, McGowan remains a non-factor in fantasy.
outlooksByWeek.4: Seth McGowan has seven career touches heading into the Colts' Week 4 game against the Commanders in London, four of which came in the Week 3 win over Houston. With star RB Jonathan Taylor healthy, McGowan's workload is expected to remain limited in Week 4 against Washington's stout run defense. McGowan's fantasy value is purely as a bench insurance policy in case of a Taylor injury.

player.seasonOutlook: McGowan was selected by the Colts in the seventh round of April's draft. McGowan is an older prospect (25), having bounced around five schools due to an off-field issue in 2021 that led to jail time and a dismissal from Oklahoma. He slowly rebuilt his career and peaked with 1,100 yards and six TDs at New Mexico State in 2024 prior to delivering 851 yards and 12 TDs at Kentucky last season. His efficiency is hit or miss, as his career 2.65 YAC is very poor, but his 4.2 forced missed tackle rate is strong. He's been effective in the passing game, as well, so there's some hope for a pro level impact. McGowan impressed at the combine, posting the top vertical and broad jump in this RB rookie class and running a solid 4.49 40-yard dash at 223 pounds. McGowan will battle DJ Giddens for primary backup duties behind Jonathan Taylor, so it's possible he finds his way to some value as an insurance hold.

outlooksByWeek.3: Konata Mumpfield's role in the Rams' Week 3 matchup against Denver could depend on the status of Puka Nacua (hip). With Nacua sidelined Monday versus Denver, Mumpfield drew the start, but he finished with just one catch on two targets for 12 yards. Meanwhile, Davante Adams posted a massive 10-195-2 line, with no other Los Angeles wideout reeling in more than one catch. The Broncos won't be an easy matchup in Week 3, as they've held opposing WRs to an average of just 13.2 fantasy points per game this season, fourth-fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Konata Mumpfield is coming off the biggest performance of his young career ahead of the Rams' Week 4 matchup in Philadelphia. Mumpfield established new professional high marks with four catches for 93 yards against Denver in Week 3, with one of his receptions going for a 48-yard touchdown. The second-year wideout logged a healthy eight targets in the loss, but important context is that Puka Nacua sat out due to a hip injury. Should Nacua be able to return in Week 4, it's reasonable to expect Mumpfield to see considerably less opportunities. Still, the Eagles have been vulnerable against wideouts and just allowed Chicago's WR duo of Luther Burden and Kalif Raymond to combine for 13 catches, 151 yards and two TDs on Monday Night Football.

player.seasonOutlook: Knox enters his eighth season as a solid role player for the Buffalo offense. He is on the field quite a bit (20th among tight ends in snaps last season), but defers to Dalton Kincaid when it comes to the team's top target priority at the TE position. Even when Kincaid was sidelined last season, Knox was limited to only 3.6 targets and 6.1 fantasy points per game. Knox has never posted a top-10 fantasy campaign and has finished outside the top 30 in PPG each of the last three seasons. Even if Kincaid misses additional time, Knox will max out as a fantasy TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Skyy Moore should be a depth option in Green Bay's passing game at New York in Week 2. Skyy Moore was unable to catch his one target, but he also did play on offense more than was expected. The fifth-year wideout should remain a secondary choice, but he could start to garner more looks given the pass-heavy offense that Green Bay has operated with. He'll face a Jets secondary that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Skyy Moore should remain a secondary option in Green Bay's passing game against the Falcons in Week 3. Moore was utilized more in Week 2 against the Jets after Jayden Reed went down with an injury, garnering three targets and bringing in two of them for six yards. The former Kansas City wideout is the top kick returner for the Packers, but his playmaking abilities make him an interesting target for Jordan Love if he gets more involved in the offense. He'll take on an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Skyy Moore should continue to get opportunities as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Moore recorded three catches for 31 yards on a career-high seven targets in Week 3 against the Falcons. While a pass-heavy game script definitely helped the fifth-year wideout's cause, he has seen more of an offensive role with Jayden Reed sidelined due to a neck injury.
